S.P.O., Headquarters,
August 4, 1937.

Proceedings against 1st Class Seaman Miyasaki
of the Japanese Naval Landing Party

According to information received
from the Japanese Naval Authorities, preliminary
investigations into the desertion of Sadao
Miyasaki, 1st Class Seaman attached to the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, having been
completed, Miyasaki has been handed over to
the Third Fleet where he will stand trial

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, July 26, 1937
8024
27 7 37

Witness Said
Not Japanese

Nippon Navy Combs
City For Missing
Seaman

That the mysterious witness who at 9:20 p.m. Saturday night reported the alleged kidnapping of Sadao Miyazaki, first class seaman, was not a Japanese at all is the theory advanced today by the headquarters of the Japanese Special Navy Landing Party. His "actions and manners" were not that of a Japanese although he spoke the language like a native.

Although three Japanese sailors and three civilians listened to the report of the missing witness, none of them suspected that he was not Japanese until after they had thought the matter over. The sailors were trained for military work, it is explained, and not for sleuthing so that they accepted the man's statement that he had to rush to the bed of his sick mother and could not accompany them to headquarters.

No Record Kept

A regulation requires Japanese sailors going on leave to travel in three's, but so far the companions of the missing seaman have not been located. The belief is that since they violated a regulation by leaving their companion, they are afraid to admit their identity. Although leaving headquarters in three's, no record is kept of which men leave together.

Efforts are still being made to locate the witness and to find the seaman "or his dead body." The Consular Police have issued an order for the witness to report to headquarters. The Japanese Landing Party feels that if he is Japanese there will be no trouble in finding him, but if he is not Japanese each day that passes makes the search for him more difficult.

10,000 Leave Chapei

Only the regular Japanese guard is being maintained in Chapei and the exodus from that area was reported to have stopped completely this morning. Between 7 a.m. and midnight yesterday, however, 10,000 refugees are estimated to have passed through Hongkew, 60 per cent of whom were headed for the French Concession, 20 per cent for Nantao and the remainder for various parts of the Settlement.

Some were just removing valuables and may already have returned to their homes. Shopkeepers moved their stock to a safer place, but kept their shops open.

Car Fleet Rumored

The Russian community today was abuzz with the report that a Russian commission agent in the French Concession had been approached by Japanese businessmen to organize a fleet of cars and trucks for use in case of emergency. It was stated that the agent today was attempting to round up approximately 300 White Russian chauffeurs in Shanghai for this purpose, and to reach an agreement with various garages and companies for an equal number of vehicles.

The plan, it was reported, was to get the 300 drivers lined up ready for any emergency in Hongkew, and access to 200 truck and 100 motorcars immediately when needed. This was to be in the nature of a precaution in case any further trouble should arise in connection with the Hongkew situation.

That 300 Russian drivers for such a purpose would be hard to locate was the opinion expressed by local Russian observers, for this would mean trouble for them with the Chinese authorities, which they can ill-afford being under Chinese law and jurisdiction.

（手写批注：ASL... AK ... 27/7）

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1937年7月26日，星期一
8024
27 7 37

证人称
并非日本人

日本海军在全市
搜寻失踪水兵

日本特别海军陆战队总部今天提出的一种理论认为，周六晚上9点20分报告称一等水兵宫崎（Sadao Miyazaki）涉嫌被绑架的那位神秘证人根本就不是日本人。尽管此人讲日语像本地人一样流利，但他的“举止和态度”并不像日本人。

虽然有三名日本水兵和三名平民听取了这位失踪证人的报告，但在仔细思考此事之前，他们中没有人怀疑他不是日本人。据解释，这些水兵接受的是军事工作训练，而不是侦探训练，因此他们接受了此人的说法，即他必须赶去照顾生病的母亲，无法陪同他们前往总部。

未保留记录

一项规定要求日本水兵在休假外出时必须三人同行，但到目前为止，尚未找到这名失踪水兵的同伴。人们认为，由于他们违反了规定离开了同伴，因此不敢承认自己的身份。虽然是三人一组离开总部，但并没有记录具体是哪几个人一起离开的。

目前仍在努力寻找该证人，并寻找这名水兵“或其尸体”。领事警察已发布命令，要求该证人向总部报到。日本陆战队认为，如果他是日本人，找到他不会有什么困难；但如果他不是日本人，每过一天，寻找他的难度就会增加。

一万人离开闸北

目前闸北仅维持常规的日本警卫部队，据报道，今早该地区的撤离已完全停止。然而，在昨天上午7点至午夜之间，估计有一万名难民穿过虹口，其中60%前往法租界，20%前往南市，其余前往公共租界的各个区域。

有些人只是搬走贵重物品，可能已经返回家中。店主将货物转移到更安全的地方，但保持店铺营业。

传闻组建车队

今天，俄侨社区中流传着一则消息，称法租界的一名俄罗斯佣金代理人受到日本商人的接洽，要求组织一支由汽车和卡车组成的车队，以备紧急情况下使用。据说，该代理人今天正试图在上海召集约300名白俄司机为此目的服务，并与各家车库和公司达成协议，提供同等数量的车辆。

据报道，该计划是让这300名司机在虹口待命，以应对任何紧急情况，并在需要时立即动用200辆卡车和100辆轿车。这是为了以防虹口局势引发进一步麻烦而采取的一种预防措施。

当地俄罗斯观察家表示，很难为这种目的找到300名俄罗斯司机，因为这意味着他们会与中国当局发生麻烦，而在受中国法律和管辖权约束的情况下，他们承受不起这种麻烦。

（手写批注：ASL... AK ... 27/7）

page_data.en:
Diamond (金桐儂) :-

JAPANESE DISCIPLINE : IS IT SO STRONG?

Japanese people always boast of their strict
discipline, especially among their Imperial Army. They
strongly criticize the disorderliness and disorganization
of China.

In recent years, however, the foundation of
discipline in the minds of the Japanese people has been
shaken. Who were they who during the January 28 Incident
begged the Big Sword Corps of the 19th Route Army for mercy?
Who was the man who, among the troops transported to Peiping
from Shanhaikwan, cried bitterly and committed suicide?
Fearing that he would be punished by his superior officers,
S. Miyazaki recently deserted his unit and after discarding
his uniform disappeared in disguise, thereby re-enacting the
incident of the disappearance of Consul Kuramoto. Subsequently
this Miyazaki took a cold bath in the Yangtsze River and would
have drowned had he not been saved by some Chinese.

Such violation of discipline as committed by a
member of the Imperial Army is a matter of regret.
page_data.zh:
Diamond（金桐儂）:-

日本纪律：真的那么严明吗？

日本人总是吹嘘他们严格的纪律，尤其是在其帝国军队中。他们强烈批评中国的混乱和无序。

然而，近年来，日本人心目中的纪律基础已经动摇。在一·二八事变期间，是谁向第十九路军的大刀队求饶？在从山海关运往北平的部队中，是谁痛哭流涕并自杀？最近，S. Miyazaki（音译）因害怕受到上级军官的惩罚，逃离了部队，脱下制服乔装消失，从而重演了仓本领事失踪的事件。随后，这名宫崎在长江洗冷水澡，若不是被一些中国人救起，他早已淹死。

帝国军队成员犯下如此违反纪律的行为，令人遗憾。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, AUGUST 2, 1937.
23395
8024
8 37

Landing Party
Voices Regrets
Over Miyazaki

Japanese Apologize For
Commotion Caused
By Search

GIVE DETAILS OF
MAN'S MOVEMENTS

Desertion, Subsequent
Falling Into Chinese
Hands Recounted

Formal regrets for the "commotion" caused by the desertion of Sadao Miyazaki, Seaman, First Class, were expressed by Rear-Admiral Denshichi Okochi, commandant of the Japanese Special Landing Party in Shanghai, in a statement published in the Japanese press yesterday.

"Deep respect and appreciation is hereby expressed by the Landing Party for the whole-hearted co-operation given by the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Japanese Consular Police, Japanese residents and officials, and, last, but not least, by the Chinese officials in the search.

"The Landing Party sincerely regrets having been the cause of such commotion at this time of crisis and hereby pledges itself to enforce self-discipline so that it may better carry out its duties for the protection of Japanese lives and property," the statement declared.

Movements Traced

The movements of Miyazaki from the time of his "disappearance" to his return on July 29 were traced in an official announcement made Saturday night.

Leaving his companions at about 6 o'clock in the afternoon, July 24, after attending the Towa Gekijo, motion picture house on Chapoo Road, Miyazaki walked along Woosung Road to an unlicensed brothel on Range Road, the announcement said.

"Emerging from the hotel," it went on, "Miyazaki saw some comrades on the street and that he had been seen by them went into a nearby alley.

"Here he met three Chinese with whom he quarrelled over money matters. In the scuffle, he lost his cap and his neckpiece.

Wanted To Kill Self

"Realizing the dishonor of returning to the barracks in such a condition, Miyazaki decided leave Shanghai and to commit suicide at a place away from his comrades. He returned to the Towa theater where he changed into sports clothes.

"On that night and on the following day, he wandered about the city and spent the night of July 25 near the Cenotaph on the Bund always seeking an opportunity to get away from Shanghai."

Miyazaki, the announcement continued, boarded a British ship at about 8 o'clock in the morning on July 26 and waited till about 11 o'clock at night when he jumped overboard.

"A good swimmer, he instinctively fought against the current and finally reached the Chinkiang shore. At about 10 o'clock the following morning, he again jumped into the Yangtse but was rescued by boatmen and handed over to the police," the announcement went on.

The following day Miyazaki was handed over to the Japanese Consulate-General in Nanking by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

"Deeply Repentent"

The sailor, the announcement said "was deeply repentent" and stated that he had been kindly treated by the Chinese police, the Kiangsu Provincial Government and the Walchiaopu.

"However, there are details concerning Miyazaki's movements that are so conflicting as to be puzzling to a normal person. He is believed to be suffering from amnesia caused by mental anguish," the statement asserted.

Kakushi Yanagida, another member of the Landing Party, who was accosted by an informer who gave his name as Okazaki on the night of July 24 was stated by the Naval Landing Party to have declared that the absconding sailor and the informer looked very much alike.

Further investigations are still being made, the statement said.

（批：JR）
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1937年8月2日，星期一。
23395
8024
8 37

陆战队
对宫崎事件
表示遗憾

日本人为搜索
引起的骚动道歉

详述该男子
的行踪

叙述其开小差及随后
落入中国人手中的经过

日本驻上海特别陆战队司令大河内传七（Denshichi Okochi）少将在昨日发表于日本报刊的一份声明中，对一等水兵宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki）开小差所引起的“骚动”正式表示遗憾。

“陆战队在此对上海公共租界工部局、日本领事警察、日本居民和官员，以及最后但同样重要的中国官员在搜寻过程中给予的全心合作，表示深深的敬意和感激。

“陆战队真诚地为在此次危机时刻造成如此骚动而感到遗憾，并在此承诺加强自律，以便更好地履行保护日本人生命和财产的职责，”声明宣称。

行踪 traced

周六晚间发布的一份官方公告追溯了宫崎从“失踪”到7月29日返回期间的行踪。

公告称，7月24日下午6点左右，在乍浦路东亚大戏院（Towa Gekijo）看完电影后，宫崎与同伴分开，沿着吴淞路走到兰路（Range Road）的一家无证妓院。

公告接着说：“从旅馆出来后，宫崎在街上看到了一些战友，因为被他们看见，他便走进附近的一条小巷。

“在这里，他遇到了三个中国人，并因金钱问题与他们发生争吵。在扭打中，他丢失了帽子和领章。

意图自杀

“意识到以这种状态回到营房是一种耻辱，宫崎决定离开上海，并在远离战友的地方自杀。他回到东亚大戏院，换上了运动服。

“当晚及次日，他在市内游荡，并在外滩纪念碑附近度过了7月25日的夜晚，一直寻找离开上海的机会。”

公告继续说道，宫崎于7月26日上午8点左右登上一艘英国轮船，一直等到晚上11点左右跳船。

“作为一名游泳好手，他本能地对抗水流，最终到达镇江岸边。次日上午10点左右，他再次跳入长江，但被船夫救起并移交给警方，”公告接着说。

第二天，宫崎由外交部移交给日本驻南京总领事馆。

“深感悔恨”

公告称，这名水兵“深感悔恨”，并表示他受到了中国警察、江苏省政府和外白渡桥方面（Walchiaopu，音译，指外白渡桥巡捕房或相关机构）的善待。

“然而，关于宫崎行踪的细节存在诸多矛盾，令常人困惑。据信他正因精神痛苦而患有失忆症，”声明断言。

陆战队另一名成员柳田角石（Kakushi Yanagida，音译），在7月24日晚被一名自称冈崎（Okazaki）的线民搭讪，据海军陆战队称，柳田声称这名逃跑的水兵与该线民长得非常相像。

声明称，进一步的调查仍在进行中。

（批：JR）

page_data.en:
August 2, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES CONSIDER MIYAZAKI CASE : HEAVY
PUNISHMENT NOT EXPECTED

Following the escorting to Shanghai
of the Japanese bluejacket named Sadao Miyazaki, who
disappeared from Shanghai on the night of July 24 and
was subsequently found and handed over to the Japanese
authorities at Nanking, an investigation was conducted
jointly into the case by the tribunal of the local
Japanese Naval Landing Party and the Criminal Division
of the Japanese Consular Police. As a result, it was
generally agreed that the absconding of Miyazaki does
not constitute an offence against military law dealing
with deserters, but was due to his fear of punishment
and repentance that drove him to a state of mental anguish,
whereupon he intended to commit suicide. For this
reason, his absconding was considered a pardonable offence.
It is now learned that Miyazaki will
be handed over to a military doctor for physical
examination as to whether or not he was suffering from
amnesia caused by mental anguish at the time of his
desertion, in order to decide whether or not a formal
charge should be brought up against him in the military
tribunal. However, it is generally believed that no
prosecution will be made against him and he will very
likely be free from any punishment. At most, he may
be accorded a bad record.
According to reliable information,
the Japanese authorities, in their investigation into
the desertion of Miyazaki, were most particular as
regards the treatment he sustained at the hands of the
Chinese authorities, because some of the radical elements
of the Japanese authorities were contemplating finding
fault with us under the pretext of ill-treatment accorded
to Miyazaki by our authorities. Fortunately, the missing
seaman is not conscientiousless and stated that he was
accorded fair treatment at the hands of the Chinese
authorities. Consequently, the Japanese authorities
were unable to secure any pretext and had to express
appreciation.
It is learned that Mr. Hitaka, Charge
d'Affaires of the Japanese Embassy, will express
appreciation to our Foreign Office, but nothing will
be mentioned about the allegation made at the time when
the seaman disappeared that he was undoubtedly kidnapped
by Chinese.
page_data.zh:
1937年8月2日。
晨间翻译。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

日本当局审议宫崎案：预计不会严惩

继7月24日晚从上海失踪、随后被发现并在南京移交给日本当局的日本水兵宫崎贞雄被护送至上海后，当地日本海军陆战队法庭与日本领事警察刑事科联合对该案进行了调查。结果，各方普遍认为，宫崎的潜逃并不构成处理逃兵的军法罪行，而是由于害怕惩罚和悔悟导致他陷入精神痛苦状态，进而意图自杀。因此，他的潜逃被视为可宽恕的过错。

据悉，宫崎将被移交给军医进行身体检查，以确定他在开小差时是否因精神痛苦而患有失忆症，从而决定是否在军事法庭对他提起正式指控。然而，人们普遍相信不会对他提起诉讼，他很可能会免受任何惩罚。至多，他可能会受到不良记录处分。

据可靠消息，日本当局在调查宫崎开小差一案时，非常关注他在中国当局手中所受的待遇，因为日本当局中的一些激进分子正企图以我国当局虐待宫崎为借口来找我们的茬。幸运的是，这名失踪水兵并非没有良心，他表示自己在中国当局手中受到了公平对待。因此，日本当局未能找到任何借口，不得不表示感谢。

据悉，日本大使馆代办高田（Hitaka，音译）先生将向我国外交部表示感谢，但对于该水兵失踪时有人指控他无疑是被中国人绑架的说法，只字未提。

page_data.en:
July 30, 1937.
Afternoon Translation

Shun Pao publishes the following letter from Kiangyin :-

PARTICULARS OF THE DISCOVERY OF S. MIYAZAKI AT KIANGYIN

The following are the particulars of how
S. Miyazaki, a member of the Japanese Naval Landing Party
in Shanghai, whose disappearance was reported on July 24,
was discovered on the river in Kiangyin on July 27.
At about 10 a.m. July 27, members of the
crew of a junk sailing in the river near Kiangyin saw some-
thing floating on the water. This was brought aboard the
junk and was found to be a naked man who was conscious and
whose head was wrapped with a piece of cloth. He was
instantly handed over to the Police and questioned. The
Inspector could not understand what the man said and on
close examination he found that the man did not look like
a Chinese. Suspecting that the man was a Chinese traitor,
the Inspector immediately reported the matter to the Hsien
Magistrate. At 2 p.m. the man was escorted to the
Magistrate's yamen where he was given refreshments, after
which he was received by the Magistrate and several other
officials of the Hsien Government. The man's skin was
dark and coarse. As he did not reply to questions put
to him in Chinese, he was asked to give his answers in
writing in Japanese. The man then stated that he was
a Japanese named S. Hikichi, employed by the Matsumoto
Yoko (松本洋行) on Woosung Road, Shanghai, and that he
had accidentally fallen into the river. When asked about
his movements and work, he did not reply.
A close scrutiny of the piece of cloth
with which his head was wrapped also produced some
suspicion. The piece of cloth was white in colour and
sparsely woven. It was about two feet in length and
about one foot in width. It was covered with red circular
marks with short red strings stitched in the centre of each
circular mark. On the right hand lower corner of the
cloth, there were inscribed two characters "Kawakami."
In the middle of the cloth there was another piece of
cloth about 5 inches in length with the inscription: "Mr.
Satao Miyazaki."
Despite the questions repeatedly put to
him by the Magistrate, the man remained reticent and it
seemed that he had certain secrets which he would not
divulge. After the interview, he was again given
cigarettes and food, and at 6 p.m. the same day he was
transferred under escort to the Kiangsu Provincial
Government at Chinkiang via Wusih together with the
statement and the piece of cloth.

China Times and other local newspapers :-

UNREASONABLE ARREST OF TWO MEN BY A FOREIGN POLICEMAN

At about 7.30 p.m. yesterday two rice shop
assistants living at No.409 Woosung Road, named Chow Foh-zung
(周福仁) and Mau Ts-ying (毛子英), whilst reading some anti-
Japanese handbills posted on a wall at the corner of Morrison
Road and Woosung Road, were unreasonably arrested by a foreign
policeman of Hongkew Police Station. The two men were falsely
accused by the foreign policeman of having posted the bills.
They are being temporarily detained in the police station
for investigation.
page_data.zh:
1937年7月30日。
下午译件

《申报》刊登如下来自江阴的信件：

在江阴发现S.宫崎的详情

以下是关于上海日本海军陆战队队员S.宫崎（其失踪于7月24日被报告）于7月27日在江阴河面被发现的详情。
7月27日上午10时许，一艘在江阴附近河道航行的舢板船员看见水面上漂浮着某物。该物体被带上舢板，发现是一名意识清醒、头部包裹着一块布料的裸体男子。他随即被移交给警方并接受讯问。巡官听不懂该男子所说的话，经仔细检查，发现该男子相貌不像中国人。巡官怀疑该男子是中国汉奸，立即将此案报告给县知事。下午2时，该男子被护送至县衙，在那里得到了茶点招待，随后由县知事及县政府其他几名官员接见。该男子皮肤黝黑粗糙。由于他对用中文提出的问题不予回答，便要求他用日文书面作答。该男子随后陈述，他是日本人，名叫S.引地（S. Hikichi），受雇于上海吴淞路的松本洋行，是不慎落入河中。当被问及他的行踪和工作时，他未作回答。
对包裹他头部的布料进行仔细查验也引起了一些怀疑。该布料为白色，织造稀疏。长约两英尺，宽约一英尺。上面布满红色圆形标记，每个圆形标记中心缝有短红线。在布料的右下角，写有“川上”二字。在布料中间，还有另一块长约5英寸的布片，上面写着：“佐藤宫崎先生（Mr. Satao Miyazaki）”。
尽管县知事反复向他提问，该男子仍保持沉默，似乎怀有不愿透露的秘密。会谈结束后，再次向他提供了香烟和食物，并于当日下午6时，连同供词和那块布料，经由无锡将其押解至镇江的江苏省政府。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, July 30, 1937

Why Mr. Miyazaki Ran Off
THE STRANGE CASE of Sadao Miyazaki now takes its place beside the famous Nanking "Kuramoto murder mystery" of 1934. Both come under the general heading of "much ado about nothing" and each has a common moral. Comparison of the two is not without interest.

Mr. Kuramoto, it will be recalled, was a Japanese consular official whose disappearance from the national capital precipitated an incident of major consequence. Gunboats churned the turgid Yangtze, impressive demands were made, war apparently threatened—and then meek and sheepish Mr. Kuramoto turned up, very hungry and dejected, out by the Ming Tomb on Purple Mountain.

It seems he had felt humiliated over some development in his official life so he went out to be eaten by wolves, even cutting the buttons off his garments in order to facilitate their gastronomic processes. But either the wolves weren't hungry or they were afraid of precipitating international complications, for Mr. Kuramoto survived to the considerable embarrassment of his fellow-countrymen who had been pounding the war drums.

Under similar conditions it appears that the Miyazaki case might have produced the same impressive results. But Seaman Miyazaki disappeared at a moment when quiet orders from Tokyo had been given up and down the China coast that because of the North China situation, Japanese provocation elsewhere was to be avoided. So although there was considerable localized excitement Saturday night, the usual rushings about of machine-gunned motorbikes and trucks and the usual haltings, searchings and general bodgering of innocent pedestrians by other than the constituted authorities (i.e. by the Naval Landing Party), and although some hundreds of terrified Chinese moved their bodies and property out of Chapei for fear of more of what they'd had previously; despite these things, the incident was kept within reasonable proportions and the resultant turning-up of Seaman Miyazaki therefore entails no particular loss of face to anybody.

Mr. Kuramoto was bundled off to Japan and so far as we know, he has not since been reported. What will happen to Seaman Miyazaki is a matter on which we need not speculate, but we suspect it may be plenty.

It appears that his misdemeanors started even before he got out of Shanghai. According to his story as reported by Central News —"I went to a house of ill fame which was not one of those designated by the Japanese Landing Party." Apparently to visit a house of ill fame not bearing the official "chop" is regarded as a heinous offense indeed; for, being seen by a fellow-seaman in this unpatriotic act, he became "full of fear" and instead of proceeding to his quarters he proceeded "in the direction of the Shanghai Cenotaph"—whether for refuge or to devote himself to pious meditation in expiation of his sin is not made clear. Meanwhile an intense search started, extending, according to one news picture, even to looking under the seats of rickshas!

Miyazaki remained in hiding for a couple of days and finally on July 26—the unseemly visit to the unofficial house occurred on July 24—he boarded a British steamer. "But in doing this," he adds, "I had no other aim than making an escape." Which should give some measure of how dreadful an offense it is for a Japanese seaman to visit a house of ill fame which has not been purified by the official approval of the Landing Party!

At Chinkiang the culprit jumped overboard, swimming ashore and spending a night in the hills—perhaps as an offering to Mr. Kuramoto's wolves, who again seem to have adopted a disdainful attitude, or perhaps again they were prudently patriotic and did not wish to break the law against anti-Japanese activities. Finally he landed in the arms of Chinese law at Kiangyin which, despite Japan's distrust of it, functioned with sufficient efficiency to deliver him back to his own—even as in the historic Kuramoto case.

The Nanking Consulate-General at last reports took a very suspicious view of the whole matter, speaking of "a person claiming to be Sadao Miyazaki" and saying it was launching an investigation, perhaps with the object of finding out why anybody should claim to be Sadao Miyazaki if he were not! We leave them to the solution of this mystery, confident that in due course they will liquidate it as effectively as was done in the instance of the well known, we trust not late, Mr. Kuramoto.

（印：31 JULY 1937）

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1937年7月30日，星期五

宫崎先生为何逃跑
佐藤宫崎的离奇案件如今可与1934年著名的南京“仓本谋杀谜案”相提并论。两者均属于“无事生非”的大类，且有着共同的寓意。比较二者并非毫无趣味。

回想起来，仓本先生是一名日本领事官员，他的从首都失踪引发了一起后果重大的事件。炮艇搅动着浑浊的长江水，提出了令人印象深刻的要求，战争显然受到威胁——随后，温顺而羞愧的仓本先生出现在紫金山明孝陵外，又饿又沮丧。

看来他因官场生涯中的某些变故感到受辱，于是出去让狼吃掉，甚至剪掉衣服上的纽扣以方便狼的消化过程。但要么狼不饿，要么它们害怕引发国际纠纷，总之仓本先生活了下来，这让那些一直在敲打响战鼓的同胞们相当尴尬。

在类似的情况下，宫崎案似乎也可能产生同样令人印象深刻的结果。但是，水兵宫崎失踪的时刻，东京已向整个中国海岸下达了平静的命令，即鉴于华北局势，应避免在其他地方进行日本挑衅。因此，尽管周六晚上局部地区相当激动，出现了机枪武装的摩托车和卡车通常的四处奔忙，以及非法定当局（即海军陆战队）对无辜行人进行的通常的拦截、搜查和一般性骚扰，尽管数百名惊恐的中国人因害怕重演之前的遭遇而将身体和财产搬出闸北；尽管有这些情况，但该事件仍保持在合理的范围内，因此水兵宫崎随后的出现并未使任何人特别丢脸。

仓本先生被匆忙送往日本，据我们所知，此后未有他的报道。水兵宫崎将面临何种结局是我们无需推测的事，但我们怀疑后果可能相当严重。

看来他的不当行为甚至在离开上海之前就开始了。根据中央通讯社报道他的故事——“我去了一家妓院，那并非日本陆战队指定的那些之一。”显然，访问一家没有官方“印章”的妓院被视为确实严重的罪行；因为，在这种不爱国行为中被一名同伴水手看见，他变得“充满恐惧”，他没有前往营房，而是朝着“上海纪念碑”方向走去——是为了寻求庇护还是为了通过虔诚的冥想来赎罪，文中并未说明。与此同时，一场激烈的搜索开始了，据一张新闻图片显示，甚至搜查了人力车的座位底下！

宫崎躲藏了两天，最终在7月26日——那次不体面的访问发生在7月24日——登上了一艘英国轮船。“但这样做，”他补充说，“我除了逃跑别无他意。”这应该能让人衡量出，一名日本水兵访问一家未经陆战队官方批准净化的妓院是何等可怕的罪行！

在镇江，这名罪犯跳船游上岸，并在山里度过了一夜——也许是作为献给仓本先生的狼的祭品，这些狼似乎再次采取了蔑视的态度，或者也许它们再次出于谨慎的爱国心，不想违反反对反日活动的法律。最后，他在江阴落入中国法律的手中，尽管日本对其不信任，但中国法律运作得足够高效，将他交还给了他自己的一方——正如历史上著名的仓本案一样。

南京总领事馆最后的报道对整个事件持非常怀疑的态度，称其为“一名自称是佐藤宫崎的人”，并表示正在展开调查，目的或许是为了查明如果不是宫崎，为何有人要自称是佐藤宫崎！我们将这个谜团的解决留给他们，相信他们会在适当的时候有效地解决它，就像在处理那位知名的、我们希望并未去世的仓本先生的案例中所做的那样。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JULY 30, 1937

3rd Fleet Commander Asks
Maintenance Of Peace

Vice-Admiral Hasegawa Warns Nanking That All
Anti-Japanese Acts Must Cease; Popular
Unrest Traced To War Preparations

If the Chinese authorities fail to take "adequate steps" to prevent "a further extension of the anti-Japanese movement," the Third Fleet will be compelled to "take steps necessary for carrying out its duty," Vice-Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa, Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet, announced in a communique issued here at 8.30 o'clock last night.

The Japanese naval authorities in China, the statement said, entertained grave concern over the trend of events and the attitude of Chinese officialdom.

"The mission of the Third Fleet," the communique stated, "has been to advance Japan's basic policy of maintaining peace in the Far East. "With this policy in mind, the Third Fleet has been endeavouring to prevent the spread of unrest from North China to other points in the country."

The communique pointed out that "the growing rampancy of the anti-Japanese activities in South and Central China hinders the peaceful pursuit of their work by Japanese officials and residents."

With Grave Concern

The statement charged that "the acceleration of the unnecessary preparations for war" leads to popular unrest.

"Such provocative actions," the communique declared, "not only form a stumbling block in the way of peaceful relations between the two nations, but may also lead to a most unhappy situation."

The Third Fleet, the statement concluded, would take every effort to prevent the outbreak of new incidents, meanwhile "watching with grave concern" the attitude of the Chinese authorities.

日本第三舰队司令长官长谷川清（Kiyoshi Hasegawa）海军中将于昨晚8时30分在此间发布的一份公报中宣布，如果中国当局未能采取“适当措施”以防止“反日运动的进一步扩大”，第三舰队将被迫“采取履行其职责所必要的措施”。

公报指出：“第三舰队的使命一直是推进日本维持远东和平的基本政策。”“本着这一政策，第三舰队一直努力防止动荡从华北蔓延至全国其他地区。”

公报指出，“华中及华南地区反日活动日益猖獗，阻碍了日本官员和居民和平开展工作。”

深表关切

该声明指责“不必要的战争准备的加速”导致民众动荡。

公报宣称：“此类挑衅行为不仅成为两国和平关系的绊脚石，还可能导致极为不幸的局面。”

声明最后表示，第三舰队将尽一切努力防止新事件爆发，同时“深切关注”中国当局的态度。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 30, 1937
“Missing” Marine And His Confession

The Japanese seaman, Sadao Miyazaki, whose disappearance Saturday was blamed on kidnapers, is shown above as he looked after being discovered in Chinkiang. He ran away from Shanghai because he was seen visiting a house of ill fame not designated by the Japanese Landing Party, he said in his confession at the right. At the top is the “thousand stiches belt” which is supposed to protect the wearer from bullets and which might have protected the seaman from being drowned in the Yangtse River.—International News Photo.

“Missing” Bluejacket Brought Back, Sped To Landing Headquarters
Miyazaki Looking Haggard, Dejected After Adventure In Chinkiang; Japanese Not Certain Of Seaman’s Identity

Haggard and visibly dejected, Sadao Miyazaki, 21-year old First Class Seaman of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, whose mysterious “disappearance” threatened to lead to another Sino-Japanese incident, arrived here from Nanking last night.

In the company of a Landing Party officer, who was sent to the capital Wednesday night to identify him, Miyazaki stepped off a train at the North Station at 9.30 o’clock. He was immediately taken to a waiting car, which sped him to the Landing Party headquarters on Kiangwan Road.

A small group of newsmen who met him at the station found the slight, youthful Japanese seaman dejected, and apparently tired. He walked slowly to the car. His face was blank and immobile.

Miyazaki, whose “disappearance” Saturday night prompted the Japanese Naval Landing Party to send armed patrols to Chapel, told authorities in Nanking that he fled from Shanghai because he feared punishment for being seen in a forbidden brothel. After remaining in Shanghai Saturday and Sunday, the seaman took a British boat bound for upriver ports.

Jumped Into River
He jumped into the Yangtse near Chinkiang but was picked up by a boatman who brought him to the local hsien government. From there, he was transferred to the Kiangsu Provincial Government, and thence to Nanking.

At the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Miyazaki made a statement to officials relating the events which occurred after he left the brothel Saturday night. He was turned over to the Japanese Consulate-General in the capital, where an officer from the Landing Party headquarters here was sent to bring him back to Shanghai.

No statement was available last night from the Landing Party headquarters regarding possible action to be taken in the case. Japanese authorities were last night withholding confirmation regarding the identity of Miyazaki. It was explained that authorities were not yet certain as to whether the man in Chinkiang is actually the missing seaman.

《大美晚报》，1937年7月30日，星期五
“失踪”的水兵及其供词

上图显示的是日本水兵宫崎贞夫在镇江被发现后的样子。上周六他的失踪曾被归咎于绑架者。他在右侧的供词中称，他逃离上海是因为被人看到光顾了一家未获日本陆战队指定的妓院。顶部展示的是据说能保护佩戴者免受子弹伤害的“千人针腰带”，这条腰带或许也保护了这名水兵，使其未在长江中溺亡。——国际新闻照片。

“失踪”水兵被带回，迅速送往陆战队总部
宫崎在镇江经历冒险后显得憔悴、沮丧；日方不确定该水兵身份

21岁的日本海军陆战队上等兵宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）昨晚从南京抵达此处。他神秘的“失踪”曾威胁引发另一起中日事件。

宫崎面容憔悴，神情明显沮丧。周三晚，一名陆战队军官被派往首都对其进行辨认。随后，宫崎与该军官一同于9时30分在北站下车。他立即被带上一辆等候的汽车，迅速驶往江湾路的陆战队总部。

在车站迎接他的一小群记者发现，这位身材瘦小、年轻的日本水兵情绪低落，显然十分疲惫。他缓慢地走向汽车。他面无表情，神态呆滞。

上周六晚宫崎的“失踪”促使日本海军陆战队向闸北派出武装巡逻队。宫崎在南京向当局表示，他逃离上海是因为害怕因被人看到进入一家禁止涉足的妓院而受到惩罚。周六和周日他留在上海，随后搭乘一艘开往上游港口的英国船只离开。

跳入江中
他在镇江附近跳入长江，但被一名船夫救起，并被带到当地县政府。此后，他被转送至江苏省政府，继而送往南京。

在外交部，宫崎向官员陈述了周六晚离开妓院后发生的事件。随后他被移交给驻首都的日本总领事馆，上海陆战队总部的一名军官被派往那里将他带回上海。

昨晚，陆战队总部未就本案可能采取的行动发表任何声明。日本当局昨晚暂不确认宫崎的身份。据解释，当局尚不确定在镇江发现的男子是否确为那名失踪的水兵。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 29, 1937

Japanese Confirmation
On Deserter Withheld

The local Japanese Consulate was still unable to confirm or deny at noon today whether the Japanese found wandering near Tsingkiang yesterday and taken to Nanking is in reality Sadao Miyazaki, whose disappearance last Saturday night from the Hongkew area created an incident which started the flow of refugees from the Chapel area. An officer of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party is in Nanking, having been sent to that city last night to identify the seaman who was handed over to the Japanese Consulate-General yesterday.

The search for the missing first class seaman has come to a halt even though the Japanese authorities are not yet convinced that Sadao, the possessor of a spotless service record, actually entered a forbidden brothel and then fled because he feared that other seamen would reveal his actions to the authorities.

Miyazaki is alleged to have confessed that after being seen in a forbidden brothel he fled out of fear of punishment. During July 24 and 25 he remained in Shanghai, then left for upriver on a British ship after throwing his uniform into the river. His cap and collar badges were thrown away during an argument with three men who came after him for money as he left the brothel. He jumped into the Yangtze near Tsingkiang, he stated, because he had no ticket and feared he might be taken to the captain and identified.

Some Chinese are elated at the outcome of the incident and suggest that Miyazaki and Kuramoto get together and form a "Dare-To-Come-Back-Alive Club." Kuramoto was the vice-consul who disappeared from Nanking in 1934, thus creating a critical situation until he was found asleep on a mountain outside the city. Other Chinese are angered and point out the hardship which this man's actions have brought to thousands of poor Chinese families who fled in terror from their homes in Chapel after the Japanese sent men in full war kit into the area. They suggest that an apology by the Japanese would be small repayment.

D. C. Koochlu
C 22/7
A. K.

OK

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年7月29日，星期四

日方暂不确认
逃兵身份

截至今日中午，日本驻沪领事馆仍无法确认或否认昨日在镇江附近被发现并已被带往南京的日本人是否确为宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）。上周六晚，宫崎从虹口地区失踪，引发了一起导致难民从闸北地区流出的事件。日本特别海军陆战队的一名军官已在南京，他于昨晚被派往该市，以辨认昨日被移交给日本总领事馆的那名水兵。

尽管日本当局尚未确信拥有清白服役记录的宫崎确实进入了一家禁止涉足的妓院，并因担心其他水兵向当局揭发其行为而逃跑，但对这名失踪上等兵的搜寻已经停止。

据称，宫崎供认，因被人看到在禁止涉足的妓院出现，他出于对惩罚的恐惧而逃跑。7月24日和25日，他留在上海，随后将军服扔进河里，乘英国船只前往上游。他说，在离开妓院时，三名向他讨钱的男子与他发生争执，期间他的帽子和领章被扔掉。他表示，由于没有船票，且担心被带到船长面前并被认出，他在镇江附近跳入长江。

一些中国人对事件的结果感到幸灾乐祸，建议宫崎与仓本（Kuramoto）聚在一起，成立一个“敢死生还俱乐部”。仓本是1934年从南京失踪的副领事，当时造成了危急局势，直到后来发现他在城外的一座山上睡觉。其他中国人则感到愤怒，指出此人的行为给成千上万贫困的中国家庭带来了苦难，在日本派遣全副武装的人员进入该地区后，这些家庭惊恐地从闸北的家中逃离。他们认为，日本的道歉仅是微不足道的补偿。

D. C. Koochlu
C 22/7
A. K.

同意

23297
8024
29 7 37
MISSING SEAMAN MYSTERY
SOLVED IN NANKING

Sadao Miyazaki Turns Up in Capital: Adventurous
Days and Nights En Route

STOWAWAY IN CHINESE RIVER STEAMER

Swims Into Arms of Gendarmes at Kiangyin Forts:
Turned Over to Foreign Office

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Nanking, July 28.
A piquant development in the present tense situation was the arrival in Nanking this afternoon of Sadao Miyazaki, first class seaman of the Imperial Japanese Navy, who was reported missing in Shanghai on the evening of July 24 and for whom Japanese, International Settlement and Chinese authorities have been combing the area for days. Miyazaki's adventures have been many and varied in the interval.

From information secured by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to whom the seaman was first turned over by Chinese gendarmerie, it appears that he was seen by comrades leaving a low class brothel in Shanghai and then followed the hue and cry and general excitement caused in the Hongkew District by patrols from the Japanese Naval Landing Party. Afraid to return to his unit, Miyazaki obtained some Chinese clothing, a singlet and a pair of Chinese trousers.

After spending the nights of July 24 and 25 on The Bund, the seaman stowed away on board a Chinese river steamer and was eventually taken into custody by the Paoantui at Chinkiang whence he was delivered to the Waichiaopu to-day. He was, after identification, turned over to the Japanese Embassy at 7.30 o'clock to-night.

Without funds, Miyazaki was in a desperate fix as the steamer approached Kiangyin. Jumping overboard at that point, he attempted to swim to the Kiangyin Forts, on the Yangtze and was pulled from the water by a passing junk who landed him on the shore. This was on Tuesday morning. All that day and through the night, Miyazaki hid in the hills behind Kiangyin, emerging yesterday morning at dawn.

On his attempting to swim across river he was again pulled from the water by a junk and this time was handed over to the Paoantui. The gendarmes, recognizing him as being anything but Chinese, immediately suspected him as a spy, a theory which was the more plausible as Kiangyin is a fortified area. Consequently he was taken to Chingkiang and later to Nanking and turned over to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

"1,000 Stitches"

Questioned there, Miyazaki at first gave his name correctly and then attempted to deny his identity. This was finally established, however, by the discovery of his name in characters on an abdominal band he was wearing, sewed with the "1,000 stitches" so popular among Japanese service men.

When visited at the Waichiaopu yesterday afternoon by your correspondent and one other foreign newspaper man, Miyazaki was nonchalantly sipping tea and munching melon seeds. He had been provided with an electric fan and was apparently being well treated. He was not greatly the worse for his four days' adventures.

First Alarm

It will be recalled that an unidentified man late on the night of July 24 reported to a Japanese marine patrol that he had seen Miyazaki involved in a fight between three Japanese blue jackets and a larger group of Chinese in an alleyway near the corner of Dixwell and North Szechuen Roads, following which Miyazaki had been whisked into a car and taken off at a high speed to an unknown destination.

This news was quickly flashed to the Naval Landing Party headquarters, the Settlement and the Chapei police, and within a few minutes the whole Hongkew area was the scene of intense military activity. Trams, motor-cars, even rickshaws were stopped and searched by marines fully armed, and with fixed bayonets, and an exodus of Chinese residents of the Chapei area immediately adjoining Hongkew began feverishly. Frequent patrols of Japanese marines continued that night, and less frequently through the days and nights that followed.

Questions and Answers

Local Japanese officials called on the City Government in connection with the affair, and questions were asked and answered as best as possible in the Diet session in Tokyo.

No information was made available yesterday, either in Nanking or Shanghai, as to the future movements of Seaman Sadao Miyazaki.

Officer Dispatched

In a special communiqué issued at 11 o'clock last night, the Japanese Naval Landing Party announced the dispatch of an official to Nanking to investigate the reports that "a Japanese, giving his name as Miyazaki, has been handed over to the Japanese Consulate-General in Nanking by the Chinese authorities."

23297
8024
29 7 37

失踪水兵之谜
在南京告破

宫崎贞夫现身首都：途中历经冒险的日夜

藏身于中国内河轮船的偷渡者

在江阴要塞游向宪兵怀抱：被移交外交部

本报特约记者

南京，7月28日电。
当前紧张局势中一个引人注目的进展是，日本帝国海军一等水兵宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）于今天下午抵达南京。他曾被报告于7月24日晚在上海失踪，连日来日本方面、公共租界当局以及中国当局一直在该区域进行搜捕。在此期间，宫崎的经历可谓多姿多彩且变幻莫测。

根据外交部获得的情报——该水兵最初由中国宪兵移交给外交部——看来，有战友看见他离开上海一家低级妓院，随后他因日本海军陆战队巡逻队在虹口区引起的喧哗和普遍恐慌而受到惊吓。由于不敢返回部队，宫崎弄到了一些中国服装，包括一件背心和一条中式裤子。

在7月24日和25日两夜露宿外滩后，这名水兵偷渡上了一艘中国内河轮船，最终在镇江被保安团拘留，并于今日被送往外交部。经身份确认后，他于今晚7时30分被移交给日本大使馆。

身无分文的宫崎在轮船接近江阴时陷入了绝境。他在那一点跳入水中，试图游向长江上的江阴要塞，后被一艘路过的舢板从水中救起并送上岸。这是星期二早晨的事。整整一天及整个夜晚，宫崎都躲在江阴背后的山丘里，直到昨天黎明时分才出来。

当他试图游泳渡江时，再次被一艘舢板从水中救起，这次他被移交给保安团。宪兵们认出他绝非中国人，立即怀疑他是间谍，鉴于江阴是要塞区，这一推测更为合理。因此，他被带往镇江，随后又被带往南京，并移交给外交部。

“千人针”

在接受询问时，宫崎起初如实报出姓名，随后又试图否认自己的身份。然而，通过在他佩戴的腹带上发现用当时在日本军人中非常流行的“千人针”缝制的汉字名字，其身份最终得以确认。

昨天下午，当本报记者和另一名外国报社记者去外交部探望时，宫崎正悠闲地喝着茶，嗑着瓜子。有人为他提供了电风扇，他显然受到了良好的待遇。经过四天的冒险，他的状况并未显得太糟。

初次警报

回想起来，7月24日深夜，一名身份不明的男子向日本海军陆战队巡逻队报告称，他看见宫崎卷入了一场冲突，冲突双方是三名日本水兵和一群人数更多的中国人，地点位于狄思威路（Dixwell Road）与北四川路（North Szechuen Road）拐角附近的一条小巷里。此后，宫崎被迅速塞进一辆汽车，高速驶往一个未知的目的地。

这一消息迅速传至海军陆战队总部、租界当局以及闸北警方，几分钟内，整个虹口地区便成为军事活动密集的场所。电车、汽车，甚至黄包车都被全副武装、刺刀上膛的海军陆战队员拦下搜查，紧邻虹口的闸北地区的中国居民随即开始惊慌外逃。日本海军陆战队的频繁巡逻持续了当晚，并在随后的日夜中虽频率降低但仍在继续。

问答环节

当地日本官员就此事拜访了市政府，而在东京的议会会议上，也就相关问题进行了尽可能详细的问询和答复。

截至昨日，无论是在南京还是上海，均未发布关于水兵宫崎贞夫未来动向的任何信息。

派遣官员

日本海军陆战队昨晚11时发布特别公报，宣布派遣一名官员前往南京，以调查有关“一名自称宫崎的日本人已由中国当局移交给日本驻南京总领事馆”的报告。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 29, 1937

MISSING JAPANESE
SAILOR IS FOUND
Signs Confession About
Details Of Leave
From Shanghai
ARRESTED NEAR WUSIH
ON SUSPICION
NANKING, July 28.—Sadao Miyazaki, the bluejacket belonging to the Japanese garrison in Shanghai, who disappeared four days ago, has been found and has been turned over to to Mr. S. Hidaka, Counsellor of the Japanese Embassy, by the Chinese Foreign Office.
Miyazaki was arrested as a suspicious character in the vicinity of the Kiangying Fort, near Wusih, yesterday. He was taken to Chinkiang and from there to the Foreign Office at Nanking, where he arrived this evening.
After he had been given tea and cakes, Miyazaki was questioned by officials of the Foreign Office. He admitted his identity, and signed a confession giving details of his departure from Shanghai, as well as his arrest near Kiangying.
Mr. Hidaka, who was notified immediately, proceeded to the Foreign Office in order to take Miyazaki to the Japanese Embassy.—Reuter.

Landing Party Officials
An officer of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party here left for Nanking by train last night to identify a Japanese, whom, the Chinese said, admitted that he is Sadao Miyazaki, First Class Seaman, who mysteriously disappeared on Saturday night.
In a special communique issued at 11 o'clock last night, the Landing Party announced the dispatch of an official to Nanking to investigate the reports that "a Japanese, giving his name as Miyazaki, has been handed over to the Japanese Consulate-General in Nanking by the Chinese authorities."—Domei.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年7月29日，星期四

失踪的日本
水兵已被找到
签署供词详述
离开上海经过
因涉嫌在无锡
附近被捕

南京，7月28日电。——隶属于上海日本驻军的水兵宫崎贞夫，在失踪四天后已被找到，并由中国外交部移交给日本大使馆参赞日高信六郎（S. Hidaka）先生。

宫崎昨日作为可疑人物在无锡附近的江阴要塞一带被捕。他被带往镇江，再从那里被送往南京的外交部，并于今晚抵达。

在享用茶点后，宫崎接受了外交部官员的讯问。他承认了自己的身份，并签署了一份供词，详细说明了其离开上海以及在江阴附近被捕的经过。

接到通知后立即前往日高先生前往外交部，以便将宫崎带往日本大使馆。——路透社

海军陆战队官员

日本特别海军陆战队的一名军官昨晚乘火车前往南京，以辨认一名日本人，据中方称，此人承认自己是上周六晚神秘失踪的一等水兵宫崎贞夫。

在昨晚11时发布的特别公报中，海军陆战队宣布派遣一名官员前往南京，以调查有关“一名自称宫崎的日本人已由中国当局移交给日本驻南京总领事馆”的报告。——同盟社

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, JULY 29, 1937

Seaman Is
Found, Safe
And Sound

'Missing' Marine Hand-
ed Over To Nanking
Consulate

TELLS STORY OF
DISAPPEARANCE

Miyazaki Jumps In River
In Chinkiang, Saved
By Boatman

NANKING, July 28.—(Central).—
Sadao Miyazaki, Japanese seaman,
whose strange disappearance from
Shanghai last Saturday had caused
much excitement, has been found
safe and sound in Chinkiang, it
was learned here tonight.

The discovery of Miyazaki in
Chinkiang, on the opposite bank of
the Yangtse River from Kiangyin,
was strongly reminiscent of the
Kuramoto case of 1934.

Miyazaki was this afternoon
handed over to the Japanese Con-
sulate-General in Nanking.

A ferry boatman, it was stated,
picked him up from the river at
Chinkiang and brought him to the
district government there.

The district government took him
to the provincial government of
Kiangsu, which in turn sent him to
Nanking this afternoon, and
officials of the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs handed over to the Japanese
authorities shortly afterwards.

In reply to questions put to him
while he was in the Foreign Office,
Miyazaki revealed his identity as
well as his mysterious movements
since July 24. Following is
Miyazaki's own story:

Visited House Of Ill Fame

"I went to a house of ill fame
which was not one of those de-
signated by the Japanese Landing
Party and was seen by a fellow
seaman. Full of fear I did not re-
turn to my quarters and proceeded
in the direction of the Shanghai
Cenotaph.

"I remained in Shanghai on July
24 and 25 and boarded a British
steamer at 8 o'clock on July 26,
but in doing this I had no other
aim than making an escape.

"At about 11 p.m. on July 26, I
jumped over-board at a point near
the police station of Chinkiang. I
reached Chinkiang and spent the
night in the hills. At about 10 a.m.
on July 27 I again jumped into
the Yangtse River and attempted
to swim across from Chinkiang.

Rescued By Boatman

"But before I got to the opposite
shore, I was rescued by a boatman
and was sent to the police station
of Chinkiang.

"The house of ill fame I visited
was located on Range Road. I
went there alone at about 9 p.m.
on July 24, and remained there till
about 9.30 p.m.

"It was a house kept by Chinese
and I paid two dollars. Just as I
was leaving three men who looked
like Chinese came after me for
money. There was an argument
but I did not pay them.

"Then I took a ricsha and went
in the direction of the cenotaph.

"When I was leaving the house
I was seen by a fellow seaman, but
I did not know his name. The
above-mentioned argument took
place after I was seen by my fellow
seaman.

"When I was involved in the
argument I was dressed in my uni-
form, but in the midst of it, I
threw away my cap and collar
badges. Then I went away on a
ricsha. When I have gone past
the cenotaph, I wrapped my uni-
form in a newspaper, which I car-
ried with me when I went aboard
the steamer.

Felt Miserable

"It was finally thrown away when
I jumped into the river because I
felt very miserable. I jumped into
the river because I was sleeping
on the topmost deck where I was
about to be discovered.

"I was afraid I might be taken
to the captain, because I had no
ticket; I was so afraid that I jump-
ed into the river."

The story was signed by Miyazaki
himself.

Issues Statement

NANKING, July 28.—(Domei).—
Admitting that a Japanese claiming
to be Sadao Miyazaki, First Class
Seaman, who disappeared in
Shanghai on Saturday night, was
delivered to its custody by the
Waichiaopu, the Japanese Con-
sulate-General here tonight an-
nounced that a formal investiga-
tion would be launched at once.

The Consular statement read:

"A person, claiming to be Sadao
Miyasaki, First Class Seaman, who
disappeared in Shanghai on Satur-
day night, was handed over to the
Consulate-General by the Wai-
chiaopu at 8 o'clock this evening.

"As it was thought certain that
the man in question was a Japanese,
the Consulate-General took the man
into custody, together with some
articles and a statement brought
with him.

Proof Awaited

"The Consulate-General is await-
ing the arrival of representatives
of the authorities concerned before
opening an investigation.

"Until this investigation is com-
pleted, the Consulate-General is not
in a position to confirm or deny
that the man is the sailor who has
been missing since the night of
July 24.

"This Consulate-General is not
yet in the possession of full informa-
tion on how this person was found
and delivered to this Consulate-
General by the Chinese authorities
in Nanking."

《大美晚报》，1937年7月29日，星期四

水兵被发现
安然无恙

“失踪”的海军陆战队员
被移交给南京领事馆

讲述失踪经过

宫崎在镇江跳入河中
被船夫救起

南京，7月28日电。（中央通讯社）——
据悉，日本水兵宫崎贞夫已于镇江被安全找到。他于上周六从上海离奇失踪，曾引起极大轰动。

在长江对岸与江阴相对的镇江发现宫崎，让人强烈想起1934年的仓本（Kuramoto）案件。

宫崎于今天下午被移交给日本驻南京总领事馆。

据称，一名渡船船夫在镇江的河里将他捞起，并将他带到当地的区政府。

区政府将他送往江苏省政府，省政府又于今天下午将他送往南京，随后由外交部官员移交给日本当局。

在外交部接受询问时，宫崎透露了自己的身份以及自7月24日以来神秘的行踪。以下是宫崎的自述：

光顾非指定妓院

“我去了一家并非日本海军陆战队指定的妓院，并被一名同僚水兵看见。出于恐惧，我没有返回营房，而是朝上海纪念碑方向走去。

“我于7月24日和25日留在上海，并于7月26日8点登上一艘英国轮船，但我这样做只是为了逃跑。

“7月26日晚上11点左右，我在镇江警察局附近的一个地点跳船。我到达镇江，并在山里过了一夜。7月27日上午10点左右，我再次跳入长江，试图从镇江游到对岸。

被船夫救起

“但在到达对岸之前，我被一名船夫救起，并被送到镇江警察局。

“我去的那家妓院位于兰路（Range Road）。我于7月24日晚上9点左右独自前往，并在那里待到晚上9点半左右。

“那是一家由中国人经营的店，我付了两美元。正当我离开时，三个看起来像中国人的男人追上来要钱。虽然发生了争执，但我没有付钱给他们。

“随后我坐了一辆黄包车，朝纪念碑方向走去。

“当我离开那家店时，被一名同僚水兵看见，但我不知道他的名字。上述争执发生在我被同僚水兵看见之后。

“卷入争执时，我身穿制服，但在争执过程中，我扔掉了帽子和领章。然后我坐黄包车离开。经过纪念碑后，我把制服包在报纸里，登船时一直带在身边。

感到痛苦

“最后当我跳入河中时把它扔掉了，因为我感到非常痛苦。我跳河是因为我睡在最顶层的甲板上，快要被人发现了。

“我担心因为没有船票而被带到船长那里；因为太害怕，所以我跳进了河里。”

这段陈述由宫崎本人签名。

发表声明

南京，7月28日电。（同盟社）——日本驻南京总领事馆今晚承认，一名自称是上周六晚在上海失踪的一等水兵宫崎贞夫的日本人，已由外交部移交给其保管，并宣布将立即展开正式调查。

领事馆声明如下：

“一名自称是上周六晚在上海失踪的一等水兵宫崎贞夫的人，于今晚8点由外交部移交给本总领事馆。

“由于认为此人确系日本人，总领事馆将其连同其携带的一些物品和一份陈述书一并收押。

等待证据

“总领事馆正在等待有关当局代表抵达，以便开始调查。

“在调查完成之前，总领事馆无法确认或否认此人就是自7月24日晚以来一直失踪的那名水兵。

“本总领事馆尚未掌握关于此人如何被发现以及由中国当局在南京移交给本总领事馆的全部信息。”

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 28, 1937
23288

29 7 37
"Thin Man" Sought
To Clear Up Mystery
Of "Missing" Marine

Belief Held Miyazaki
And Informer One
And The Same

WAR-TIME COUNCIL
ORGANIZED HERE

Flag, Water Melons,
Chicken Figure In
Kiangwan Mystery

Is Sadao Miyazaki, the "missing"
Japanese bluejacket, and Yoshio
Okasaki, the mysterious Nipponese
civilian who claimed to have eye-
witnessed the former's "kidnap-
ing," the same man?

This question was being asked
yesterday in certain local foreign
official circles as the alleged "dis-
appearance" of the 21-year-old First
Class Seaman of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party remained
shrouded in mystery after three
days of intensive investigation.

One theory on which the investi-
gators of the case were said to be
working was to the effect that
Miyazaki executed a perfect
"A.W.O.L.", changed to civilian
clothes, and then reported his own
"kidnaping."

No Factual Support

Although this theory, like the
original story of the "abduction,"
has no factual support, investiga-
tors were reported to be speculat-
ing on the chance that Okasaki,
the informer, who gave a false
name and address, was no other
person than the "missing" blue-
jacket, whose disappearance caused
the Naval Landing Party to send
out armed patrols to Chapel.

The only available description of
the mysterious informer was that
he is a "thin man." This descrip-
tion, it was pointed out, is inclined
to tally with that of Miyazaki.
Japanese sources had previously
stated that in the "hands of the
'thin man' lies the solution of the
Miyazaki case."

Another "Incident"

Meantime, as the search for the
bluejacket continued, local Japanese
newspapers yesterday devoted large
space not to the "kidnaping," but
to the new incident centering
around the disappearance Monday
of a Japanese flag, 10 water melons
and one chicken from the fruit
farm of K. Temizu on Shuitien
Road, Kiangwan.

Japanese reports stated yesterday
that the "Japanese officialdom
moved swiftly on Monday in taking
action" regarding the incident, and
that "with implications of a de-
liberate attempt to insult the
national colors by the Peace Pre-
servation Corps freely mentioned in
the local Japanese press, the case
assumed a serious proportion in
view of the tense situation."

Mr. Y. Fukui, Japanese Vice-
Consul, called on Mayor O. K. Yui
to draw the latter's attention to the
affair. Mr. Yui was reported to
have replied that he would order
an investigation.

Form Emergency Council

For the first time since the days
of the "Shanghai war" in 1932,
local Japanese officials and civic
organizations on Monday decided
to form an Emergency Council, de-
signed to deal with "possible local
developments in the present delicate
situation in North China."

Mr. S. Okamoto, Consul-Gen-
eral, was elected chairman of the
Council at a meeting Monday after-
noon. Represented on the organiza-
tion will be the Japanese Con-
sulate-General, the Japanese Naval
Landing Party, the office of the
Japanese Military Attache, the
Japanese Residents' Corporation,
the Federation of the Amalgamated
Japanese Street Unions and other
bodies.

Measures for creating relief faci-
lities for Japanese refugees from
the interior and for the evacuation
of local Japanese women and
children were discussed at the
meeting.

《字林西报》，1937年7月28日，星期三
23288
8024
29 7 37
寻找“瘦子”
以解开“失踪”
海军陆战队员之谜

据信宫崎
与线人系
同一人

战时委员会
在此组织

旗帜、西瓜、
鸡卷入江湾谜案

这名“失踪”的日本水兵宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki），与声称亲眼目睹前者被“绑架”的神秘日本平民冈崎芳夫（Yoshio Okasaki），是否是同一个人？

昨日，在当地某些外国官员圈子中，人们纷纷提出这一疑问。经过三天的密集调查，这名21岁的日本海军陆战队一等水兵的所谓“失踪”案依然笼罩在迷雾之中。

据称，案件调查人员正在依据的一种理论认为，宫崎实施了一次完美的“擅离职守”（A.W.O.L.），换上便衣，然后报告了自己被“绑架”。

缺乏事实支持

尽管这一理论与最初的“绑架”故事一样，缺乏事实支持，但据报道，调查人员正在推测这样一种可能性：即提供了虚假姓名和地址的线人冈崎，并非他人，正是那名“失踪”的水兵；他的失踪导致海军陆战队派出武装巡逻队前往闸北（Chapei）。

关于这位神秘线人的唯一描述是他是一个“瘦子”。有人指出，这一描述倾向于与宫崎的特征相符。日本方面此前曾表示，“‘瘦子’手中掌握着解决宫崎案的关键”。

另一起“事件”

与此同时，在继续搜寻这名水兵的过程中，当地日本报纸昨日并未大篇幅报道“绑架”案，而是大量报道了另一起新事件，该事件围绕周一发生在江湾水电路（Shuitien Road）K. Temizu 果园的一面日本国旗、10个西瓜和一只鸡的失踪案展开。

日本方面的报道昨日称，针对此事件，“日本官方周一迅速采取行动”，并且“鉴于局势紧张，当地日文报刊 freely 提及保安队故意侮辱国旗的暗示，使得此案显得事态严重”。

日本副领事福井（Y. Fukui）拜会了市长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui），提请后者注意此事。据报道，俞市长回答说他将下令进行调查。

成立紧急委员会

自1932年“上海战争”以来，当地日本官员和民间团体于周一首次决定成立一个紧急委员会，旨在应对“当前华北微妙局势下可能出现的本地事态发展”。

在周一下午举行的会议上，总领事冈本（S. Okamoto）当选为委员会主席。日本总领事馆、日本海军陆战队、日本武官处、日本居留民团、日本各街道联合会以及其他团体将在该组织中派有代表。

会议讨论了为来自内地的日本难民建立救济设施，以及撤离当地日本妇女和儿童的措施。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JULY 28, 1937.
83283

Exodus From
Chapei Grows
On War News

Japanese Maintain Calm;
Leave Is Granted By
Landing Party

REWARD IS OFFERED IN
DISAPPEARANCE CASE

Police, S. V. C., Reported
To Have Received An
Emergency Order

With news of further clashes
in North China and the
vernacular afternoon papers
appearing with alarmist head-
lines on the situation, a large
exodus from Chapei into the
Settlement was witnessed late
yesterday afternoon, lasting
right up to midnight.

Scenes that came very close to
duplicating those witnessed here in
1932 were seen along North Honan
Road and especially in the vicinity
of the North Railway Station, from
which area residents trekked into
the Settlement south of the creek.
It is estimated that about 10,000
Chinese moved out of Chapei yes-
terday, but the exodus was not
large enough, nor was panic
sufficiently widespread, to warrant
action such as was taken by Mayor
Wu Te-chen last summer in prev-
enting an exodus from Chapei. It
will be remembered that exodus
started following the killing of a
Japanese sea-food broker, named
Kayau, on Chienmen Road on July
10, 1936.

While a certain portion of the
Chinese public was taking a very
gloomy attitude of the northern
situation, and taking precautions to
protect their personal belongings,
the local Japanese were viewing
the situation in different light.
Despite there still being no news
at all of the allegedly kidnapped
sailor, leave was once again grant-
ed to members of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party.

Reward Offered

A reward of $25 was offered by
the Shanghai Municipal Police yes-
terday to the ricsha coolie who was
engaged by the informer, who still
remains a great mystery, it being
freely suspected that he was
not a Japanese. It was even
hinted in some quarters that
the missing sailor Miyazaki might
himself have made the report, after
having changed into civilian dress.
Belief in the possibility of this

theory by the Japanese authorities
has been shown during the three
days by the great vigilance shown
by the Japanese Consular Police in
watching all outgoing boats and
trains.

Emergency Order

An emergency order was report-
ed to have been issued by the
Shanghai Municipal Police and the
Shanghai Volunteer Corps yester-
day. The officers of the Shanghai
Volunteer Corps, it is understood,
were requested to check up on
means of communicating with their
men in case of urgent mobilization.
It was understood yesterday that,
in view of large crowds coming into
the Settlement and the likely neces-
sity of dealing with mobs, most of
the junior detectives of the S.M.P.
would be ordered into uniform.
Men up to the rank of Detective
Sub-Inspector will probably go into
uniform in case of an emergency
arising.

Rumours were also circulated that
Japanese residents were contemplat-
ing forming a volunteer police force
with a view to protecting the areas
densely populated by their
nationals.

Japanese Meet

For the first time since the days
of the Shanghai "war," local Japan-
ese official and civic bodies on
Monday decided on the formation
of an Emergency Council, designed
to deal with possible local develop-
ments in the present delicate situa-
tion in North China.

Mr. Suemasa Okamoto, Consul-
General, was elected chairman at
the Council's first meeting held at
the Japanese Club from 4.30 o'clock
Monday afternoon.

Represented on the body will be
the Japanese Consulate-General, the
Special Naval Landing Party, the
office of the Military Attache, the
Japanese Residents' Corporation, the
Chamber of Commerce and In-
dustry, the Federation of Japanese
Cotton Millowners in China and the
Federation of Amalgamated Japan-
ese Street Unions.

Among the objectives of the
organization is the creation of re-
lief facilities for possible refugees
from the interior of China and for
the evacuation of local women and
children should the situation war-
rant such a step.—Domei.

Chinese Press Comment

With the imminent large scale
fighting in North China threatening,
practically all leading Chinese
papers here yesterday believed that
the "last minute" for the abandon-
ing of hopes for peace has arrived.
The journals unanimously declar-
ed that China has reached her limit
of endurance and has no more room
to retreat.

The "Ta Kung Pao" offered two
points for consideration of the
authorities:

Firstly; General Sung Cheh-yuan
should be responsible to the Cen-
tral Government, and his 29th Army
should form a portion of the uni-
form movement of the country and
receive their orders directly from
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek.

Secondly: the ultimate responsi-
bility should rest with the Central
Government. Now that the last
minute has arrived, it should make
known its attitude and movement
and give final instructions to Gen-
eral Sung Cheh-yuan.

The "Shun Pao" and the "Central
China Daily News" both clamoured
for the last sacrifice in view of the
gravity of the situation.—Central
News.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年7月28日，星期三
83283

随着战事消息传来
闸北居民外逃增多

日本人保持冷静；
海军陆战队批准休假

失踪案悬赏

据报道，警方及上海义勇队
已接到紧急命令

随着华北进一步冲突的消息传来，以及中文晚报以耸人听闻的标题报道局势，昨日下午晚些时候至午夜，目睹了大量居民从闸北涌入租界。

沿北河南路，特别是在北站附近，出现了几乎重现1932年此处所见景象的画面，该地区的居民徒步向南越过浜进入租界。据估计，昨天约有1万名中国人搬离闸北，但外逃规模并不大，恐慌也未广泛到足以 warrant 采取去年夏天吴铁城市长为防止闸北居民外逃所采取的那种行动。值得回忆的是，那次外逃始于1936年7月10日一名名叫 Kayau（音译）的日本海鲜经纪人在江门路（Chienmen Road）被杀之后。

虽然部分中国公众对北方局势持非常悲观的态度，并采取措施保护个人财产，但当地日本人则以不同的眼光看待局势。尽管据称被绑架的水兵仍无音讯，日本海军陆战队成员再次获准休假。

提供赏金

上海公共租界工部局警务处昨日向受雇于线人的黄包车夫提供25美元赏金，该线人至今仍是个巨大的谜团，人们普遍怀疑他并非日本人。甚至有人在某些场合暗示，失踪的水兵宫崎可能在换上便装后自己进行了报案。日本当局在这三天里通过日本领事警察对所有出境船只和火车表现出的高度警惕，显示了他们对这种理论可能性的相信。

紧急命令

据报道，上海公共租界工部局警务处和上海义勇队昨日发布了紧急命令。据了解，上海义勇队的军官被要求核实与其下属联络的方式，以备紧急动员之需。据悉，鉴于大量人群涌入租界，以及可能需要应对暴民，大多数警务处初级侦探将被命令穿上制服。在出现紧急情况时，职级高达侦探副督察的人员可能会穿上制服。

另有谣言流传称，日本居民正考虑组建一支志愿警察部队，以保护其国民密集居住的地区。

日本人集会

自上海“战争”时期以来，当地日本官方和民间团体于周一首次决定成立一个紧急委员会，旨在应对当前华北微妙局势下可能出现的本地事态发展。

周一下午4点30分在日本俱乐部举行的委员会第一次会议上，总领事冈末政（Suemasa Okamoto）当选为主席。

日本总领事馆、特别海军陆战队、武官处、日本居留民团、工商会、在华日本棉纺业者联合会以及日本各街道联合会将在该机构中派有代表。

该组织的目标之一是为可能来自中国内地的难民建立救济设施，并在局势需要时撤离当地妇女和儿童。——同盟社

中文报刊评论

随着华北大规模战斗迫在眉睫的威胁，昨日这里几乎所有主要中文报纸都认为，放弃和平希望的“最后时刻”已经到来。各报一致宣称，中国已达到忍耐的极限，再无退路。

《大公报》提出两点供当局考虑：

第一；宋哲元将军应向中央政府负责，其第二十九军应纳入国家统一行动的一部分，并直接接受蒋介石委员长的命令。

第二：最终责任应由中央政府承担。既然最后时刻已经到来，政府应表明其态度和行动，并向宋哲元将军发出最终指示。

鉴于局势严重，《申报》和《华中日报》均呼吁做出最后牺牲。——中央通讯社

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, July 27, 1937
n3272
8024
28 7 37

Hongkew Quiet,
Exodus Resumed

Theory Advanced Sailor
On "French Leave;"
Bonds Drop

While the local hunt for the allegedly kidnapped Japanese seaman continues, the Japanese authorities appear today to be taking a less serious view of the incident than at first. The Japanese consul-general, Mr. S. Okamoto, called on Mr. Stirling Fessenden, secretary-general of the Shanghai Municipal Council, yesterday afternoon but instead of asking for assistance in locating the missing bluejacket as alleged, expressed his thanks for the operation given by the S.M.P. in the hunt.

Rumors of Japanese military maneuvers to be held in Chapei during the early hours of this morning, although without foundation were sufficient to start another exodus on a small scale. As indicative of the wild stories that are now in circulation among the illiterate portion of the Chinese population, Mr. Fessenden related how an excited Chinese had informed him last night that the Japanese were about to occupy the Central Post Office.

French Leave Theory
The Japanese now hint openly that the witness who reported the kidnapping of the bluejacket and then gave a false name and address was in reality a Chinese or Korean. The Chinese press counters by stating that the whole incident was invented by the Japanese out of thin air or that the man has already returned to the barracks.

One popular theory is that Miyazaki is in reality on "French leave," having developed a great fondness for a cabaret or beer parlor cutie in whose home he is now hiding. He and the mysterious witness are believed to be one and the same person. After changing to civilian clothes, according to this theory, Miyazaki approached several bluejackets with whom he was not familiar, they being from another ship, and handed them his own cap and tie, telling them about his own kidnapping.

Melon Patch Case
The "Melon Patch Incident" at the fruit farm of Mr. Kiyoshi Temizu at Kiangwan is apparently not being taken very seriously by the Chinese authorities although Mr. Temizu sees in the disappearance of a Japanese flag and the uprooting of his flagpole the nefarious work of the Peace Preservation Corps. He also alleges that the same body took his Chinese helpers into custody on July 22. Vegetable beds had been trampled down during Sunday night and 10 melons and one chicken stolen. Japanese papers seized on this affair as a new insult to Japan and devoted much space to it, but the vernacular press was inclined to ridicule Mr. Temizu and his melon patch incident. The Chinese helpers are reported released, but cannot be located.

Japanese reports state that Japanese officialdom "moved swiftly" on Monday in taking action regarding the reported disappearance of a sun flag from the Japanese truck farm. Implications of a deliberate attempt to insult the national colors by the Chinese Peace Preservation Corps are freely mentioned, the case "assuming serious proportions in view of the tense situation."

Mr. Yasumitsu Fukui, vice-consul, called on Mr. O. K. Yui, Acting mayor of Greater Shanghai, to draw the latter's attention to the affair. Mr. Yui is said to have replied that he would order an investigation.

As a result of the disappearance of the bluejacket, Japanese residents have been advised to adopt a "cautious and watchful" attitude. The scanning of passenger lists on outgoing vessels and visits to hospitals as well as the questioning of a Japanese waitress and the hunt for the "Thin Man" in connection with the Miyazaki case occupied the Japanese naval and consular authorities yesterday, but results were nil.

Emergency Council Formed
For the first time since the days of the Shanghai "war", local Japanese official and civic bodies have decided on the formation of an Emergency Council, designed to deal with possible local developments in the present delicate situation in North China.

Mr. Suemasa Okamoto, consul-general, was elected chairman at the Council's first meeting held at the Japanese Club from 4:30 o'clock yesterday afternoon.

Relief Planned
Represented on the body will be the Japanese Consulate-General, the Special Naval Landing Party, the office of the military attache, the Japanese Residents Corporation, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Federation of Japanese Cotton Millowners in China and the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions.

Among the objectives of the organization is the creation of relief facilities for possible refugees from the interior of China and for the evacuation of local women and children should the situation warrant such a step.

Planes Curtailed
With the Sino-Japanese armed clash again flaring up near Peiping, transportation between the old capital and Shanghai remained at a standstill today. Airplanes and trains from Shanghai again made Tientsin the terminal.

A China National Aviation Corporation plane left for Tientsin this morning while The Eurasia plane left Hongkong this morning for Taiyuan from where the passengers will be conveyed to Peiping by a smaller craft if the situation is favorable. The Blue Express as usual, arrived from Tientsin this morning while the northbound night express will leave tonight for Tientsin.

Chinese government bonds this morning again dropped as gloomy reports poured in from North China. As result of the trading on the Chinese Bond and Stock Exchange, the A class issues declined by $1.70 for August and the B class dropped by $1.15. The other issues dropped slightly from five cents to 75 cents.

Trading was confined to the August deliveries as the settlement for the spot trading is to take place on Thursday.

虹口平静，
外逃 resumed（恢复）

水手“不辞而别”说甚嚣尘上；
公债下跌

尽管当地仍在搜寻据称被绑架的日本水兵，但日本当局今日似乎已不像起初那样重视此事。日本总领事冈本先生（S. Okamoto）昨日下午拜访了上海公共租界工部局总董费信惇先生（Stirling Fessenden），但他并未如传言所称请求协助寻找失踪的水兵，反而对工部局警务处（S.M.P.）在搜寻行动中提供的协助表示感谢。

有关日军将于今日凌晨在闸北举行军事演习的谣言，虽无事实根据，却足以引发另一轮小规模的外逃潮。费信惇先生讲述了一名激动的华人昨晚告知他日本人即将占领中央邮政总局一事，以此说明目前在中国不识字人群中流传的荒诞故事之程度。

“不辞而别”理论
日本人现在公开暗示，那名报告水兵被绑架、随后却提供虚假姓名和地址的证人，实际上是一名中国人或朝鲜人。中国报刊则反驳称，整个事件完全是日本人凭空捏造，或者该人已经返回兵营。

一种流行的说法是，宫崎（Miyazaki）实际上是“不辞而别”（即擅离职守），因为他迷恋上了一位歌舞厅或啤酒馆的女郎，并正藏匿在其家中。人们相信他和那位神秘的证人是同一个人。根据这一理论，宫崎换上便服后，接近了几名他不熟悉的、来自另一艘舰艇的水兵，将自己的帽子和领带交给他们，并向他们讲述了自己被绑架的经历。

瓜田案
位于江湾的清吉·清水（Kiyoshi Temizu）先生果园发生的“瓜田事件”，显然未引起中国当局的高度重视，尽管清水先生认为日本国旗失踪及旗杆被拔起是保安队的恶行。他还指控该组织于7月22日拘捕了他的中国助手。周日夜间，菜地被践踏，10个瓜和1只鸡被盗。日本报纸抓住此事作为对日本的新侮辱，并大篇幅报道，但中文报刊则倾向于嘲笑清水先生及其瓜田事件。据报道，中国助手已被释放，但下落不明。

日本方面的报告称，日本官方周一就日本卡车农场 Reported（据报道）丢失太阳旗一事“迅速采取行动”。有人随意提及中国保安队故意侮辱日本国旗的企图，鉴于局势紧张，此案“事态严重”。

副领事福井康光先生（Yasumitsu Fukui）拜访了上海特别市代理市长俞鸿钧先生（O. K. Yui），提请后者注意此事。据说俞先生回答说他将下令调查。

由于水兵失踪事件，日本侨民被建议采取“谨慎和警惕”的态度。昨日，日本海军和领事当局检查了离境船只的乘客名单，走访了医院，讯问了一名日本女招待，并搜寻与宫崎案有关的“瘦子”，但一无所获。

成立紧急委员会
自上海“战争”时期以来，当地日本官方和民间团体首次决定成立一个紧急委员会，旨在应对当前华北微妙局势下可能出现的本地事态发展。

昨日下午4时30分在日本俱乐部举行的委员会第一次会议上，总领事冈本周政先生（Suemasa Okamoto）当选为主席。

计划救济
该机构的代表包括日本总领事馆、特别海军陆战队、武官办公室、日本居留民团、工商会、在华日本棉纺业联合会以及日本各街道工会联合会。

该组织的目标之一是为可能来自中国内地的难民建立救济设施，并在局势需要时撤离当地的妇女和儿童。

航班缩减
随着中日武装冲突再次在北平附近爆发，旧都（北平）与上海之间的交通今日仍处于停滞状态。从上海出发的飞机和火车再次以天津为终点站。

一架中国航空公司的飞机今晨飞往天津，而欧亚航空公司的飞机今晨从香港出发前往太原，如果局势有利，乘客将从那里换乘小型交通工具前往北平。蓝皮特快列车如常于今晨从天津抵达，而北上的夜车将于今晚开往天津。

今晨，随着来自华北的悲观消息纷至沓来，中国政府公债再次下跌。受中国债券股票交易所交易影响，A类债券8月交割价下跌1.70美元，B类债券下跌1.15美元。其他债券小幅下跌，跌幅从5美分到75美分不等。

交易仅限于8月交割，因为现货交易的结算将于周四进行。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JULY 27, 1937

SHANGHAI "PERILS"
Curious News in Japan

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Without any lengthy introduc-
tion I desire you to know that I was
very greatly surprised to receive a
letter from my wife, now in Japan,
which expressed a great deal of
anxiety over the safety of foreigners
in general at present in Shanghai.
The letter was written on the 21st
and arrived by the last N.Y.K.
Express steamer. In the letter it is
clearly stated that the landing party
had already taken charge of the
Hongkew district and fullest instruc-
tions given as to my daughter's
movements amongst the terrible
dangers.
Already I have answered the letter
and have given every assurance that
no such trouble exists, but I keep
on looking at the news column of
this morning, especially noting such
remarks as "and took him off at a
high speed in an unknown direction"
also, "The informer could not be
found last night" etc., etc. and I am
yet trying to discover how the news
was about in Japan before the
incident.
For confirmation of the foregoing I
enclose name of one who travelled by
the steamer bearing similar state-
ments.
PERPLEXED.
Shanghai, July 26.

"It has been evident from the
reports of listeners to the Broadcasts
and from sensational telegrams
received apparently abroad, that
Shanghai has been pictured during
the last week as in the throes of
disorder. That rather than any
magical prevision seems to have
caused the anxiety expressed in the
lady's letter. For example a London
telegram of July 14 reported that
"Japanese troops and the naval
landing party stationed in barracks
near Hongkew Park have been
ordered to stand by in readiness for
eventuality, while Japanese warships
in harbour have cleared for action."
It must be confessed that these ex-
citements escaped the notice of this
journal and apparently of the
Japanese authorities here as well.

S

上海的“危险”
日本的奇闻

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——无需冗长的介绍，我想让您知道，我收到身在日本的妻子来信，信中表达了对目前在上海的外国人整体安全的极大焦虑，这让我感到非常惊讶。这封信写于21日，由最后一班日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）的特快轮船送达。信中明确 stated（陈述），登陆部队已经接管了虹口区，并就我女儿在可怕危险中的行动给予了最充分的指示。
我已经回信，并保证根本不存在此类麻烦，但我仍不断查看今晨的新闻栏目，特别注意到诸如“并以高速将其带往未知方向”以及“线人昨晚未能找到”等评论，等等，等等，而我仍在试图弄清在该事件发生之前，日本是如何得知这些消息的。
为证实上述情况，我附上了一位乘坐轮船旅行者的姓名，该人也发表了类似的声明。
困惑者
上海，7月26日。

“从广播听众的报告以及显然发往国外的耸人听闻的电报中可以明显看出，上周上海被描绘成处于混乱的痛苦之中。这似乎比任何神奇的预见更导致了那位女士信中表达的焦虑。例如，7月14日的一则伦敦电报报道称，‘驻扎在虹口公园附近兵营的日本军队和海军陆战队已奉命待命，以备不测，而港内的日本军舰也已做好战斗准备。’必须承认，这些骚动未被本报注意到，显然也未引起此地日本当局的注意。

23261

27 7 37

Hongkew Continues Calm
Despite Frantic Search
For Missing Bluejacket

Police Said To Be Pinning Hopes On “Thin Man”
To Solve Miyazaki Case; Appearance Of
Chinese Papers Brings New Exodus

IMPORTANCE ATTACHED TO DEPARTURE
OF CHINESE DIPLOMAT TO-DAY

With the allegedly kidnapped Japanese bluejacket still missing and things taking a turn for the worse in North China the Hongkew area was quiet at a late hour last evening. Word of the renewed fighting and of the progress of local investigations in the Miyazaki case was circulated through late hour editions of Chinese newspapers, however, and there was certain evidence that another exodus was beginning.

Many residents quietly piled their worldly belongings into waiting rickshas and headed towards the sanctuary on the other side of Soochow Creek. All over Hongkew the favourite Japanese amusement places were quiet and empty, and Japanese were conspicuous by their absence on the streets.

An announcement of unusual interest was circulated by Chinese sources at a late hour when it was stated that Mr. Huang Peh-tu, Secretary to the Chinese Embassy in Tokyo, was to leave aboard the President Coolidge this morning with instructions for the Ambassador. It was thought that the instructions which Mr. Huang is carrying contained a strong demand from the Nanking Government that all Japanese troop movements in North China should cease at once.

The uncertainty of the situation was reflected in the local markets by a general fall in prices, Government bonds having dropped anywhere from $1.70 to $3.60. There was also a slacking off in the cotton exchange by $1 and $1.30, while the price of cotton cloth also registered a severe drop.

Seek “Thin Man”

A great many of the vernacular papers in Shanghai openly branded the Miyazaki case as mysterious, while one Chinese news agency insisted that the missing man had turned up at the Japanese barracks and was unharmed. An interesting sidelight on the case was given with a report that the Chinese police constable who had been on duty near the scene of the alleged kidnapping on Saturday night told his superiors that he had witnessed no disturbance.

It was also stated that Consul-General S. Okamoto had called on Mr. Stirling Fessenden asking his assistance in locating the missing bluejacket, and a report from Domei said that picked detectives were pressing a search for a “thin man” in whose hands rested the key to a solution to the Miyazaki case.

This “thin man” supplied the first report of the disappearance of Sadao Miyazaki, first-class seaman of the Japanese Naval Landing Party here, on Saturday night and the only two clues now in the hands of the naval authorities—the missing sailor’s cap and neckpiece.

Accosting three Japanese bluejackets on North Szechuen Road, the “thin man” told them he witnessed the kidnapping of Miyazaki by a group of Chinese a few minutes earlier and handed over the two clues.

Asked to go to the Landing Party’s headquarters, the man declined, explaining that his mother was sick. He gave his name as Yoshio Okazaki and his address as 85, Woosung Road. Both proved fictitious.

Study Passenger Lists

Informed that a man of “Okazaki’s” appearance arrived here from Hankow on July 24, the Japanese police made a thorough study of the passenger lists of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha for the past 12 months.

All men bearing the name of Okazaki, and aged between 20 and 40 years, have also been examined.

On a tip supplied by an informer, a Japanese residing on North Szechuen Road was summoned to the Consulate-General for a grilling on Sunday afternoon, but was shortly afterwards released.

Miss Shigeko Maeda, 24, a waitress at the Shanghai Club, Meimei Terrace, North Szechuen Road, and another unidentified person were also taken to the Consulate-General on Sunday to give testimony relating to the case.

Japanese police authorities, the local Nipponese papers reported, believe that a failure to find the “thin man” would indefinitely postpone the solution of the Miyazaki case.

Working in close co-operation with the S.M.P. and the Consular Police, the Chinese Police Bureau early on Sunday morning arrested five suspects on Yuehnai Road. Their names and occupations were given as follows by the Japanese papers: Han Tsung-chi, 35, worker, 243, Chungshing Road; Peo Li-chuan, 40, worker, 373, Liuying Road; Chu Ming-cheng, worker, 373, Liuying Road, Yu Fu-hai, 42, carpenter, Tanchiachao; Yu Pi-teh, 28, carpenter, Tanchiachao.

Cautious And Watchful

Headed by Deputy Commissioner Uyehara, of the Shanghai Municipal Police, members of the Special Political Section of the force and of the C.I.D. spent a sleepless night on Sunday trying to trace the movements of Miyazaki before the fateful hour.

The S.M.P., the Japanese papers said, are guided in their search for the “thin man” by a belief that he is not Japanese, but a Chinese or a Korean, speaking fluent Japanese.

The Dixwell Road station of the S.M.P. has become the headquarters of the officers assigned to solve the case.

Following an interview with Rear-Admiral Ohkochi, Commander of the Naval Landing Party, two officials of the Federation of Japanese Street Union Associations told the organization’s standing committee, in an emergency meeting, that the authorities desired Japanese residents here to maintain a “cautious and watchful” attitude.

Following a brief exchange of information, the members of the standing committee decided to supply each Japanese resident in the city with a description of “Okazaki.”

Authorities of the Naval Landing Party late last night emphatically denied the report, circulated by Chinese news agencies, of the return of Miyazaki to the barracks on Kiangwan Road earlier in the day.

尽管疯狂搜寻失踪水兵
虹口仍保持平静

警方据称将希望寄托于“瘦子”
以解决宫崎案；中文报纸的出现引发新一轮外逃

重视中国外交官今日离沪

由于据称被绑架的日本水兵仍然下落不明，且华北局势恶化，昨晚深夜虹口地区一片寂静。然而，关于战事重起以及宫崎案当地调查进展的消息通过中文报纸的晚版流传开来，且有某些迹象表明另一轮外逃已经开始。

许多居民悄悄地将家当装上等候着的黄包车，前往苏州河对岸的避难所。整个虹口地区，日本人喜爱的娱乐场所都安静且空无一人，街上也见不到日本人的身影。

中方消息源在深夜发布了一则备受关注的公告，称中国驻东京大使馆秘书黄伯度（音译）先生将于今天上午乘坐“柯立芝总统号”轮船离开，并携带给大使的指示。人们认为，黄先生所携带的指示中包含南京政府的一项强烈要求，即所有日军在华北的军事行动应立即停止。

局势的不确定性反映在当地市场上，价格普遍下跌，政府公债下跌了1.70至3.60美元不等。棉花交易所的交易也减少了1至1.30美元，棉布价格亦大幅下跌。

搜寻“瘦子”

上海的许多中文报纸公开称宫崎案神秘莫测，而一家中国通讯社坚持称失踪者已出现在日本兵营且安然无恙。该案的一个有趣侧面是，据报道，周六晚上在所谓绑架现场附近执勤的中国巡捕向其上级报告称，他未目睹任何骚乱。

另有消息称，总领事冈本（S. Okamoto，音译）曾拜访费森登（Stirling Fessenden）先生，请求其协助寻找失踪水兵；同盟社的报道则称，精选的侦探正在加紧搜寻一名“瘦子”，据说解开宫崎案的关键就在此人手中。

这名“瘦子”提供了关于日本海军陆战队一等水兵宫崎定夫（Sadao Miyazaki）周六晚上失踪的第一份报告，也是目前海军当局掌握的唯一两条线索——失踪水兵的帽子和领饰——的来源。

这名“瘦子”在北四川路上拦住三名日本水兵，告诉他们他几分钟前目睹了一群中国人绑架宫崎的过程，并交出了这两条线索。

当被要求前往陆战队总部时，此人予以拒绝，解释称其母亲生病。他自称名为冈崎芳雄（Yoshio Okazaki，音译），住址为吴淞路85号。后证实均为虚构。

研究乘客名单

得知一名外貌与“冈崎”相似的人于7月24日从汉口抵达上海后，日本警察彻底研究了日清汽船株式会社过去12个月的乘客名单。

所有姓冈崎且年龄在20至40岁之间的男子也都接受了审查。

根据线人提供的情报，周日下午，一名居住在北四川路的日本男子被传唤至总领事馆接受严厉讯问，但不久后即被释放。

前田茂子（Shigeko Maeda，音译）小姐，24岁，北四川路美美台（Meimei Terrace，音译）上海俱乐部的服务员，以及另一名身份不明者，也在周日被带往总领事馆，就案件相关事项作证。

据当地日文报纸报道，日本警方当局认为，若找不到这名“瘦子”，宫崎案的解决将无限期推迟。

与中国警察局密切合作，工部局警务处特别政治股和刑事侦缉处的成员在周日彻夜未眠，试图追踪宫崎在关键时刻之前的行踪。

据日文报纸称，工部局警务处在搜寻“瘦子”时秉持一种信念，即此人并非日本人，而是能说流利日语的中国人或朝鲜人。

工部局警务处狄思威路分局已成为负责侦破此案的警官们的总部。

在与海军陆战队指挥官大河内（Ohkochi，音译）少将会谈后，日本街道联合会联合会的两名官员在一次紧急会议上告诉该组织的常务委员会，当局希望在此的日本居民保持“谨慎和警惕”的态度。

经过简短的信息交流，常务委员会成员决定向市内每位日本居民提供一份关于“冈崎”的外貌描述。

昨晚深夜，海军陆战队当局坚决否认了中国通讯社散布的关于宫崎当天早些时候返回江湾路兵营的报道。

MISSING MARINE AND GLIMPSES OF SEARCH
（批：23233）
（批：8024）
（批：6 7 37）

Sadao Miyazaki is still the object of a concentrated search which is being carried on in Shanghai following his alleged abduction by a party of Chinese on Saturday night. The missing first class seaman of the Japanese Naval Landing Party is seen in the above photograph at left, while at right the searchers are shown questioning the occupants of an automobile and a ricksha in the Hongkew area. [Domei.

Hongkew Resumes Normal Aspect But Police Find No Clue Of Missing Man

Methodical Search Of Hospitals For Sick Mother Of Informer Is Fruitless; Special Patrols Are Withdrawn Following Long Vigil

REPORT OF MARTIAL LAW IS SAID BY AUTHORITIES TO BE UNFOUNDED

Hongkew began to take on a more normal appearance yesterday following the several hours' excitement which prevailed the previous evening upon the announcement that a Japanese bluejacket had been kidnapped by a party of Chinese. The special patrols of Japanese marines in full field-kit were withdrawn at an early hour in the morning, while the stand-by orders issued to the Reserve Unit and the Special Branch of the Shanghai Municipal Police were cancelled.

This was in spite of the fact that the Japanese Naval Landing Party saw fit to make an announcement to the effect that First Class Seaman Sadao Miyazaki was officially missing, an all-night search for him by the Landing Party and the police of three administrations having proven quite fruitless.

During the early hours of yesterday morning the streets of Hongkew resounded with blasts blown by Landing Party buglers, these having been sent to those areas where sailors are likely to congregate. When roll call was taken at 6 o'clock yesterday morning, Miyazaki was not in the ranks of uniformed men.

A report to the effect that the Chinese authorities had declared martial law in Chapei proved to be wholly unfounded when a careful check-up was made by representatives of "The Shanghai Times" yesterday morning, and, in addition, it was ascertained that the 300 or more Japanese marines delegated to do duty on extra-Settlement roads had been withdrawn.

Search Is Continued

During the greater part of the day, the Naval Landing Party continued its methodical search of places of amusement and other public houses in the area, and although a certain amount of tension was caused whenever one of these searching parties put in an appearance, there was no general exodus from Hongkew. At an early hour in the morning, not a few residents could be seen getting their belongings together and heading for the other side of Soochow Creek, but such activity was less in evidence as the day wore on.

Although officers of the Naval Landing Party admitted that they were working on the abduction theory, those closely connected with the case seemed to be at a loss to know in what direction to push their inquiries. Japanese naval officials continued to maintain silence on the political aspects of the disappearance, and no official communique was released for publication.

It was pointed out in a report issued by Domei that the pivot of the case yesterday morning appeared to rest in the tracing of a mysterious informer whose finding of the missing sailor's cap and neckpiece gave the first inkling of a possible abduction. This man, Japanese officials were understood to have established as the result of an all-night questioning of three Japanese sailors, was dressed in a short sleeved polo shirt, white duck trousers with a white belt, white shoes and a slouch tennis hat.

He was reported to have approached a party of three Japanese sailors at about 9.15 o'clock on Saturday night in front of a gasoline pump on the west side of North Szechuen Road across the street from the Uchiyama Magazine Store at number 1071.

Hospitals Are Checked

The three sailors were proceeding along North Szechuen Road in the direction of the Landing Party barracks. Approaching the trio from behind, the man is said to have presented the cap and neckpiece, saying that he had found them on Dixwell Road where "a Japanese sailor had been abducted and whisked away in a motor car."

Kakushi Yanagida, seaman first class, immediately crossed the street to telephone from the Uchiyama Magazine Store to Naval Landing Party Headquarters. His two companions, Yoshiji Kuramasu and Tokusaburo Morimoto, remained on the sidewalk with the informer.

When they asked him to proceed with them at once to the Landing Party Headquarters, he was stated to have refused, claiming that he

《字林西报》，1937年7月26日，星期一
失踪水兵及搜寻一瞥
（批：23233）
（批：8024）
（批：6 7 37）

宫崎定夫仍然是上海集中搜寻的对象，此前他据称于周六晚被一群中国人绑架。上图左侧为失踪的日本海军陆战队一等水兵，右侧显示搜寻者在虹口地区询问一辆汽车和一辆黄包车上的人员。[同盟社]

虹口恢复常态但警方未发现失踪者线索

对线报人病母的医院进行系统性搜寻无果；长时间警戒后特别巡逻队撤离

当局称戒严令报道毫无根据

继前一晚因宣布一名日本水兵被一群中国人绑架而引发数小时骚动后，虹口昨日开始呈现出更为正常的景象。清晨时分，身着全套野战装备的日本海军陆战队特别巡逻队被撤回，同时发给工部局警务处后备队和特别分支的待命命令也被取消。

尽管如此，日本海军陆战队认为有必要发布公告，正式宣布一等水兵宫崎定夫失踪，陆战队及三方警政机构整夜的搜寻均一无所获。

昨日凌晨，虹口的街道上回荡着陆战队号手吹奏的号角声，这些号手被派往水兵可能聚集的区域。昨日早上6点点名时，宫崎不在制服人员队伍中。

《字林西报》代表昨日早晨经仔细核查，证实有关中国当局在闸北宣布戒严的报道完全毫无根据，此外还查明，被指派在租界以外道路执勤的300多名日本海军陆战队员已被撤回。

搜寻仍在继续

白天大部分时间里，海军陆战队继续对该地区的娱乐场所和其他公共场所进行系统性搜寻，虽然每当这些搜寻队出现时都会引起一定程度的紧张，但虹口并未发生大规模外逃。清晨时分，可以看到不少居民收拾行李前往苏州河对岸，但随着一天时间的推移，此类活动逐渐减少。

虽然海军陆战队军官承认他们正依据绑架理论开展工作，但与案件密切相关的人士似乎对调查方向感到困惑。日本海军官员继续对失踪事件的政治方面保持沉默，未发布任何官方公报供发表。

同盟社发布的一份报告指出，昨日上午案件的关键似乎在于追踪一名神秘的线人，正是他发现了失踪水兵的帽子和领饰，从而首次透露出可能发生绑架的迹象。据了解，日本官员通过对三名日本水兵整夜的讯问，确定此人身穿短袖马球衫、白色斜纹布长裤配白色腰带、白鞋和一顶软边网球帽。

据报道，周六晚上约9点15分，此人在北四川路西侧一个汽油泵前接近一组三名日本水兵，对面是1071号内山书店。

这三名水兵正沿着北四川路向陆战队兵营方向行进。据说此人从后方接近这三人，出示了帽子和领饰，称他在狄思威路发现了这些东西，当时“一名日本水兵被绑架并被一辆汽车迅速带走”。

一等水兵柳田角石（Kakushi Yanagida，音译）立即穿过马路，从内山书店打电话给海军陆战队总部。他的两名同伴，藏间义次（Yoshiji Kuramasu，音译）和森本德三郎（Tokusaburo Morimoto，音译），则与线人一起留在人行道上。

当他们要求他立即随他们前往陆战队总部时，据说他予以拒绝，声称其

不得不赶回家，因为他的母亲“病危”。在乘坐人力车之前，他自称名为冈崎义雄（Yoshio Okazaki），地址为吴淞路85号，但经调查证实，这两者均为虚构。

当这一情况被发现后，警方立即开始讯问人力车夫，试图寻找线索，同时领事警察走访了所有日本医院。医生被要求提供病危女性患者的姓名。

据称，这名失踪的水兵年仅21岁，于去年5月19日从吴海军陆战队抵达上海。登陆部队军官形容他习惯安静，记录良好，最近曾向家里汇款25日元，约占其月薪的三分之二。

他和几名同伴在东亚大戏院（Toa Theatre）观看了一场下午场演出，随后于6时30分在虹口大戏院前与同伴分手。他的记录显示，他曾在7月8日和12日“外宿”，当时他住在米勒路400号的日本海军士兵俱乐部，次日早晨返回兵营。

谜团加深

据同盟社报道，随着一名身份不明的线人首次拿出证明事态有异的唯一确凿证据至今已过去24小时，围绕宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki）失踪案的谜团昨晚进一步加深。

该线人在自愿提供一名日本水兵被绑架的信息后便消失不见，尽管三家警察机构、日本宪兵队和登陆部队 efforts 搜寻，但其行踪仍未查明。

昨晚，在海军登陆部队兵营内设立了一个临时总部，作为汇总各机构所获信息的中心。登陆部队、日本宪兵队、日本领事警察和上海公共租界工部局警务处均派代表参加。

该联合小组与中国警察局保持着密切合作。

后者致力于遏制闸北地区重新出现的逃离倾向。“难民”们在白昼时分尚属稀少，但在日落时分开始涌入租界。

日本总领事冈本末政先生昨晨拜访大上海代市长俞鸿钧先生，请求中国当局协助追查失踪水兵。

据悉，这位中国官员在同意命令其下属机构协助搜寻的同时，要求冈本先生减少日军军事活动，因为后者有引起中国民众恐慌的倾向。
