THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JULY 26, 1937
Nipponese Marine
Still Lost; Patrols
Called In; City Quiet

Search Fails To Locate
Missing Man Said
Kidnaped

SLIM EVIDENCE
BEING PROBED

Acting Mayor Expresses
Regret Over Hasty
Japanese Moves

While the mystery of the alleged disappearance of a Japanese bluejacket continued last night to baffle Chinese, Japanese and Settlement police investigators, tension, which gripped Shanghai's northern areas for nearly 10 hours as a result of the military display of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, began to subside by daybreak yesterday.

The exodus of terrified Chinese residents from Chapel, however, continued all day yesterday despite the withdrawal of the Japanese armed patrols shortly after 5 o'clock yesterday morning.

First Class Seaman Sadao Miyazaki, whose alleged disappearance Saturday night caused the Naval Landing Party to send heavy armed patrols into Chapel, was yesterday officially listed as "missing" by the Nipponese naval authorities.

Kidnaping Is Theory

Despite exhaustive investigation conducted since Saturday night by Settlement and Chinese police as well as the Japanese consulate and naval authorities, the original story that Miyazaki was "kidnaped" near the corner of North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads remained a theory, unsupported by any tangible fact.

Japanese consular and naval investigators continued last night to trace the identity of one Japanese civilian, who vanished after volunteering the information that he eyewitnessed the "abduction." The informant gave a false name and address.

The assurance that the Japanese do not desire to aggravate the situation arising out of incident was given yesterday morning by Mr. S. Okamoto, Japanese Consul-General, to Mr. O. K. Yui, Acting Mayor, during an interview at the City Government Building, Civic Center, at 11.30 a.m.

Mr. Okamoto expressed the appreciation for the assistance given by the Chinese authorities in investigating the case. After briefly relating the incident and the subsequent tense situation Saturday night, the Japanese Consul-General also informed Mr. Yui that Naval Landing Party units had been withdrawn from Chinese areas early yesterday morning.

Yui Regrets Rush Action

Replying, Mr. Yui expressed his deep regrets over the unwarranted activities of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, which sent patrols in full war kits into the Chinese territory even before any thorough investigation had been made into the alleged disappearance.

Disastrous consequences, Mr. Yui said, were only averted Saturday by the careful and cool-headed manner with which the Chinese police and City Government officials handled the situation. He expressed the hope that in the future the Japanese Naval Landing authorities would exercise greater consideration in order to avoid any similar disturbance of the peace and order of the city.

During the interview, Mr. Yui also informed the Japanese Consul-General that immediately after the report of a Japanese bluejacket was "missing," the Chinese authorities sent out investigators to probe the case with the Settlement police. Several points which led to suspicion were discovered Saturday night such as the fictitious name and address given by the Japanese informant, Y. Okazaki, who claimed that he was the only witness to the alleged abduction.

The fact that no other witness was to be found appeared to be unbelievable, Mr. Yui remarked. The place where the incident allegedly took place is one of the busiest sections of the northern district, Mr. Yui pointed out.

Areas Quiet

Meantime Hongkew and Chapel at midnight last night were quiet at least on the surface. An undercurrent of tension, however, was still in existence among the residents of the area.

The majority of the Japanese Naval Landing Party patrols were withdrawn from Chapel, about 500 yards north of the Woosung-Shanghai railway tracks, at about 5 o'clock. A small group of about 30 men remained, however, around the vicinity of the Japanese cemetery in Chapel and there was no report that it had been withdrawn up to late last night.

On North Szechuen, Dixwell, Haining Roads and other Hongkew streets, the military activities of the Landing Party ceased by dawn yesterday. Military trucks and armed patrols which cruised the district had disappeared from the Settlement and extra-Settlement streets when a CHINA PRESS reporter returned from a tour of the area at 5 o'clock.

Up until that time, Japanese bluejackets with bayoneted rifles were stopping all cars, pedestrians and rickshas on practically all Settlement and extra-Settlement roads north of Wanpang Bridge. From that point northward, Japanese bluejackets were overrunning the entire Hongkew area.

Residents Frightened

Across the railroad tracks, on the Chapel side, some 150 to 200 Japanese bluejackets were posted along the roads as far as the Wanpang Creek. On main roads leading into the Settlement, machine guns and parties of 10 to 15 men were stationed.

The martial display of the Japanese caused an immediate stampede of frightened Chapel residents who up to late last night were still moving out from the area in cars, on foot and on rickshas with their trunks, furniture and other movable belongings. A steady stream of evacuees entered into the Settlement all day yesterday. The largest crowd gathered on Peiping Road, near North Station, and jammed the entrance to North Honan Road.

The pivot of the case yesterday morning appeared to rest in the tracing of the mysterious informer, whose finding of the missing sailor's cap and uniform neckpiece gave the first inkling of a possible abduction.

This man, Japanese officials were understood to have established as a result of an all-night questioning of three Japanese sailors, was dressed in a short-sleeved polo shirt, white duck trousers with a white belt, white shoes and a slough tennis hat.

He was reported to have approached a party of three Japanese sailors at about 9:15 o'clock Saturday night in front of a gasoline pump on the western side of North Szechuen Road across the street from the Uchiyama Magazine Store at No. 1071.

Hurried Away

The three sailors were proceeding along N. Szechuen Road in the direction of the Landing Party barracks.

Approaching the trio, assertedly from behind, the man is stated to have presented the cap and the neckpiece, saying that he had found them on Dixwell Road where "a Japanese sailor" had been "abducted and whisked away in a motor car."

When the two bluejackets asked the informant to proceed with them at once to the Landing Party headquarters, he was stated to have refused, claiming that he had to hurry home where his mother was "dangerously ill". Before boarding a ricsha he gave his name as Yoshio Okazaki and his address as 85 Woosung Road. Both proved fictitious.

When this was discovered, the police immediately began questioning ricsha pullers in an attempt to find a clue. Simultaneously, all Japanese hospitals were visited by the Consular Police, while doctors were requested to furnish the names of female patients who were critically ill. These activities had produced no results by noon.

Miyazaki, 21 years old, arrived in Shanghai on May 19, from the Kure Marine Corps. He was described by officers at the Landing Party as "a quiet fellow" with a good record.

On Saturday afternoon he attended an afternoon show at the Towa Theater, following which he separated from his companions in front of the Hongkew Theater at 6:30 o'clock.

Had "Slept Out"

His record showed that he had "slept out" on July 8 and 12, when he stayed at the Japanese Naval Soldier's Club, 400 Miller Road, returning to the barracks the following morning.

When roll-call was taken at 6 o'clock yesterday morning, when overnight liberty for Japanese marines ends, Miyazaki's name alone remained unanswered.

This extra precaution was taken by the Landing Party authorities, a Japanese naval spokesman said, to forestall the possibility of Miyazaki having failed to hear the "assembly" bugle call rang out in Hongkew Saturday night. Buglers were sent out of trucks to blow their call in all areas where sailors are likely to congregate.

In addition, all Japanese establishments frequented by sailors were searched during the night by parties led by officers, the spokesman stated.

《字林西报》，1937年7月26日，星期一
日本水兵
依然失踪；巡逻队
被召回；城市平静

搜寻未能找到
据称被绑架的
失踪者

证据薄弱
正在调查中

代市长对日本
仓促行动表示遗憾

尽管昨晚 alleged 一名日本普通水兵失踪的谜团仍令中国、日本及租界警方调查人员困惑不解，但因日本海军登陆部队展示武力而笼罩上海北部地区近10小时的紧张局势，已于昨日黎明时分开始缓和。

然而，尽管日本武装巡逻队于昨日清晨5时许撤离，惊恐的中国居民从闸北（Chapel，原文误拼，应为Chapei）逃离的现象昨日全天仍在持续。

一等水兵宫崎贞雄，其周六晚间的 alleged 失踪导致海军登陆部队派遣重武装巡逻队进入闸北，昨日被日本海军当局正式列为“失踪”。

绑架仅为推测

尽管自周六晚间以来，租界和中国警察以及日本领事馆和海军当局进行了详尽调查，但最初关于宫崎在北四川路与狄思威路拐角附近被“绑架”的说法仍仅为一种推测，没有任何确凿事实支持。

日本领事和海军调查人员昨晚继续追查一名日本平民的身份，该平民在自愿提供信息称其目击了“绑架”事件后便消失无踪。该线人提供了虚假的姓名和地址。

日本总领事冈本S.先生昨日上午11时30分在市中心市政府大楼会见代市长俞鸿钧先生时保证，日本方面不希望加剧因该事件引发的局势。

冈本先生对中国当局在调查此案中提供的协助表示感谢。在简要叙述了该事件及随后周六晚间的紧张局势后，日本总领事还告知俞先生，海军登陆部队各单位已于昨日清晨撤出中国区域。

俞氏对仓促行动表示遗憾

俞先生在答复中对日本海军登陆部队毫无根据的活动深表遗憾，该部队在对 alleged 失踪事件进行任何彻底调查之前，就派遣全副战备的巡逻队进入中国领土。

俞先生称，周六之所以避免了灾难性后果，全靠中国警察和市政府官员以谨慎冷静的态度处理局势。他表示希望日本海军登陆部队当局今后能更加体谅，以避免类似扰乱城市和平与秩序的事件再次发生。

会谈期间，俞先生还告知日本总领事，在接到一名日本水兵“失踪”的报告后，中国当局立即派出调查人员与租界警察共同调查此案。周六晚间发现了一些引起怀疑的点，例如日本线人Y.冈崎提供的虚假姓名和地址，此人声称自己是 alleged 绑架事件的唯一目击者。

俞先生指出，找不到其他目击者这一事实似乎令人难以置信。他指出，alleged 事件发生的地点是北区最繁忙的地段之一。

区域平静

与此同时，昨晚午夜时分，虹口和闸北至少在表面上恢复了平静。然而，该地区居民中仍存在一股紧张的暗流。

约在5点钟，大部分日本海军登陆部队巡逻队从位于吴淞-上海铁路轨道以北约500码处的闸北撤离。然而，一小群约30人的队伍仍留在闸北日本公墓附近，直到昨晚深夜尚无撤回报告。

在北四川路、狄思威路、海宁路及其他虹口街道，登陆部队的军事活动于昨日黎明时分停止。当《字林西报》记者于5点钟结束对该区域的巡视返回时，在该区域巡航的军用卡车和武装巡逻队已从租界内及租界外的街道上消失。

直到那时，持带刺刀步枪的日本水兵仍在万邦桥以北的几乎所有租界内及租界外道路上拦截所有汽车、行人和人力车。从该点向北，日本水兵遍布整个虹口地区。

居民受惊

在铁轨另一侧的闸北一边，约有150至200名日本水兵沿道路部署至万邦浜。在通往租界的主要道路上，驻扎有机枪队和10至15人的小队。

日本的武力展示导致惊恐的闸北居民立即奔逃，直到昨晚深夜，他们仍带着行李箱、家具和其他可移动财物，乘汽车、步行或坐人力车离开该地区。昨日全天，撤离者源源不断地进入租界。最大的人群聚集在北站附近的北平路上，堵塞了河南北路的入口。

昨日早晨，案件的关键似乎在于追踪那名神秘的线人，他发现了失踪水兵的帽子和制服领饰，从而首次透露出可能发生绑架的线索。

据了解，日本官员通过对三名日本水兵进行通宵讯问，确定此人身穿短袖马球衫、白色斜纹布长裤配白色腰带、白鞋和一顶软呢网球帽。

据报道，周六晚间约9时15分，他在北四川路西侧的一个汽油泵前接近了一组三名日本水兵，对面是北四川路1071号的内山书店。

匆匆离去

这三名水兵正沿着北四川路朝登陆部队兵营方向行进。

据称，该男子从后方接近这三人，出示了帽子和领饰，称他在狄思威路发现了这些物品，那里有一名“日本水兵”被“绑架并用汽车带走”。

当两名水兵要求线人立即随他们前往登陆部队总部时，据称他拒绝了，声称必须赶回家，因为他的母亲“病危”。在登上人力车之前，他自称名为冈崎义雄，地址为吴淞路85号。后经证实，两者均为虚构。

当这一情况被发现后，警方立即开始讯问人力车夫，试图寻找线索。与此同时，领事警察走访了所有日本医院，并要求医生提供病危女性患者的姓名。截至中午，这些行动均未产生结果。

宫崎，21岁，于5月19日从吴海军陆战队抵达上海。登陆部队军官形容他为“一个安静的人”，记录良好。

周六下午，他在东亚大戏院（Towa Theater）观看了一场下午场演出，随后于6时30分在虹口大戏院前与同伴分手。

曾“外宿”

他的记录显示，他曾在7月8日和12日“外宿”，当时他住在米勒路400号的日本海军士兵俱乐部，次日早晨返回兵营。

昨日早晨6点点名时，即日本海军陆战队队员夜间外出许可结束之时，只有宫崎的名字无人应答。

一位日本海军发言人称，登陆部队当局采取这一额外预防措施，是为了防止宫崎可能未听到周六晚间在虹口响起的“集合”号角声。号手被派出卡车，在水兵可能聚集的所有区域吹奏号角。

此外，该发言人称，夜间由军官带领的小队搜查了水兵常去的所有日本场所。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, JULY 26, 1937

Japanese Consul-General In
Interview With O. K. Yui

Consul-General Okamoto Tells Acting Mayor It
Is Not Japan's Desire To Aggravate The
Situation Arising From Incident

Japan's desire not to aggravate the situation, arising from the alleged disappearance of a Japanese marine was conveyed by Mr. S. Okamoto, Japanese Consul-General, in an interview with Mr. O. K. Yui, Acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, at 11.30 o'clock yesterday morning.

Mr. Okamoto also expressed appreciation to Mr. Yui for the assistance of the Greater Shanghai authorities in investigating the circumstances surrounding the missing of Sadao Miyazaki.

After briefly relating the situation arising from Saturday night's incident, the Japanese Consul-General also informed Mr. Yui of the withdrawal of the Naval Landing Party units from the Chinese area early in the morning.

In reply, Mr. Yui stated that immediately following receipt of reports of the incident, Chinese police authorities sent out men to co-operate with the S.M.C. police in launching investigations.

Several suspicious points, Mr. Yui said, were discovered, such as the fictitious address of the informant Y. Okazaki, who alleged he was the only one to have seen the abduction of the Japanese marine.

Expresses Disapproval

No other witnesses of the abduction, Mr. Yui told Mr. Okamoto, were stated to have been found, which seemed to be unbelievable, because the incident was said to have occurred long before midnight and the scene of the incident was known to be a busy section.

However, Mr. Yui expressed deep regret over the unwarranted activities of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, which sent out fully-equipped patrols to territory outside of the International Settlement even before they had made any investigations into the incident.

Mr. Yui expressed the hope that, in the future, the Japanese Naval Landing Party should exercise greater consideration in order to avoid misunderstanding.

As to Chinese assistance in investigating the case, Mr. Yui said it was natural because it was part of the duties of the Chinese police to do so.

The interview lasted for over half an hour.—Central News.

《字林西报》，1937年7月26日，星期一

日本总领事
会见俞鸿钧

总领事冈本告诉代理市长，
日本无意加剧因该事件而引发的局势

昨日上午11时30分，日本总领事冈本S.先生（Mr. S. Okamoto）在与大上海特别市代理市长俞鸿钧先生（Mr. O. K. Yui）的会晤中传达称，针对据称一名日本海军陆战队士兵失踪一事所引发的局势，日本方面希望不予加剧。

冈本先生还对俞先生表示感谢，感谢大上海当局在调查宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）失踪情况过程中提供的协助。

日本总领事在简要叙述了周六晚间事件引发的局势后，还告知俞先生，海军陆战队分队已于清晨撤出华界区域。

俞先生回答说，在接到事件报告后，中国警方当局立即派出人员，与工部局警务处（S.M.C. police）合作展开调查。

俞先生称，发现了几处可疑之处，例如报案人Y. Okazaki（音译）的地址是虚构的，此人声称他是唯一目睹该日本海军陆战队士兵被绑架的人。

表示不满

俞先生告诉冈本先生，据称未发现该绑架案的其他证人，这似乎令人难以置信，因为据说事件发生在午夜之前很久，且事发地点已知为繁华地段。

然而，俞先生对日本海军陆战队毫无理由的行动深表遗憾，该部队在未对事件进行任何调查之前，就向公共租界以外的地区派出了全副武装的巡逻队。

俞先生表示希望日本海军陆战队今后能更加审慎行事，以避免误解。

关于中方协助调查此案一事，俞先生表示这是理所当然的，因为这是中国警方的职责所在。

会晤持续了半个多小时。——中央通讯社。

STEPS TO PREVENT
COMMOTION

Naval Authorities Of
Japan In Shanghai
On Qui Vive

NEEDLESS POTHER TO
BE CHECKMATED
TOKYO, July 25.—"Strong efforts"
to prevent unnecessary commotion
are being made by the Japanese
naval authorities in Shanghai, a
communique issued by the Navy
Ministry at 11 o'clock this morning
said.
The investigations into the dis-
appearance of Seaman Sadao Miya-
zaki; the announcement added, were
being continued.
In view of the "complicated con-
ditions" prevailing in Shanghai, the
communique went on, endeavours
were being made to "learn the facts
and ascertain the circumstances" of
the affair.
"The most suitable measures" to
deal with the situation will be taken
after the facts in the case are deter-
mined, the communique said.
The disappearance of the sailor was
announced in a communique issued
by the Navy Ministry at 3 o'clock
this morning.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party
in Shanghai, the announcement said,
had taken precautionary measures
following the receipt of information
from a resident that First Class Sea-
man Miyazaki had been abducted by
Chinese near the intersection of
North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads
at about 9 o'clock last night.
Investigations to ascertain the
facts of the case were being made
by the Landing Party in co-operation
with the Chinese Police Bureau and
the Shanghai Municipal Police, the
announcement added.—Domei.

Circumspect Procedure
TOKYO, July 25.—Admiral Mis-
tumasa Yonai, Minister of the Navy,
this noon obtained the approval of
the Cabinet to his policy of "pro-
ceeding with circumspection" in
dealing with the disappearance of
a Japanese sailor in Shanghai.
The assent of other ministers was
given at an informal meeting of the
Cabinet at the official residence of
the Premier, Prince Fumimaro
Konoye, held after a luncheon
given following the opening cere-
mony of the 71st session of the
Diet.
General Gen Sugiyama, Min-
ister of War, made a report on
the situation in North China, point-
ing out that the slow evacuation
of the vicinity of Peiping did not
warrant optimism at this time.—
Domei.

谈判。

防止
骚乱的步骤

驻沪日本
海军当局
保持警惕

不必要的喧嚣
将被遏制

东京，7月25日电。——海军省今晨11时发布的公报称，驻沪日本海军当局正在做出“大力努力”，以防止不必要的骚乱。

公报补充说，对水兵宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）失踪案的调查正在进行中。

公报接着指出，鉴于上海 prevailing 的“复杂状况”，各方正努力“查明事实并弄清”该事件的“情况”。

公报称，在确定案件事实后，将采取“最适当的措施”来应对局势。

海军省在今晨3时发布的公报中宣布了这名水兵的失踪消息。

公告称，驻沪日本海军陆战队在收到一名居民提供的信息后采取了预防措施，该信息称一等水兵宫崎昨晚9时许在北四川路与狄思威路（Dixwell Road）交叉口附近被中国人绑架。

公告补充说，陆战队正与中国警察局和工部局警务处合作，调查以查明案件事实。——同盟社。

谨慎的程序

东京，7月25日电。——海军大臣米内光政（Mistumasa Yonai，音译）海军上将今日中午获得内阁对其在处理上海一名日本水兵失踪事件中采取“谨慎行事”政策的批准。

其他大臣的同意是在首相近卫文麿亲王（Prince Fumimaro Konoye）官邸举行的非正式内阁会议上给出的，该会议是在第71届帝国议会开幕式后的午宴之后举行的。

陆军大臣杉山元（Gen Sugiyama）将军报告了华北局势，指出北平周边地区的缓慢撤离表明目前不宜乐观。——同盟社。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JULY 25, 1937
232>1

TENSION BREAKS HONGKEW CALM
AS JAPANESE MARINES MOBILIZE
IN SEARCH OF "MISSING" SAILOR

All Roads
In Hongkew
Are Guarded

Area Disturbed In Spite
Of Orderly Movements
By Japanese Troops

Surface calm prevailing in
Hongkew since the start of the
Lukouchiao Incident in the
north on July 9 was rudely
broken last night with the
reported kidnapping of a
Japanese seaman, by a group of
Chinese, following an alleged
quarrel on North Szechuen
Road, near the corner of
Dixwell Road.

Before the reports of the actual
kidnapping and the alleged "whisk-
ing away" in a motor car could be
confirmed, denied, or checked up
by the cancellation of all leave by
the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
patrols of marines in full field-ser-
vice marching order were im-
mediately sent out over the major
portion of the Hongkew district
north of Range Road.

Truck after truck filled with
armed marines left the Landing
Party Barracks on Kiangwan Road
as soon as they were assembled
and patrols were immediately post-
ed all along North Szechuen Road
right up to Wan Pan Chiao (Bridge)
and along Dixwell Road almost to
Kashing Road.

Marines stopped motor cars, tram-
cars and omnibuses at almost every
corner and subjected the occupants
of the vehicles to a search. The
marines on stopping the double
decker omnibuses, immediately
mounted to the second deck carry-
ing their rifles, with fixed bayonets,
with them and searching all Chin-
ese male passengers.

The motor car in which two
representatives of "The Shanghai
Sunday Times" were touring the
Hongkew area at about midnight
was stopped by marines on Dixwell
Road not far from the Kashing
Road Bridge. A youthful marine
made the occupants rise from
their seats, while he felt super-
ficially over the seat covering.

Apparently not wishing to create
any undue disturbance and uneasi-
ness until it was definitely ascer-
tained that a sailor had been kid-
napped, the patrolling of the
streets and dispatch of troops was
carried out in perfect order.

Nevertheless the rush of armed
troops at midnight, the clatter of
motorcycle patrols over the area and
the activities of the Japanese photo-
graphers in setting off flares in order
that numerous pictures at once could
be taken of the movements of the
marines around the barracks and
the Japanese school on North Sze-
chuen Road, where a temporary
sub-headquarters was established,
all combined to create uneasiness in
the district.

Officers of the Chinese Police
Bureau attached to the stations
bordering the Hongkew area, kept
on patrol as usual, no special
measures having been taken until
midnight. High officers of the
Bureau called at the Naval Landing
Party Barracks shortly before mid-
night in order to obtain information
on the situation.

No extra patrols were put on the
street by the Dixwell Road Police
Station, the whole incident being
left mainly in the hands of the
Japanese authorities, who continued
as time progressed to comb the dis-
trict more and more.

A report of the alleged kidnap-
ping was made to the Shanghai
Municipal Police, all high officers
were informed, but up to an early
hour this morning, no development
was recorded.

(印：S. L. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 8024 Date 27 7 37)

District Is
Patrolled By
Armed Groups

Seaman Said "Whisked
Away" After Quarrel
With Chinese Group

CONFLICTING REPORTS
ON "INCIDENT"

Hongkew district was thrown
into a state of tension last
night as it was reported that,
following a quarrel on North
Szechuen Road near Dixwell
Road, a Japanese sailor had
allegedly been kidnapped by
several Chinese and "whisked
away" in a motor car. The
Japanese Naval Landing Party
was mobilized and marines
were sent out to patrol the
Hongkew district, north of
Range Road.

Excitement reigned in the area
while intensive investigations were
being conducted to ascertain whe-
ther or not a kidnapping had ac-
tually taken place, as reported by
a Japanese civilian, who since mak-
ing the first report at about 9.20
p.m. was reported to have disappear-
ed.

The latest "incident" began when
a Japanese civilian, wearing a white
tennis cap and white duck trousers,
walked up to a bluejacket named
Yamagita and reported that he had
just witnessed a quarrel between a
Japanese sailor or sailors, and a
number of Chinese and that he saw
a sailor pushed into a motor car by
the Chinese and "whisked away."
He stated that the fracas took place
on North Szechuen Road near the
corner of Dixwell Road, according
to an official statement released last
night.

The sailor and the civilian im-
mediately walked into the Uchiyama
bookstore off North Szechuen Road,
where the sailor passed on the in-
formation to the Naval Landing
Party headquarters by telephone.

The civilian, who gave his name
as Yoshio Okasaki and his address as
8 Woosung Road, then left im-
mediately, and it was ascertained at
midnight, according to the Domei
News Agency, that both the name
and the address were found to be
fictitious.

Patrols Sent Out

As soon as the first report of the
alleged kidnapping was received
by the Naval Landing Party head-
quarters, a general alarm was sent
out and all available marines were
rushed out in armed patrols
throughout the district.

Conflicting reports flew around the
district and even in high official
circles. The first report available
at Dixwell Road Police Station was
that there had been a fight between
Japanese sailors, or marines, and a
group of Chinese. A subsequent re-
port, from Japanese quarters, was to

《上海星期日报》，1937年7月25日
232>1

随着日本海军陆战队动员搜寻“失踪”水兵，
虹口的平静被紧张气氛打破

虹口所有道路
均受守卫

尽管日军行动有序，
该地区仍受扰动

自7月9日北方卢沟桥事变爆发以来，虹口地区表面一直维持平静，但昨晚这一平静被粗暴打破，据报道，一名日本水手在北四川路靠近狄思威路（Dixwell Road）拐角处发生 alleged 争吵后，被一群中国人绑架。

在实际绑架和 alleged “驾车带走”的报告得到证实、否认或通过日本海军陆战队取消所有休假来进行核查之前，全副野战行军装备的海军陆战队巡逻队已立即出动，覆盖了兰路（Range Road）以北虹口区的大部分区域。

一辆辆载满武装海军陆战队员的卡车在集结完毕后立即从江湾路（Kiangwan Road）的海军陆战队营房出发，巡逻队随即部署在北四川路沿线，直至万板桥（Wan Pan Chiao），以及沿狄思威路几乎延伸至嘉善路（Kashing Road）。

海军陆战队员在几乎每个路口拦停汽车、电车和公共汽车，并对车内乘客进行搜查。在拦停双层公共汽车时，海军陆战队员立即携带装有刺刀的步枪登上二层，搜查所有男性中国乘客。

《上海星期日报》的两名代表大约在午夜时分乘车巡视虹口地区时，他们的汽车在离嘉善路桥不远的狄思威路上被海军陆战队员拦下。一名年轻的海军陆战队员让车内人员从座位上起身，同时他 superficially 摸索了座椅套。

显然，在确切查明有水兵被绑架之前，不希望造成任何过度的动荡和不安，因此街道巡逻和部队派遣均井然有序地进行。

尽管如此，午夜时分武装部队的匆忙出动、摩托车巡逻队在该地区发出的嘈杂声，以及日本摄影师为了能够一次性拍摄大量照片而在海军陆战队营房周围及北四川路的日本学校（此处设立了临时分指挥部）附近点燃闪光弹的活动，共同造成了该地区的不安情绪。

隶属于虹口地区周边各派出所的中国警察局警官像往常一样继续巡逻，直到午夜前未采取任何特殊措施。该局的高级官员在午夜前不久前往海军陆战队营房，以获取有关局势的信息。

狄思威路警察局未在街头增派巡逻队，整个事件主要交由日本当局处理，随着时间的推移，他们继续对该地区进行越来越细致的搜捕。

有关 alleged 绑架的报告已提交给工部局警务处，所有高级官员均已获知，但直到今天凌晨早些时候，尚无进展记录。

（印：S. L. 登记号 S. B. D. 8024 日期 37年7月27日）

该地区由
武装小组
巡逻

据称水兵在与
一群中国人争吵后
被“带走”

关于“事件”的
相互矛盾的报告

昨晚，虹口区陷入紧张状态，据报道，在北四川路靠近狄思威路处发生争吵后，一名日本水手 allegedly 被几名中国人绑架并“驾车带走”。日本海军陆战队被动员起来，派出海军陆战队员巡逻兰路（Range Road）以北的虹口区。

当 intensive 调查正在进行以确定是否真的发生了如一名日本平民所报告的绑架案时，该地区弥漫着兴奋情绪，该名平民在晚上9点20分左右做出首次报告后，据报已失踪。

最新的“事件”始于一名头戴白色网球帽、身穿白色斜纹布裤子的日本平民走向一名名叫 Yamagita（音译）的水手，并报告说他刚刚目睹了一名或几名日本水手与数名中国人之间的争吵，并且看到一名水手被中国人推入一辆汽车并“带走”。根据昨晚发布的官方声明，他表示冲突发生在北四川路靠近狄思威路拐角处。

该水手和平民立即走进北四川路旁的内山书店，水手通过电话将信息传递给海军陆战队总部。

这名自称名为 Yoshio Okasaki（音译）、地址为吴淞路8号的平民随后立即离开，据同盟社报道，在午夜时查明，其姓名和地址均为虚构。

派出巡逻队

海军陆战队总部一收到有关 alleged 绑架的首份报告，便发出全面警报，所有可用的海军陆战队员均以武装巡逻队的形式迅速派往全区。

相互矛盾的报告在该地区甚至在高层官方圈子里流传。狄思威路警察局收到的第一份报告称，日本水手或海军陆战队员与一群中国人之间发生了斗殴。随后来自日本方面的报告则称，一名水手已被

It was reported that the authorities are in possession of the cap and neckpiece of the missing man, whose name is given as Sadao Miyazaki, First Class Seaman, according to a Domei News Agency report.
It could not be ascertained last night whether this had been confirmed. A spokesman of the Press Information Officer of the Japanese Naval Landing Party was not in a position to give out any definite statement on the alleged kidnapping, when interviewed by a representative of "The Shanghai Sunday Times" at the barracks.
Asked for an official report, the spokesman answered that higher officers were investigating. Asked whether the Japanese authorities were convinced that there was a fight or some sort of altercation between Japanese bluejackets and some Chinese, he answered that it had been reported in that manner.
"Is a bluejacket missing?"
"We are investigating the matter," he replied.
"Is it not true that under a recent order issued by the commanding officer of the Landing Party, no marines or sailors are allowed to go on liberty except in parties of threes?"
"That is true."
Japanese Check-Up
"Then if the order was carried out, there should have been two sailors who witnessed the alleged kidnapping?"
"Logically correct," answered the spokesman.
"Were there two other men present, or one other man, or was the kidnapped man alone?"
"We do not know, we are checking; please come to-morrow morning, when we can give you more correct information," was the rejoinder.
"Then it has not been ascertained definitely that the kidnapping actually took place?"
"The press officer is not here. He is making inquiries. I cannot say."
"In the meantime general precautions are being taken?"
"Yes, you can see"—pointed to the parties of Marines.
Search Being Made
A thorough search was being carried on in the early hours of this morning for the missing man in Hongkew and Chapei areas, the Japanese authorities receiving full co-operation from the Chinese Bureau of Police, the Shanghai-Woosung Garrison Headquarters and the Special Political Section of the S.M.P.
Domei reported that Consul-General Suemasa Okamoto called on Lieutenant Commander Matao Okino, Assistant Naval Attache, at the office on Dixwell Road, at 11.30 p.m. and remained closeted in conference after midnight.
Late at night, the Landing Party seized a suspicious Chinese carrying a revolver.
Taken to the headquarters of the Landing Party, he said that he was a detective of the Chinese Bureau of Police and that earlier in the day he was detailed to guard a payroll. Satisfied with his explanation, the Landing Party authorities released him, Domei News Agency reported.

据同盟社报道，当局已掌握失踪者的帽子和领饰，该失踪者名为宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki），一等水兵。

昨晚尚无法证实此消息是否属实。《上海星期泰晤士报》（The Shanghai Sunday Times）的一名代表在兵营采访日本海军陆战队新闻发言人时，该发言人表示无法就所谓的绑架事件发表任何确切声明。

当被要求提供官方报告时，该发言人回答说高级军官正在调查。当被问及日本当局是否确信日本水兵与某些中国人之间发生了打斗或某种争执时，他回答说收到的报告是这样描述的。

“有一名水兵失踪吗？”

“我们正在调查此事，”他回答道。

“根据陆战队指挥官最近发布的一项命令，除非三人成群，否则海军陆战队员或水兵不得外出休假，这难道不是真的吗？”

“是真的。”

日方核查

“那么如果命令得到执行，应该会有两名水兵目击了所谓的绑架？”

“逻辑上正确，”发言人回答。

“当时还有另外两人在场，还是只有一人，或者被绑架者是独自一人？”

“我们不知道，我们正在核查；请明天早上再来，届时我们可以提供更准确的信息，”这是他的回应。

“那么尚未确定绑架确实发生了吗？”

“新闻官不在这里。他正在进行查询。我不能说。”

“与此同时，正在采取一般性的预防措施吗？”

“是的，你可以看到”——他指向几队海军陆战队员。

正在进行搜查

今天凌晨，在虹口和闸北地区对失踪者进行了彻底搜查，日本当局得到了中国警察局、淞沪警备司令部以及工部局警务处特别政治组的充分合作。

同盟社报道，总领事冈本季正（Suemasa Okamoto）于晚上11点30分在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）的办公室拜访了海军副武官奥野又太郎（Matao Okino）少佐，并在午夜后继续闭门会议。

深夜，陆战队抓获了一名携带左轮手枪的可疑中国人。

他被带到陆战队总部后，声称自己是中国警察局的侦探，当天早些时候被指派看守薪饷。据同盟社报道，陆战队当局对他的解释感到满意，将其释放。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JULY 25, 1937
EXCITEMENT IN CHAPEI
Hongkew Turned Into
War Camp As Japanese
Marine Disappears
Chinese Residents Stampede From Chapei As
Landing Party Searches For Missing Member;
S.M.C., Chinese Police Co-operating

Japanese Naval Landing Party details, searching for
one of their comrades who was alleged to be missing, last
night turned the northern areas of Shanghai into a virtual
armed camp and caused a stampede of Chinese residents
from Chapei.

Up to 2 o'clock this morning, Japanese sentries armed
in full field kits were remaining in Chapei, as far as about
500 yards north of the Woosun, -Shanghai Railway track.
Hongkew was seething with military activities as Japanese
naval trucks went up and down North Szechuen Road, Dix-
well Road and other streets.

The tense situation was the result
of the alleged disappearance of a
plainclothed Japanese Naval Landing
Party member, Sadao Miyazaki, a
First Class Seaman. The bluejacket,
according to a report furnished by
the Naval Landing Party headquar-
ters to the Dixwell Road Police, was
spirited away by a group of un-
identified persons after a scuffle at
the corner of North Szechuen and
Dixwell Roads at about 9.30 o'clock.

Cap and Tie Picked Up

First reporting the incident was a
Japanese civilian, who gave his
name as Yoshio Okazaki, living at 2
Woosung Road. The informant,
who stated that he witnessed the
scuffle and the alleged abduction,
picked up a cap and a tie said to have
belonged to the missing bluejacket.

The Japanese civilian informed a
Nipponese bluejacket and handed
the latter the two only clues of the
missing man. The two later tele-
phoned the Naval Landing Party
headquarters, the officers of which
immediately sent out a heavy armed
patrol.

A later check revealed that both
the name and address given by the
only eyewitness of the alleged abduc-
tion were false. At the time he
reported the incident, the informant
said that he could not visit the
Naval Landing Party headquarters.

All Cars Searched

Immediately after the receipt of
the news of the missing bluejacket,
a search was instituted by the Naval
Landing Party details. At 10 o'clock
all cars proceeding along North
Szechuen Road, Dixwell Road and
other Hongkew streets were search-
ed.

Settlement Police of the Dixwell
Road station, who were informed of
the incident by the Naval Landing
Party headquarters, also sent a large
party of officers to the scene to
investigate the affair and to help
in the search.

Cars, Pedestrians Searched

Meantime, Japanese bluejackets
with bayonetted guns and in full
field kits were sent across the Woo-
sung-Ehanghai Railway track. A
tour at midnight revealed that the
Landing Party patrols extended as
far as 500 yards north of the track
along Tungchi Road, Paoshing
Road and several other points.

In this section, which is under
the jurisdiction of the Municipality
of Greater Shanghai, cars and
pedestrians were also being stopped
and searched by the Japanese
patrols.

The Greater Shanghai Police, in-
formed of the incident by the
Japanese Consulate-General and
the Naval Landing Party head-
quarters, had ordered all constables
in the Chapei areas to start a
systematic combing for the allegedly
missing bluejacket.

Col. Liang Pu-chu, Chief of the
North Station branch of the Bureau
of Police, told THE CHINA PRESS at
midnight that apart from a re-
quest for assistance in the search,
no other communication has been
received by the Chinese authorities
from the Japanese naval officers.

Col. Liang has ordered his men
in the Chapei area to assist the
Japanese patrols.

Refugees Jam Streets

The exodus in Chapei started at
around 11 o'clock when Japanese
sentries started to march into the
Chinese areas. Despite efforts of
the Settlement and the Greater
Shanghai Police to keep the frigh-
tened residents from moving, large
parties of refugees were jamming all
roads leading to the Settlement
around the North Station.

A tour at midnight of the Chapei
area on both sides of the Woosung
Railway line and in the North
Station vicinity revealed widespread
excitement among the populace.
Belongings were hastily being loaded
into rickshas, wheelbarrows and
motor-cars, and a wholesale exodus
was under way. People streamed
along Paoshan Road, in particular,
toward the Settlement boundary at
North Klangse Road and Range
Road. Here they were being halted
by Chinese police and Settlement
police and prevented from entering
the Settlement. Police made efforts
to persuade the frightened people
to return to their homes. They
turned around, and some doubtless
went back to their houses, but others
obviously sought entry into the
Settlement by other routes and no
doubt succeeded.

Covers Wide Area

Taxis were in great demand and
traffic was jammed along Paoshan
Road. About four blocks beyond
the Settlement Boundary along
Paoshan Road, Chinese police
patrols became scarce. Here Japan-
ese patrolling started and covered
a wide area in the vicinity of the
Japanese Cemetery. Peace Preser-
vation Corpsmen were out in num-
bers at North Station and entrance
was prohibited to the station except
for persons with very necessary
business there.

Japanese patrols were stopping
motor-cars at practically every
street intersection in Chapei beyond
Range Road and scanning occu-
pants closely; Chinese police were
doing likewise in the area under
their control.

The district police station off
Paoshan Road bristled with activ-
ity. Detectives and high officers
rushed in and out and reporters,
Japanese, Chinese and Western,
thronged the place.

No Confirmation

Exhaustive investigations made by
a CHINA PRESS reporter into the
incident last night failed to produce
any corroboration of the story of the
missing Japanese sailor as given by
the anonymous Nipponese civilian.

Residents in the vicinity of North
Szechuen Road and Dixwell Road
said that they saw no scuffle and
no one being "kidnapped" at 9.30
o'clock.

Constable Yu Hu attached to the
North Szechuen Road Station of the
Bureau of Police, who was on duty
near the place of the alleged abduc-
tion said that at 9.30 o'clock, "every-
thing was quiet along the North
Szechuen Road and Dixwell Road
corner."

The place where the incident
happened is on an extra-Settlement
road, under the jurisdiction of the
Shanghai Municipal Police. Dixwell
Road Station officers reported that
constables on beat duty in the vicin-
ity of North Szechuen and Dixwell
Roads made no report that an
"abduction" took place.

Officials In Conference

Consul-General Suemasa Okamoto
called on Lieut.-Commander Matao
Okino, assistant naval attache, at
the naval attache's office in Dixwell
Road, at 11:30 o'clock at night, and
still remained closeted in confer-
ence half an hour later.

Late at night, the Landing Party
seized a suspicious Chinese carrying
a revolver.

Taken to the headquarters of the
Landing Party, he said that
he was a detective of the
Chinese Bureau of Police and that
earlier in the day he was
detailed to guard a payroll.
Satisfied with his explanation, the
Landing Party authorities released
him.

《字林西报》，1937年7月25日，星期日

闸北局势紧张

随着一名日本水兵失踪，虹口变成军营

陆战队搜寻失踪成员引发闸北中国居民恐慌出逃；

工部局与中国警方合作

日本海军陆战队分队昨晚搜寻一名据称失踪的同伴，将上海北部地区变成了事实上的武装营地，并导致中国居民从闸北恐慌出逃。

截至今天凌晨2点，全副武装的日本哨兵仍驻守在闸北，北至淞沪铁路轨道以北约500码处。随着日本海军卡车在北四川路、狄思威路和其他街道来回穿梭，虹口充满了军事活动。

紧张局势源于一名便衣日本海军陆战队成员、一等水兵宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki）的所谓失踪。据海军陆战队总部向狄思威路警察局提供的报告称，这名水兵在晚上9点30分左右于北四川路与狄思威路拐角处发生争执后，被一群身份不明的人强行带走。

拾获帽子和领带

最早报告此事的是一名日本平民，自称冈崎义夫（Yoshio Okazaki），住在吴淞路2号。这位线人称目睹了争执和所谓的绑架，并捡到了据称属于失踪水兵的一顶帽子和一条领带。

这名日本平民通知了一名日本水兵，并将这两件唯一的线索交给了他。两人随后致电海军陆战队总部，总部官员立即派出了一支重型武装巡逻队。

后来的核查显示，这起所谓绑架案唯一目击者提供的姓名和地址均为虚假。他在报告此事时称，他无法前往海军陆战队总部。

搜查所有车辆

接到水兵失踪的消息后，海军陆战队分队立即展开了搜查。10点钟，所有沿北四川路、狄思威路及其他虹口街道行驶的车辆均受到搜查。

狄思威路巡捕房的租界警察接到海军陆战队总部的通知后，也派遣了大量警员前往现场调查此事并协助搜查。

搜查车辆和行人

与此同时，手持装有刺刀的枪支并全副武装的日本水兵被派往越过淞沪铁路轨道。午夜时的巡视显示，陆战队巡逻队沿通北路（Tungchi Road）、宝兴路（Paoshing Road）及其他几个点延伸，远至轨道以北500码处。

在这一属于大上海市政府管辖的区域，日本巡逻队也在拦截和搜查车辆及行人。

大上海警察局接到日本总领事馆和海军陆战队总部的通知后，已命令闸北地区的所有警员开始系统地搜捕据称失踪的水兵。

警察局北站分局局长梁朴初（Liang Pu-chu，音译）上校在午夜告诉《字林西报》，除了请求协助搜查外，中国当局未收到日本海军军官的其他任何通信。

梁上校已命令其手下在闸北地区协助日本巡逻队。

难民堵塞街道

闸北的出逃始于11点左右，当时日本哨兵开始进入中国区域。尽管租界和大上海警察局努力阻止惊恐的居民移动，但大批难民仍挤满了通往北站周围租界的所有道路。

午夜时对淞沪铁路线两侧及北站附近闸北地区的巡视显示，民众中普遍存在恐慌情绪。财物被匆忙装上人力车、独轮车和汽车，大规模出逃正在进行中。人们特别是沿着宝山路涌向租界边界，即北康司脱路（North Klangse Road，音译）和雷恩路（Range Road）。在这里，他们被中国警察和租界警察拦下，并被阻止进入租界。警方努力劝说惊恐的人们返回家园。他们转身离开，有些人无疑回到了家中，但其他人显然试图通过其他路线进入租界，并且无疑成功了。

覆盖广大区域

出租车需求量大增，宝山路的交通陷入拥堵。在沿宝山路越过租界边界约四个街区的地方，中国警察巡逻队变得稀少。此处开始了日本人的巡逻，覆盖了日本公墓附近的大片区域。北站有大量保安队队员出动，除有非常必要事务的人员外，禁止进入车站。

日本巡逻队在闸北雷恩路以外的几乎每个街道交叉口拦截机动车，并仔细检查乘客；中国警察在其控制区域内也在做同样的事情。

宝山路附近的区警察局内活动频繁。侦探和高级警官进进出出，日本、中国和西方记者挤满了这个地方。

未经证实

《字林西报》记者昨晚对该事件进行的详尽调查，未能找到任何证据佐证那名匿名日本平民所说的关于日本水兵失踪的故事。

北四川路和狄思威路附近的居民表示，他们在9点30分没有看到任何争执，也没有看到任何人被“绑架”。

警察局北四川路巡捕房的警员余虎（Yu Hu，音译）在所谓绑架地点附近执勤，他说在9点30分，“北四川路和狄思威路拐角处一切平静”。

事发地点位于越界筑路，由上海公共租界工部局警务处管辖。狄思威路巡捕房官员报告称，在北四川路和狄思威路附近巡逻的警员未报告发生“绑架”事件。

官员举行会议

晚上11点30分，总领事冈本季正（Suemasa Okamoto）在狄思威路的海军武官办公室拜访了海军副武官奥野又太郎（Matao Okino）少佐，半小时后仍在闭门会议中。

深夜，陆战队抓获了一名携带左轮手枪的可疑中国人。

他被带到陆战队总部后，声称自己是中国警察局的侦探，当天早些时候被指派看守薪饷。陆战队当局对他的解释感到满意，将其释放。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, JULY 25, 1937

JAPANESE NAVY
PATROLS COMB
HONGKEW AREA

Bluejacket Kidnapped By
Three Chinese

PUSHED IN MOTOR CAR

Strange Disappearance is
Aftermath of Fight

Hongkew, in a calm but nervous state since news of the northern trouble filtered through into Shanghai, was suddenly plunged into a state of high tension last night by the reported kidnapping of a Japanese bluejacket by a party of Chinese. The details of the incident are not yet known, and full investigations were still proceeding up to an early hour this morning.

As far as could be ascertained, however, a party of three Japanese bluejackets became involved in a fight with a larger party of Chinese in an alleyway near the corner of Dixwell Road and North Szechuen Road at about 3.20 p.m. Following the fracas, the Chinese party whisked one of the Japanese, Sadao Miyozak.

Chinese Declare
Martial Law

It was reported early this morning that the Chinese authorities had declared martial law in Chapei and adjacent Chinese areas.

first class seaman, into a car, and took him off at a high speed in an unknown direction. News of this sensational incident was first conveyed by a Japanese civilian to a patrol party, and was quickly flashed through to Naval Landing Party Headquarters, and to Chinese and Settlement police stations.

The informer could not be found last night, and an intensive search was being made for him throughout Hongkew. Meanwhile, the whole district was plunged into a fever of excitement. Japanese blue jackets, in full war kit, wearing steel helmets and carrying rifles with fixed bayonets, were speedily stationed all along Dixwell Road, and for a large distance along North Szechuen Road. Frequent patrols were encountered by a "North-China Daily News" representative who toured the district soon after the incident, and all cars were stopped, and their occupants interrogated.

Trucks crammed full of fully equipped Landing Party personnel tore through the streets, depositing the men at various points in Hongkew, setting up a cordon of grim figures around the area within which the kidnapping took place. All along the pavements, little groups of Chinese were gathered, discussing in whispers the ominous event which had within a flash plunged a large part of the northern district into a fever of excitement.

It was noticeable that, although a large area around the spot where the kidnapping is believed to have occurred was enclosed with a cordon of marines, that part of Hongkew fronting the Soochow Creek was quiet, and gave no outward signs of disturbance. Seemingly, all precautions were confined to the area immediately around the fateful spot, and there appeared to be a desire on the part of the Japanese military authorities not to plunge the whole of the Hongkew area into an atmosphere of suspense by the stationing of troops around the entire district.

Outside the Dixwell Road barracks of the Landing Party were drawn up a long line of military trucks waiting to convey marines swiftly to any part of Hongkew. Their feet tapping out a steady rhythm on the asphalt, a company of marines were observed running in formation along Dixwell Road.

Outside Dixwell Road police station were a couple of Japanese marines standing guard with fixed bayonets, while inside the compound Japanese officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police conferred on the seriousness of the situation. A visitor to the police station was Inspector "Power" Chen, of the Bureau of Public Safety of the Shanghai City Government. No extra details were sent out from Dixwell Road or Hongkew Police Stations, but the usual precautions were taken. The Reserve Unit was standing by yesterday evening in case the situation should become more serious.

A spokesman at the Landing Party Headquarters stated that it was not possible to give out any detailed information at that time as investigations were still proceeding.

《字林西报》，1937年7月25日，星期日

日本海军
巡逻队搜查
虹口地区

三名华人绑架
一名水兵

被推入汽车

离奇失踪系斗殴之后果

自北方事态的消息传入上海以来，虹口一直处于一种平静但紧张的状态，而昨晚据报道发生了一起日本人水兵被一群华人绑架的事件，使该地区突然陷入高度紧张之中。事件详情尚不清楚，直至今日凌晨，全面调查仍在进行中。

据目前所能查明，下午3时20分左右，三名日本水兵在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）与北四川路（North Szechuen Road）拐角附近的一条小巷里，与一群人数较多的华人发生了斗殴。混战之后，这群华人将其中一名叫宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyozak）的日本水兵

华人宣布
戒严

据悉，今日凌晨中国当局已在闸北及邻近华人区域宣布戒严。

一等水兵强行塞进一辆汽车，并高速驶向一个未知的方向。这一轰动性事件的消息最初由一名日本平民告知一支巡逻队，随后迅速通报至海军陆战队总部以及中外巡捕房。

昨晚未能找到这名举报人，整个虹口地区正在对他进行密集搜寻。与此同时，整个街区陷入了狂热的兴奋状态。身穿全套作战装备、头戴钢盔、手持装有刺刀步枪的日本水兵迅速沿狄思威路部署，并在北四川路很长一段距离内布防。《字林西报》的一名代表在事件发生后不久巡视了该地区，遇到了频繁的巡逻队，所有车辆均被拦停，车内人员受到盘问。

载满全副武装陆战队人员的卡车呼啸穿过街道，将士兵部署在虹口的各个地点，在发生绑架事件的区域周围设立了一道由严峻身影组成的警戒线。人行道上聚集着一小群一小群的华人，低声议论着这一不祥事件，该事件在瞬间使北部大片地区陷入狂热的兴奋之中。

值得注意的是，尽管被认为发生绑架的地点周围的大片区域被海军陆战队的警戒线包围，但虹口面向苏州河的那部分区域却很安静，没有表现出任何骚乱的迹象。看来，所有的预防措施都局限于那个致命地点附近的 immediate 区域，日本军事当局似乎不希望因在整个街区部署军队而使整个虹口地区陷入悬疑的气氛中。

在陆战队狄思威路兵营外，排列着一长列军用卡车，随时准备将海军陆战队员迅速运送到虹口的任何地方。有人看到一连海军陆战队员排着队形沿狄思威路奔跑，他们的脚在沥青路上踏出稳定的节奏。

狄思威路巡捕房外，几名日本海军陆战队员持枪站岗，刺刀已装上；而在院内，上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本警官正在就局势的严重性进行磋商。上海市公安局的陈“鲍尔”（Power）督察（音译）曾到访该巡捕房。狄思威路或虹口巡捕房未发布更多细节，但采取了常规的预防措施。后备队昨晚待命，以防局势变得更加严重。

陆战队总部发言人表示，由于调查仍在进行，当时无法提供任何详细信息。

Dixwell Rd. Area is Quiet:
Seaman Missing
(Continued from page 9)

O. K. Yui, Acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, at 11.30 o'clock yesterday morning.
Mr. Okamoto also expressed appreciation to Mr. Yui for the assistance of the Greater Shanghai authorities in investigating the circumstances surrounding the affair.
After briefly relating the situation arising from last night's incident, the Japanese Consul-General also informed Mr. Yui of the withdrawal of the Naval Landing Party units from the Chinese area early this morning.

Mr. Yui's Reply
Replying Mr. Yui stated that immediately following receipt of reports of the incident, Chinese police authorities sent out men to co-operate with the S.M.C. police in their investigations.
Mr. Yui expressed deep regret over the unwarranted activities of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, which sent out fully-equipped patrols to territory outside of the International Settlement even before they had made any investigations into the incident.
Mr. Yui expressed the hope that in the future the Japanese Naval Landing Party would exercise greater consideration in order to avoid misunderstandings.
As to Chinese assistance in investigating the case, Mr. Yui said it was natural because it was part of the duties of the Chinese police to do so. The interview lasted for over half an hour.

Tokyo Orders
Tokyo, July 25.
"Strong efforts" to prevent unnecessary commotion are being made by the Japanese naval authorities in Shanghai, a communiqué issued by the Navy Ministry at 11 o'clock this morning said.
The investigations into the disappearance of Seaman Sadao Miyazaki, the announcement added, were being continued.
In view of the "complicated conditions" prevailing in Shanghai, the communiqué went on, endeavours were being made to "learn the facts and ascertain the circumstances" of the affair. "The most suitable measures" to deal with the situation will be taken after the facts in the case are determined, the communiqué said.
The disappearance of the sailor was announced in a communiqué issued by the Navy Ministry at 4 o'clock this morning.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party in Shanghai, the announcement said, had taken precautionary measures following the receipt of information from a resident that Seaman Miyazaki had been abducted by Chinese near the intersection of North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads at about 9 o'clock last night.
Investigations to ascertain the facts of the case were being made by the Landing Party in co-operation with the Chinese Police and the Shanghai Municipal Police, the announcement added.

Navy's Action
Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai, Minister of the Navy, this noon obtained the approval of the Cabinet to his policy of "proceeding with circumspection" in dealing with the disappearance of a Japanese sailor.
This assent of other ministers was given at an informal meeting of the Cabinet at the official residence of the Premier, Prince Fumimaro Konoye, held after a luncheon given following the opening ceremony of the session of the Diet.—Domei.

（续第9版）

大上海代理市长俞鸿钧先生于昨日上午11时30分。
冈本先生还对俞先生在调查此事相关情况时给予的大上海当局的协助表示感谢。
日本总领事在简要叙述了昨晚事件引发的局势后，还通知俞先生，海军陆战队部队已于今日凌晨撤出华人区域。

俞先生的答复
俞先生回答说，在收到事件报告后，中国警察当局立即派出人员配合工部局警务处进行调查。
俞先生对日本海军陆战队毫无理由的行动深表遗憾，他们在尚未对事件进行任何调查之前，就向国际租界以外的地区派出了全副武装的巡逻队。
俞先生希望日本海军陆战队今后能更加谨慎行事，以避免误解。
关于中方协助调查此案，俞先生说这是自然的，因为这是中国警察的职责所在。会谈持续了半个多小时。

东京命令
东京，7月25日。
海军省今早11时发表的一份公报称，上海日本海军当局正在做出“巨大努力”以防止不必要的骚动。
公报补充说，对一等水兵宫崎贞雄（Sadao Miyazaki）失踪案的调查仍在继续。
公报接着说，鉴于上海 prevailing 的“复杂局势”，正努力“了解事实并查明情况”。公报称，在确定案件事实后，将采取“最合适的措施”来处理局势。
水兵失踪的消息是在海军省今早4时发表的一份公报中宣布的。
公告称，上海日本海军陆战队在接到一名居民提供的信息后采取了预防措施，该信息称宫崎水兵昨晚9时许在北四川路与狄思威路交汇处附近被华人绑架。
公告补充说，陆战队正与中国警察和上海公共租界工部局警务处合作，调查以查明案件事实。

海军的行动
海军大臣米内光政（Mitsumasa Yonai）海军中将于今日中午获得内阁对其在处理日本水兵失踪事件中“谨慎行事”政策的批准。
其他大臣的同意是在首相近卫文麿亲王官邸举行的非正式内阁会议上给出的，该会议是在国会会议开幕式后的午餐会后举行的。——同盟社

All was quiet late last night in the Hongkew District. The streets were well crowded with the usual Sunday night crowds, but there was no tension in the air and most people sauntered along, chatting in carefree manner.

TERRITORY DISPUTE
IN EUROPE

U.S.S.R. Claim to Bessarabia
Feared in France

Paris, July 25.
Will a new territorial dispute disturb the already shattered peace of Europe? Such is the question asked by several Paris dailies to-day in commenting upon a recent article of the Soviet newspaper "Pravda" which complained of the policies followed by Rumania and which was interpreted as again putting forward the U.S.S.R. claim to Bessarabia.
It will be recalled that the province of Bessarabia, which was formerly under Russian administration, was occupied by Rumanian forces after the World War. The Union of Bessarabia with Rumania was ratified by the signatories of the Treaty of Versailles in 1920, but the Soviet Union did not recognize the validity of this annexation.
Studying the question in "L'Oeuvre," Mme. Genevieve Tabouis writes: "In 1934, in London, the Rumanian Foreign Minister, M. Nicholas Titulesco, obtained from the Soviet Foreign Commissar, M. Maxim Litvinov, a statement in which both statesmen recognized that Bessarabia belonged to Rumania, as all the authority in its territory was for the time being held by Rumanians. It is easy to see how feeble is the title of possession created by this document and how much Rumanians must praise good relations with U.S.S.R.
"It is generally believed," Mme. Tabouis concludes, "that the new attitude of the U.S.S.R. is meant to be a warning to Rumanian politicians at the moment when King Carol II is leaving for Germany to interview Herr Adolph Hitler."—Havas.

欧洲领土争端

苏联对比萨拉比亚的主权要求
引发法国担忧

巴黎，7月25日。
新的领土争端会扰乱欧洲已经破碎的和平吗？这是几家巴黎日报今天在评论苏联报纸《真理报》最近的一篇文章时提出的问题，该文章抱怨罗马尼亚遵循的政策，并被解读为再次提出苏联对比萨拉比亚的主权要求。
回想一下，比萨拉比亚省以前由俄罗斯管理，在世界大战后被罗马尼亚军队占领。1920年，《凡尔赛条约》的签署国批准了比萨拉比亚与罗马尼亚的合并，但苏联不承认这一兼并的有效性。
吉纳维芙·塔布伊斯（Genevieve Tabouis）夫人在《作品报》（L'Oeuvre）上研究这一问题时写道：“1934年在伦敦，罗马尼亚外交部长尼古拉·蒂图莱斯库（Nicholas Titulesco）先生从苏联外交人民委员马克西姆·李维诺夫（Maxim Litvinov）先生那里获得了一份声明，两位政治家都承认比萨拉比亚属于罗马尼亚，因为其领土内的所有权力当时都由罗马尼亚人掌握。不难看出，这份文件所创造的占有权是多么薄弱，罗马尼亚人必须多么赞扬与苏联的良好关系。”
塔布伊斯夫人总结道：“人们普遍认为，苏联的新态度意在警告罗马尼亚政客，此时卡罗尔二世国王正前往德国会见阿道夫·希特勒先生。”——哈瓦斯社

At about 8 a.m. on July 26 he noticed a steamer fly-

Having already made up his mind to pay for with his life for

However, being a good swimmer he failed in his attempt and
finally swam to the shore at Tsingkiang Hsien. Utterly
exhausted, he spent the night on the bank of the river and,
still not being satisfied, he made another futile attempt

about 10 a.m. on July 27th when he was picked up by a native
junk the crew of which took him to the Police Bureau at
Tsingkiang Hsien. In due course, he was transferred from
here to the Administrative Office of the Kiangsu Province.
The provincial officials, in turn, sent him to the Weichiao-
pu in Nanking on July 29th. At about 8 p.m. the same day

General at Nanking by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

宫崎表示，他对青浦县公安局、江苏省政府以及南京外交部对待他的方式没有任何抱怨，并断言事实上，在他受他们照管期间，他们对他非常好。
在审查关于宫崎行动的细节时，人们注意到几处相互矛盾的陈述，这些陈述在常人听来绝不合理，但很可能，这是由于他在从上海出逃时，因过度焦虑而引发了失忆症发作所致。
根据一等水兵柳田（Yanagida）的证词，那位自称冈崎（Okasaki）的线人与一等水兵宫崎之间有着惊人的相似之处，目前正通过讯问宫崎及其他相关人员进一步调查，以澄清这一点。”
以下是日本海军陆战队指挥官就同一案件发表的公开声明。
“借此机会，我代表日本海军陆战队，向两个市议会当局、日本领事警察、日本侨民团体以及中国当局表示诚挚的感谢，感谢他们在7月24日晚发生的一等水兵宫崎失踪案的调查中给予的迅速合作和不懈努力。

Sir,
Acting on the suggestion made to the Japanese Naval
Authorities, the three seamen who were accosted by the informant
and whom they declare they would be able to identify, attended
this station at 5 p.m. 27-7-37, in plain clothes. Three
separate parties were formed consisting of an S.M.P. Japanese
detective, a Consular Police Official and one of the seamen. In
the hope of locating the informant these parties visited numerous
Japanese cafes, restaurants and other likely resorts between the
hours of 5.30 p.m. and 11 p.m.

J.D.S. 51 (Dixwell Road) accompanied one party and visited
all likely places on the East side of North Szechuen Road and
roads and alleyways leading into Chapel.

J.D.C. 132 (Hongkew) did likewise on the West side of North
Szechuen Road and roads and alleyways leading thereof.

J.D.C. 138 (Hongkew) did likewise in Hongkew District,
concentrating on such roads as Woosung, East Haining, Chapeo,
etc, where Japanese predominate.

No successful results have so far been met with but arrange-
ments are being made to continue the search tomorrow evening,

Made by D. I. Duncan. Forwarded by...
Sir,
Following the disappearance of a member of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party during the evening of July 24 and the
subsequent activities of special patrols, a certain tenseness
was noticed in the district and a number of inhabitants of
houses in Chinese territory North of Range Road moved into
the Settlement. The majority of the persons who moved did so
by rickshas and carried with them a few boxes and personal
effects.
At 8 a.m. this morning 25/7/37 the district was quiet
and the movement of persons seeking the safety of the Settle-
ment had greatly diminished. Chinese territory adjoining
Hongkew district is quiet although a few members of the
Peace Preservation Corps armed with rifles and bayonets
were seen on duty at different points.

Dixwell Road Station, 37
REPORT
Date July 25, 19 37
Subject Alleged kidnapping of a member of the Special Japanese Naval Landing
Party Headquarters.
Made by D.S.I. Cumming Forwarded by Jmanson Insp.

Sir,
At 9.15 p.m. 24-7-37, three Japanese Naval Ratings named
(1) Tanaka, (2) Karomasu and (3) Morimoto (ranks unknown) were
returning to the Special Naval Landing Party Barracks via North
Szechuen Road, and when passing the Uchiyama Book Store, 1071 N.
Szechuen Road, near Darroch Road corner, they were accosted by a
Japanese civilian. The latter told the sailors that a Japanese
sailor had been dragged into a waiting motor car by some Chinese
on Dixwell Road about two cho (4 200 yards) East of North Szechuen
Road corner. At the same time he handed the sailors a naval
uniform scarf and hat, stating that these were the property of
the kidnapped sailor. The sailors were on the point of entering
the above mentioned book store to telephone when the civilian
stepped into a ricsha intending to depart. He was stopped by
the seamen but excused himself on the grounds that his mother
was seriously ill and his attendance at home was urgently needed.
Before he was allowed to depart, however, one of the sailors
procured a piece of paper and pencil from the book store and
asked the civilian to write his name and address thereon. The
following particulars were then given :-
"Yoshio Okasaki, 85 Woosung Road."
The informant was then allowed to go and he departed by
ricsha in a Southerly direction. The sailors first telephoned
the Landing Party Headquarters and then returned to make a
personal report.
The Landing Party was immediately mobilized and strong
pickets stationed at all cross-roads and other strategic points
in the Northern district, along North Szechuen Road as far as
Wang Pang Jao and along Dixwell Road as far as Kashing Road

先生，
1937年7月24日晚上9点15分，三名日本海军士兵，名为(1) 田中（Tanaka），(2) Karomasu（音译）和(3) 森本（Morimoto）（军衔不详），正经由北四川路返回特别海军陆战队营房，当经过达罗克路（Darroch Road）拐角附近的北四川路1071号内山书店时，他们被一名日本平民搭讪。后者告诉水兵们，大约在距北四川路拐角以东两町（约4200码）的狄思威路上，一名日本水兵被一些中国人拖进了一辆等候的汽车。同时，他递给水兵们一条海军制服围巾和一顶帽子，称这些是被绑架水兵的财物。水兵们正打算进入上述书店打电话，该平民却踏上一辆黄包车准备离开。水兵们拦住了他，但他以母亲病重、急需回家照料为由为自己开脱。然而，在允许他离开之前，其中一名水兵从书店拿来纸笔，要求该平民写下他的姓名和地址。随后提供了以下信息：
“吉雄·冈崎（Yoshio Okasaki），吴淞路85号。”
随后允许该线人离开，他乘黄包车向南离去。水兵们首先给陆战队总部打了电话，然后回去亲自汇报。
陆战队立即动员，并在北区的所有十字路口和其他战略要点部署了强力哨位，沿北四川路直至王邦焦（Wang Pang Jao，音译），沿狄思威路直至嘉善路（Kashing Road）

Bridges. Patrols were also posted on Tien Tung An Road and Pao-
shan Road, Chapei, as far as Wang Pang Road Railway crossing.
All passing motor vehicles were challenged. Considerable
consternation was evident amongst the populace but no evacuation
on a large scale took place in this district although I understand
that a considerable number of people were evacuating that part of
Chapei situated just North of the railway line.

The sailors cap, on examination, proved to belong to 1st
class seaman Sadao Miyazaki, attached to the Special Naval Landing
Party Headquarters, Kiangwan Road. Lieut. Commander Yamanouchi,
Adjutant, J.N.L.P., was interviewed and stated that the missing
sailor left Barracks at 12.15 p.m. 24-7-37. When leaving he was
asked by Warrant Officer Kichino to call for his (Kichino's)
wrist watch which was being repaired. He had apparently fulfill-
ed this mission as he handed the watch over to another sailor,
named Sanada at the Japanese Naval Club, Miller Road, after 3 p.m.,
telling the latter to return it to the Warrant Officer as he
intended to spend the night at the Naval Club. The missing
sailor was last seen at 7 p.m. leaving the Town Tao Theatre, Chapoo
Road, alone.

The circumstances surrounding this incident are, on the
whole, difficult in the way of forming any feasible conclusion
as will be shown by the following points :-
(1) The informant gave a fictitious name and address, there
being no number 85 on Woosung Road. There is only one Japanese
by the name of Okasaki in Shanghai. He has been investigated by
the Consular Police, and found to have no connection with this
incident.
(2) The evident anxiety of the informant to get away from the

桥梁。巡逻队也部署在闸北的天通庵路和宝山路，直至王浜路铁路道口。所有过往机动车辆均受到盘查。民众中明显表现出相当大的恐慌，尽管据我了解，有相当数量的人正在撤离位于铁路线以北的闸北地区，但该区域并未发生大规模疏散。

经检查，那顶水手帽被证实属于隶属于江湾路日本海军特别陆战队司令部的上等兵宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）。日本海军特别陆战队副官山内（Yamanouchi）少佐接受询问时表示，该名失踪水兵于1937年7月24日下午12时15分离开营房。离开时，军士长吉野（Kichino）要求他顺道取回正在修理的（吉野的）手表。他显然完成了这项任务，因为下午3点后，他在米勒路（Miller Road）的日本海军俱乐部将手表交给了另一名名为真田（Sanada）的水兵，并告诉后者将其归还给军士长，因为他打算在海军俱乐部过夜。该失踪水兵最后被人看见是在晚上7点，独自离开乍浦路（Chapoo Road）的道陶大戏院（Town Tao Theatre）。

总体而言，围绕此事件的情况难以得出任何可行的结论，理由如下：
(1) 报案人提供了虚假的姓名和地址，吴淞路并没有85号。上海只有一名名叫冈崎（Okasaki）的日本人。领事警察已对其进行了调查，发现他与本事件无关。
(2) 报案人在向日本水兵提供信息后，明显急于离开

scene after giving his information to the Japanese sailors.
    (3) The locality given by the informant would place the scene
of the incident approximately opposite Dixwell Road Station, which
would hardly be a likely place for an incident of this nature to
be staged.
    (4) Japanese sailors are under instructions never to go about
singly but must always to walk two or more together.
    Two shop assistants named Shigern Tamasaki and Chuzaburo
Okamoto employed at the book store previously referred to were
interrogated at the station but could give no information which
would add to that supplied by the three seamen.
    I am unable to ascertain definitely whether or not the missing
sailor had an all night pass but from his conversation at the
Naval Club, it would approve that he had.
    Mr. Ueyhara, D.C.P., interviewed the Commander of the J.N.L.P.
with regard to the possible withdrawal of street patrols to
avoid consternation amongst the populace.    The commander
expressed his regrets and stated that these precautions might be
relaxed at 6 a.m. tomorrow morning, 25-7-37, if the situation
permitted.
    A teleprinter message has been circulated to all stations
to have enquiries made at ricksha hongs in the hope of locating
the puller who was engaged by the informant on North Szechuen
Road.    A description of the informant is as follows:- Age about
21/2 years, 5'3" in height, slim build, sallow complexion, narrow
slant eyes, thin face, wearing white cotton singlet, white pants,
white belt and white tennis cap.
    Meanwhile the J.N.L.P. is being kept in touch with and they
have been assured of Police cooperation in efforts to trace the

    (4) 日本水兵奉命不得单独行动，必须两人或多人同行。
    此前提到的书店的两名店员，名为玉崎茂（Shigern Tamasaki）和冈本忠三郎（Chuzaburo Okamoto），在分局接受了讯问，但未能提供超出三名水兵所供信息之外的任何内容。
    我无法确切查明该失踪水兵是否持有通宵通行证，但根据他在海军俱乐部的谈话来看，他似乎持有。
    警务处副处长（D.C.P.）上原（Ueyhara）先生就撤除街头巡逻以避免民众恐慌的可能性，会晤了日本海军特别陆战队指挥官。指挥官表示遗憾，并称如果局势允许，这些预防措施可能会在明天早上，即1937年7月25日上午6时放宽。
    已向各分局分发电传打字机消息，要求在黄包车行进行查询，希望能找到报案人在北四川路雇用的车夫。报案人的体貌特征如下：年龄约21至22岁，身高5英尺3英寸，身材瘦削，面色蜡黄，细长的斜眼，瘦脸，身穿白色棉背心、白色裤子、白色腰带和白色网球帽。

from the Custodian of the Open Air Swimming Pool, Kiangwan Road,
reporting that a male Japanese was causing trouble there and
requesting for the service of a Japanese Policeman. J.P.S. 96
attended and found out that at about 10.30 a.m. even date a male
Japanese, Y. Ochie of 1680 Ward Road was taking off his bathing
suit in the presence of the public at the Swimming Pool and when
told by the Custodian to go in the dressing rooms refused to do
so. Left the pool on arrival of J.P.S. 96.

Radio Van
No. 88
Patrol
Between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. 24-7-37, a Radio Van patrolled
Dixwell Road and Kashing Road districts. No searching done in
the Dixwell Road district and no reports.

Accident
at the
S.M.C.
Swimming
Pool
At 3.08 p.m. 24-7-37, a telephone message was received from
C.C.R. reporting a S.F.3. ambulance had been sent to the Open
Air Swimming Pool, Kiangwan Road. C.D.C. 240 attended and ascer-
tained that one Yui Mei Chang, 25, Ningpo, m/shop assistant was
at about 3 p.m. swimming under the diving stand when an unknown
male Chinese dived into the pool and as he came to the surface
his head struck him in the face. Sent to St. Luke's Hospital a
Dr's chit was returned as follows;- "Laceration of nose, not
serious".

Alleged
Kidnapping
of Japanese
Naval Ratings
At 9.15 p.m. 24-7-37 three Japanese Naval Ratings were
returning to the J.N.L.P. Barracks when they were accosted out-
side the Uchiyama Book Store No. 1071 N. Szechuen Road near
Darroch Road by a Japanese civilian who informed them that a
Japanese sailor had been dragged into a waiting motor car by some
Chinese on Dixwell Road about 240 yards East of N. Szechuen Road
corner. At the same time he handed the sailors a naval uniform
scarf and hat which on investigation proved to belong to 1st
Class Seaman Sadao Miyazaki. After giving this information the
informant attempted to leave by ricksha but before doing so he
wrote on a piece of paper his supposed name and address "Yoshio
Okazaki, 85 Woosung Road.
The sailors immediately informed the Landing Party Head-
quarters and an officer called at this station to enquire if any
report had been received. On being informed that we had no such
report he returned to Headquarters and the Landing Party were
immediately mobilised. Strong pickets were stationed at all cross-
roads and other strategic points along N. Szechuen, Dixwell, and
Kiangwan Roads from the Wang Pang Bridge to the Hongkew Park West
gate and as far East as Kashing Road. Patrols also operated on
these roads stopping all vehicles and interrogating the occupants.
After an all night search and up to 7 a.m. 25-7-37 the missing man
had not been located, though enquiries are still being instituted
by S.M.P. Consular, and Naval Authorities. Investigations by the
the above go to show that the name and address of the informer
are fictitious and some doubt is expressed as to the genuineness
of the report since the informer appeared in a hurry to get away.

狄思威路警察分局主管每日报告副本。

1937年7月25日，星期日。

露天
游泳池
事件
1937年7月24日上午10时35分，接到江湾路露天游泳池管理员的电话报告，称一名日本男子在那里滋事，并要求派遣一名日本巡捕。日本巡捕第96号（J.P.S. 96）到场，发现当日上午10时30分左右，住在华德路1680号的一名日本男子Y. Ochie在游泳池当众脱去泳衣，当管理员要求其进入更衣室时，他拒绝照办。日本巡捕第96号到达后，该男子离开了游泳池。

无线电
警车
第88号
巡逻
1937年7月24日上午11时至下午3时之间，一辆无线电警车在狄思威路和嘉善路（Kashing Road）地区巡逻。狄思威路地区未进行搜查，也无相关报告。

工部局
游泳池
事故
1937年7月24日下午3时08分，接到中央无线电室（C.C.R.）电话报告，称一辆S.F.3型救护车已被派往江湾路露天游泳池。中央调度室第240号（C.D.C. 240）到场，查明一名名为张维梅（Yui Mei Chang，音译）、25岁、宁波籍的男店员，大约在下午3时在跳水台下方游泳时，一名身份不明的中国男子跳入池中，浮出水面时头部撞到了他的面部。被送往圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital），医生出具的诊断书如下：“鼻子撕裂伤，不严重”。

涉嫌
绑架
日本
海军士兵
1937年7月24日晚上9时15分，三名日本海军士兵在返回日本海军特别陆战队营房途中，在北四川路1071号内山书店（Uchiyama Book Store）外、靠近达罗克路（Darroch Road）处，被一名日本平民拦下。该平民告知他们，一名日本水兵在狄思威路被一些中国人拖进了一辆等候的汽车，地点位于北四川路口以东约240码处。同时，他交给水兵们一条海军制服围巾和一顶帽子，经查证，这些物品属于上等兵宫崎贞夫。提供此信息后，报案人试图乘黄包车离开，但在离开前，他在一张纸上写下了他所谓的姓名和地址：“冈崎义雄（Yoshio Okazaki），吴淞路85号”。
水兵们立即通知了陆战队司令部，一名军官来到本分局，询问是否收到任何报告。得知我们没有此类报告后，他返回司令部，陆战队随即动员。从王浜桥到虹口公园西门，以及向东至嘉善路，沿北四川路、狄思威路和江湾路的所有十字路口和其他战略要点都部署了强力哨位。巡逻队也在这些道路上行动，拦截所有车辆并盘查车内人员。经过彻夜搜索，截至1937年7月25日上午7时，尚未找到失踪者，尽管工部局警务处、领事馆和海军当局仍在进行调查。上述机构的调查表明，报案人的姓名和地址是虚构的，且由于报案人显得急于离开，人们对报告的真实性表示怀疑。

Reports (Continued)

All pickets etc. were withdrawn at 5 a.m. and only four
patrols are now operating in the area i.e. N. Szechuen, Darroch,
Dixwell and Chapel.
The D.C. Divisions, Mr. Uyehara, D.D.O. "C" and other
officials attended this station during the course of enquiries.

Jammalson

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No. 48/37
Dixwell Road Station,
REPORT
Date July 25, 19 37

Subject Further Alleged kidnapping of a member of the Special Japanese Naval
Landing Party Headquarters.
Made by D.S.I. Cumming Forwarded by Jmrason Inspt

Sir,
Further to my previous report on the above subject dated
25th July, 1937, I have to report that conditions in the Northern
Area have now returned to normal. All extra pickets and patrols
were withdrawn at 5 a.m. this inst. and now only routine patrols
are being maintained. There has been a considerable exodus of
people from Chapei especially from the Paoshan Road area during
the last 24 hours due to the spread of alarmist rumours and
evacuation is still continuing although not to such a great
extent.

During the course of enquiries into the disappearance of the
missing seaman information was obtained by Japanese detectives
concerning a fracas which took place amongst Japanese sailors at
the Teikoku Cafe, situated in an alleyway off North Szechuen Road
next to the 'Blue Bird' Cabaret, O.O.L. It appears that at
8.30 p.m. 24-7-37 trouble arose between two seamen named Hikida
and Mayada. The latter apparently put on the former's shoes by
mistake, as the result of which an argument took place, in which
a number of sailors participated. Considerable excitement
prevailed but with the intervention of a Warrant Officer the
affair was amicably settled. Owing to the proximity of this
cafe to the Uchiyama Book Store (where the information re the
alleged kidnapping was given to the three sailors), it was
thought that this might supply a clue to the disappearance of the
seaman. This information was therefore passed to Commander
Takide, Chief of Staff, J.N.L.P., who questioned the principals
in the fracas, but as far as could be ascertained no connection
between this and the disappearance of the seaman could be establish
-ed.

（左侧批注：C 26/7）
（左侧批注：S.I. 8/802 26/7）
（印章：26 JULY 1937）

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
杂项档案号 48/37
狄思威路分局，
报告
日期 1937年7月25日

事由 关于日本海军特别陆战队司令部成员进一步涉嫌被绑架的报告。
呈报人 卡明（Cumming）分区副督察长 转呈人 贾姆拉森（Jmrason）巡官

先生，
继我于1937年7月25日就上述主题提交的前一份报告之后，兹报告北区局势现已恢复正常。所有额外哨位和巡逻队已于今日凌晨5时撤除，目前仅维持常规巡逻。在过去24小时内，由于恐慌性谣言的传播，大量人口从闸北撤离，特别是从宝山路地区，尽管撤离规模已不如之前那么大，但仍在继续。

在调查失踪水兵的过程中，日本侦探获得了一些信息，涉及在日本水兵之间发生的一场争吵，地点位于北四川路旁的一条小巷内的帝国咖啡馆（Teikoku Cafe），紧邻“蓝鸟”歌舞厅（'Blue Bird' Cabaret），O.O.L.。看来在1937年7月24日晚上8时30分，两名名为引田（Hikida）和真田（Mayada，音译）的水兵之间发生了纠纷。后者似乎误穿了前者的鞋子，由此引发了一场争论，多名水兵卷入其中。现场气氛相当激动，但在一位军士长的干预下，此事得以和平解决。鉴于这家咖啡馆靠近内山书店（即向三名水兵提供所谓绑架信息的地点），人们认为这可能为水兵的失踪提供线索。因此，这一信息被转告给日本海军特别陆战队参谋长高出（Takide，音译）指挥官，他讯问了争吵的主要当事人，但据查，此事与水兵失踪之间无法建立任何联系。

（左侧批注：C 26/7）
（左侧批注：S.I. 8/802 26/7）
（印章：1937年7月26日）
（左侧批注：c.p. 8/802 26/7 已阅 26/7 JMR）

Further efforts to follow the movement of the missing man
on the day in question show that he was last seen at the Osakaya
Naval Tailors, Woosung Road, at about 7 p.m., having apparently
gone there direct from the Tao Theatre, Chapoo Road, mentioned
in my previous report. The manager of this establishment was
therefore interviewed but could give no information of value, as
seamen to the number of about 80 had visited his place of business
during the afternoon and evening in question. No further inform-
ation concerning the movements of the missing man after 7 p.m.
can be obtained despite exhaustive enquiries made by the Naval
Authorities.

It is of interest to note that the informant when giving
his address to the three seamen, stated that he lived at 80 (not
85 as stated in first report) Woosung Road, and that his home was
located opposite the Naval Tailors above referred to. His motive
in making this statement was apparently to inspire confidence, as
the location of this establishment is well known to all Japanese
naval men. The numbers in the vicinity of this tailors store
run in the three hundreds which would appear to prove that the
informant was deliberately making a misleading statement.

Further enquiries resulted in the finding of a Japanese
witness, who overheard the conversation between the informant and
the three seamen. He is one Jumico Iida, manager of the Toa Jute
Factory, 64 Robison Road. Interviewed by detectives this man
stated that about 9.15 p.m. 24-7-37, he was standing by his car
parked on the East side of North Szechuen Road about 30 yards
South of Chanchun Road, waiting for a wheel to be changed, as he
had a flat tyre. He saw the informant crossing North Szechuen
Road diagonally from a North Westerly direction and getting in

为进一步追踪失踪男子在事发当日的行踪，调查显示他最后被人看见是在晚上7点左右，位于吴淞路的大阪海军裁缝店（Osakaya Naval Tailors），显然是直接从此前报告中提到的乍浦路桃剧院（Tao Theatre）前往该处的。因此，对该店经理进行了问询，但他未能提供有价值的信息，因为在当天下午和晚间，约有80名水手光顾了他的店铺。尽管海军当局进行了详尽的调查，仍无法获得关于该失踪男子晚上7点以后行踪的进一步信息。

值得注意的是，线人在向三名水手提供地址时，声称自己住在吴淞路80号（而非第一份报告中所述的85号），并称其住所就在上述海军裁缝店的对面。他作出这一陈述的动机显然是为了博取信任，因为该店铺的地点为所有日本海军人员所熟知。该裁缝店附近的门牌号均为三位数，这似乎证明线人是在故意提供误导性陈述。

进一步调查找到了一名日本证人，他无意中听到了线人与三名水手之间的对话。此人名为饭田纯三郎（Jumico Iida，音译），系罗宾森路64号东亚黄麻厂（Toa Jute Factory）经理。侦探对此人进行问询时，他表示1937年7月24日晚上9点15分左右，他正站在停于北四川路东侧、长春路以南约30码处的汽车旁，等待更换轮胎，因为他的车胎爆了。他看见线人从西北方向斜穿北四川路，并走到

behind the three seamen, he shouted to them. He then observed
the informant handing one of the sailors the uniform cap which
he held folded up in his hand. A subsequent examination of the
cap showed that the wire ring had been deliberately broken, so that
the cap could be folded and concealed about the person. This
witness is of the opinion that the informant was not a Japanese
born subject. He formed this opinion from the fact that he (the
informant), when referring to his mother's illness referred to her
as "Okasan". This is an expression used in Japanese by children
only and never by adults, thus indicating that Japanese was not
the mother tongue of the informant. It is significant to note
that according to this witness several petty officers who were
walking in front of the seamen were ignored by the informant, he
having suspiciously chosen the seamen to tell his story to.
It has now been ascertained that there are about thirty
Japanese bearing the surname Okazaki in Shanghai, fifteen of whom
are between the ages of 21 and 40 years. The Consular Police are
at present checking up on those. Doctors and dispensaries are
also being visited in view of the statement by the informant that
his mother was ill.
The missing man, it was ascertained, was attached to Staff
Headquarters and is said to have been of a steady and reliable
character. He was in possession of about $10.00 when he left
barracks, a considerable amount for a man of his position.
A photograph is attached to this file and at the request
of the Naval Authorities I ask that reproduction be made (say
about 80) for distribution amongst all Japanese and Chinese
detectives. The question of printed circulars bearing the
photograph was broached but I understand that the Naval Authori-

那三名水手身后，并向他们喊话。随后，他观察到线人将手中折叠的一顶制服帽递给其中一名水手。事后对这顶帽子进行检查，发现金属丝圈被故意折断，以便将帽子折叠并藏匿在身上。这位证人认为，线人并非在日本出生的臣民。他形成这一看法的依据是，线人（即该线人）在提及母亲病情时，称其为“Okasan”（母亲）。这是日语中仅由儿童使用而成年人从不使用的表达方式，从而表明日语并非线人的母语。值得注意的是，据该证人称，线人无视了走在几名水手前面的几名士官，而是可疑地特意选择向这几名水手讲述他的故事。

现已查明，上海约有三十名姓冈崎（Okazaki）的日本人，其中十五人年龄在21至40岁之间。领事警察目前正在对这些人员进行核查。鉴于线人声称其母亲患病，医生和诊所也在走访之列。

经查，失踪男子隶属于参谋总部，据说性格沉稳可靠。他离开兵营时身上带有约10美元，对于他这种身份的人来说，这是一笔不小的数目。

Sir,
No further trace of the missing seaman has so far been found.
I therefore suggest that circulars in the following form be print-
ed for the usual distribution :-
"Missing from barracks and alleged to have been
kidnapped on Dixwell Road near North Szechuen Road
at about 9 p.m. 24-7-37.
1st class seaman SADAO MIYAZAKI of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party Headquarters, Kiangwan Road, age 22 years,
height 5'3", medium build, round face, small eyes,
pointed chin, several small bald spots on head."
I also suggest that circulars be printed for distribution
amongst ricsha boys, etc., bearing the following description of
the informant and offering a reward of $25.00 to anyone supplying
information which would help in locating him :-
"Age about 21/2 years, height 5'3", slim build, sallow
complexion, narrow slit eyes, thin face, wearing white
cotton singlet, white pants, white belt and white tennis
cap." Probably of Japanese or Korean nationality.
In view of the fact that the three sailors to whom the
information was first supplied, state that they would be able to
identify the informant, it was suggested to the Naval Authorities
that they be allowed to visit bars, cafes and other likely places
in plain clothes, accompanied by Consular and S.M. Police, in the
hope of locating the informant. The Authorities are at present
considering this suggestion.

feasible conclusion is difficult to arrive at but it is logical
to suppose that the motive behind it was to create a state of

报告
日期 1937年7月26日
续前
事由 关于日本海军特别陆战队总部一名成员被绑架的指控。
制作人 刑事侦缉督察坎宁（Canning） 转呈人 情报科

先生，
截至目前，尚未发现失踪水手的任何踪迹。
因此，我建议按以下格式印制通缉传单，以便常规分发：
“于1937年7月24日晚9点左右，在北四川路附近的狄思威路兵营失踪，据称被绑架。
日本海军陆战队总部（江湾路）一等水兵宫崎贞夫（SADAO MIYAZAKI），年龄22岁，身高5英尺3英寸，中等身材，圆脸，小眼睛，尖下巴，头顶有几处小秃斑。”

我还建议印制传单，在人力车夫等人群中分发，附上对线人的如下描述，并向提供任何有助于 locating 此人信息的人提供25美元赏金：
“年龄约21/2岁（原文如此，疑为21或22岁之误），身高5英尺3英寸，身材瘦削，面色蜡黄，细缝眼，瘦脸，身穿白色棉背心、白裤、白腰带，头戴白色网球帽。”可能为日本或韩国国籍。

鉴于最初向其提供信息的三名水手表示能够辨认出该线人，已向海军当局建议，允许他们在领事警察和工部局警务处警察的陪同下，便衣前往酒吧、咖啡馆及其他可能的场所，希望能找到该线人。当局目前正在考虑这一建议。

July 28, 1937.
3.
Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated July 27:

MYSTERIOUS AEROPLANE DROPS BOMBS AT TSENG-NYI

According to a recent arrival from Soochow,
there appeared over Soochow on the afternoon of July 26 a
mysterious aeroplane, which, after reconnoitering for some
time, flew to the vicinity of the Tseng-nyi Station (正儀站)
of the Nanking-Shanghai Line and dropped four bombs about
200 lbs each in weight. Fortunately, they fell in the
muddy fields and thus caused no casualties. The local
authorities of the district are at present conducting
enquiries into this matter.

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE SITUATION IN THE NORTHERN DISTRICT

A rumour circulated last night that the Japanese
Naval Landing Party would carry out manoeuvres caused great
alarm among the residents of Chapei, who removed into the
Settlement in large numbers. When a reporter of the
Central News Agency went to North Szechuen Road and Chapei
at midnight, however, he saw no Japanese military activities
whatever, and the situation was normal except for the
removal of the panic-stricken residents. Colonel Liang
Fu-chu, Officer in Charge of the North Station Branch Police
Bureau, asked the Commander of the Japanese Landing Party
by telephone last night as to whether there would be any
manoeuvres, and received a reply in the negative. Colonel
Liang assured the reporter last night that there need be no
anxiety for the peace and order of Shanghai, and hoped
that the people would not believe rumours and get alarmed
unnecessarily.

As a result of the complete withdrawal of Japanese
marines from various places in the afternoon of July 26,
increased calmness prevailed in Chapei and Hongkew throughout
yesterday. About 100 Japanese marines remained at the old
site of the Seya Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden on
Kiangwan Road, but this was more or less a usual sight ever
since the place was converted into a camp in spring last.
The additional men sent there following the so-called
Miyazaki case have practically been wholly withdrawn. The
military telephone line connecting the place with the
Rokusan Garden has been removed, and a large number of camp
beds have been taken out. There were no Japanese marines
at the Japanese Cemetery at Pah Za Jao (八字橋), the
Japanese Primary School on North Szechuen Road or the
Japanese Primary School for Girls on Huyang Road. Japanese
military motor-cycle patrols, however, continued to enter
Kiangwan Road and other districts under Chinese jurisdiction,
at an average of five or six times an hour.

At 11 a.m. yesterday, a Japanese armoured car,
led by a motor-cycle, was seen proceeding from North to South
at the corner of North Szechuen and Haining Roads. At the
corner of North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads and North Szechuen
and Scott Roads, a party of about 10 Japanese marines were
repairing a military telephone wire, with a large number of
pedestrians looking on.
