1937年7月28日。
3.
晨间译文。

7月27日《华美晚报》：

神秘飞机在正仪投弹

据一位刚从苏州抵达的人士称，7月26日下午，一架神秘飞机出现在苏州上空，经过一段时间的侦察后，飞至京沪铁路正仪站附近，投下四枚炸弹，每枚重约200磅。幸运的是，炸弹落在泥泞的田野中，未造成人员伤亡。该地区地方当局目前正就此事件进行调查。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

北区局势

昨晚流传着日本海军陆战队将进行演习的谣言，引起闸北居民极大恐慌，大量居民涌入租界。然而，当中央通讯社记者于午夜前往北四川路和闸北时，未发现任何日本军事活动，除了惊慌失措的居民搬迁外，局势正常。北站公安分局局长梁福柱上校昨晚通过电话询问日本陆战队指挥官是否会有演习，得到否定的答复。梁上校昨晚向记者保证，无需为上海的和平与秩序担忧，并希望民众不要轻信谣言，无谓惊慌。

由于7月26日下午日本海军陆战队从各地完全撤出，昨天一整天闸北和虹口的气氛趋于平静。约100名日本海军陆战队士兵留在江湾路六三花园后面的旧塞华啤酒厂（Seya Brewery）遗址，但这自去年春天该地改为营地以来，几乎已是寻常景象。所谓宫崎案发生后派往那里的增援部队实际上已基本全部撤走。连接该地与六三花园的军用电话线已被拆除，大量行军床也被运出。八字桥的日本墓地、北四川路的日本小学以及沪阳路（Huyang Road，音译）的日本女子小学均无日本海军陆战队士兵。然而，日本军用摩托车巡逻队继续进入江湾路及其他中国管辖区域，平均每小时五六次。

昨天上午11点，有人看到一辆由摩托车引领的日本装甲车，在北四川路与海宁路路口由北向南行驶。在北四川路与狄思威路路口，以及北四川路与斯科特路（Scott Roads，音译）路口，约10名日本海军陆战队士兵正在修理军用电话线，许多行人驻足观看。

page_data.en:
July 28, 1937.    Morning Translation.

It was reported that the Japanese marines appeared to be massing in the Western District, in view of the busy movements of trucks in that district. The fact is that Japanese marines were originally stationed in Japanese mills in the Western District, and their movements to and from there are only an ordinary occurrence.
The report that Miyazaki, the missing Japanese marine, has returned safely is being refuted by the Japanese Consulate-General.

Japanese marines are reported to be active during the night although they are no longer posted at various places during the daytime. As a result rumours are rife and the residents are deprived of peace. It is said that the Japanese marines will carry out manoeuvres to-day.

Although appeased on the surface, the situation in Shanghai remains tense in reality. The Japanese sentries posted in the Hongkew District have mostly been withdrawn, but they still come out during the night to carry out their activities.
As a result of several days' conference between local Japanese organizations such as the Japanese Residents' Corporation and the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions, it has been decided to organize a People's Police for the purpose of giving protection to the Japanese residents and watching the movements of the Chinese. Participation in the People's Police by the Japanese residents in Shanghai will be voluntary. An Intelligence Department will also be formed and connection will be maintained with the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.

Large quantities of supplies have been arriving recently from Japan for the Japanese Naval Landing Party here.
Yesterday, 650 packages of medical and electrical supplies and military instruments, about 80 military pigeons and 300 packages of sulphur were transported here on board the Japanese s.s. Tsukuba Maru and landed at Yangtsepoo. They were immediately removed to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters in motor vehicles.

China Times and other local newspapers :-

ENEMY-RESISTING ASSOCIATION ACTIVE

The Shanghai Various Circles' Enemy-Resisting Support Association started to function officially yesterday with its offices in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce building, North Soochow Road. The officials are appointed from among those of various public organizations.
A meeting of the Contribution Collection Committee of the Association will be held at 4 p.m. to-day at the Chamber of Commerce for the purpose of discussing the ways and means of raising a national salvation fund. Members of the Committee have been notified to attend.
page_data.zh:
1937年7月28日。晨间译件。

据报，鉴于该区域卡车往来频繁，日本海军陆战队似乎正在西区集结。事实是，日本海军陆战队原本就驻扎在西区的日本纱厂内，他们往返于此只是平常之事。

关于失踪的日本海军陆战队员宫崎已安全返回的报告，正遭到日本总领事馆的驳斥。

据报，日本海军陆战队在夜间活动频繁，尽管白天不再在各处布岗。因此谣言四起，居民不得安宁。据悉，日本海军陆战队将于今日进行演习。

虽然表面看来局势已平息，但上海的实际局势依然紧张。派驻虹口区的日本哨兵大多已撤回，但他们仍在夜间出来活动。

经过日本居留民团和日本街道工会联合会等当地日本组织数日的会议，决定组建一支“人民警察”，目的是保护日本居民并监视中国人的动向。上海日本居民参加“人民警察”将基于自愿原则。还将成立一个情报部门，并与日本海军陆战队总部保持联系。

最近有大量物资从日本运抵此地，供日本海军陆战队使用。
昨日，650包医疗和电气用品及军用仪器、约80只军用信鸽以及300包硫磺由日本轮船“筑波丸”号（Tsukuba Maru）运抵并在杨树浦登陆。随后立即用汽车将其转运至海军陆战队总部。

《中国时报》及其他本地报纸：

抗敌协会活跃

上海各界抗敌后援会昨日正式开始运作，办公地点设在北苏州路的中国商会大楼。其职员从各公共团体中任命。
该会募捐委员会将于今日下午4时在商会举行会议，讨论筹集救国基金的方法和途径。已通知委员会成员出席。

page_data.en:
July 27, 1937.
8024
Morning Translation 27. 7. 37.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

HONGKEW AND CHAPEI RETURN TO NORMAL

The situation in the vicinity of North Szechuen Road Extension and Chapei, which were thrown into a state of great consternation on the night of July 24 following the reported disappearance of Satao Miyazaki, a Japanese seaman, returned to normal yesterday. With the exception of the railway crossing at Tien Tung An (天通庵) where two Japanese marines stood on guard duty, all the Japanese forces stationed in the old site of the Seya Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden on Kiangwan Road, the Japanese Cemetery at Pah Sz Jao (八字桥), the Japanese Primary School on North Szechuen Road and the Japanese Primary School for Girls on Euyang Road were withdrawn between noon and 2 p.m. yesterday to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters on Kiangwan Road. Japanese patrols, either on foot or on motor cycles, were also fewer. The public were greatly relieved and the exodus nearly died down.

Despite the diligent enquiries conducted by the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau and the Shanghai Municipal Police in conjunction with the Japanese Naval Landing Party and the Japanese Consular Police, no trace has yet been found of the missing Japanese seaman. It also remains unsolved whether or not there is such a person as the so-called only eye-witness Okazaki, whose name and address cannot be confirmed.

At 11.30 a.m. yesterday, Mr. Okamoto, the Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai, called on Mr. S. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, requesting the Settlement authorities to continue to assist in the investigation. According to information given out yesterday afternoon by the Police, the missing Japanese seaman was said to have safely returned to his barracks.

On the surface, the situation in Hongkew has returned to normal, but the Japanese marines are still active. When making a tour of inspection yesterday, a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency (大公社) witnessed several military trucks fully loaded with Japanese marines in full war kit, proceeding to the western district of Shanghai by way of North Szechuen Road and Nanking Road. According to certain residents in Hongkew, a large number of Japanese marines were transferred to the Toyoda Cotton Mill in the Western District at 11.30 p.m. July 25.

About 350 Japanese marines are now in Chapei. They are concentrated in the Japanese Brewery behind Hwo Yuen Ka (花园街), where certain works are being put up. It seems that they will not be withdrawn in the near future.

The number of Japanese marines stationed in the Japanese cemetery on Tung Chi Road (同济路) was increased to about 20 yesterday. They posted sentries in the evening but refrained from unlawful acts such as the searching of pedestrians, etc.

1937年7月27日。
8024
1937年7月27日晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

虹口与闸北恢复常态

继日本水兵佐藤宫崎（Satao Miyazaki，音译）失踪消息传出后，于7月24日晚陷入极大恐慌的四川北路延伸段及闸北附近地区，于昨日恢复常态。除天通庵铁路道口有两名日本海军陆战队员站岗外，所有驻扎在江湾路六三花园背后的旧涩谷啤酒厂遗址、八字桥日本公墓、四川北路日本小学以及欧阳路日本女子小学的日军部队，均于昨日中午至下午2时之间撤至江湾路的海军陆战队总部。徒步或骑摩托车的日本巡逻队也减少了。公众大为宽慰，外逃潮几乎平息。

尽管上海市公安局警务处与上海公共租界工部局警务处联合日本海军陆战队及日本领事警察进行了勤勉调查，但仍未发现该失踪日本水兵的任何踪迹。此外，所谓唯一的目击者冈崎（Okazaki），其姓名和地址无法确认，此人是否确有其人亦未解决。

昨日上午11时30分，日本驻上海总领事冈本先生拜访了上海公共租界工部局秘书长费森登（S. Fessenden）先生，请求租界当局继续协助调查。根据警方昨日下午发布的信息，据说该失踪的日本水兵已安全返回兵营。

表面上，虹口的局势已恢复正常，但日本海军陆战队仍然活跃。《大公通讯社》的一名记者昨日巡视时目睹，几辆满载全副武装日本海军陆战队员的军用卡车，经由四川北路和南京路驶往上海西区。据虹口某些居民称，大量日本海军陆战队员于7月25日晚上11时30分被调往西区的丰田棉纺厂。

目前约有350名日本海军陆战队员在闸北。他们集中在花园街背后的日本啤酒厂，那里正在搭建某些工事。看来他们在近期不会撤离。

昨日，驻扎在同济路日本公墓的日本海军陆战队员人数增加至约20人。他们在傍晚布置了哨兵，但克制了搜查行人等非法行为。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. S. REGISTRY.
No. D. 8024
2.
July 27, 1937. Afternoon Translation 7/27

Star Daily News (明星日报) publishes the following brief comment :-

MISSING SOLDIERS, ETC. ALWAYS A PRELUDE TO FURTHER AGGRESSION

People of the certain nation are often reported missing. For example, Nakamura disappeared prior to the Mukden Incident of September 18; the disappearance of Kuramoto caused a stir in Nanking; the loss of a horse belonging to the army of the certain nation brought about the Fengtai Incident, and the disappearance of a soldier had led to an attack on the city of Wanping. Lately, Shanghai was thrown into a state of great consternation due to the reported disappearance of a member of the Naval Landing Party of the certain nation and the extensive measures taken by the marines in conducting the search and examining pedestrians.

No matter whether the disappearance is real or not, the people of the certain nation always manage to accrue benefits afterwards. Instances have shown us that they secured control of the North-East through the disappearance of Nakamura, that they occupied Fengtai for the loss of a horse, and that they are at present exercising pressure on General Sung Cheh-yuen because one of their soldiers had disappeared at Lukouchiao. For this reason, we are most afraid of the disappearance of the people of the certain nation, because the disappearance of one of them often results in the loss of our territory.

What can we do to avoid such cases? The only thing we can do is to consolidate our strength and then drive away the people of the certain nation from our country, thereby putting a stop to such incidents.

Shanghai Public Daily News (Editorial) :-

Japan is a country that lacks sincerity in her words and faithfulness in her deeds. She is at all times contemplating invading China.

Under the pretext of the disappearance in Mukden of a Japanese soldier named Nakamura and alleging that he had been murdered by the Chinese, she forcibly seized from us our North-eastern provinces. If it had not been for the strict vigilance of the Chinese Police, the disappearance in Nanking of a Japanese consul named Kuramoto would have resulted in untoward consequences, enabling Japan to realize her objectives. Thirdly and fourthly there took place in Shanghai the alleged murder by Chinese of a Japanese bluejacket named Nakayama and a Japanese civilian Kayau. Fortunately due to the careful handling of the situation on the part of both the local Chinese and Japanese authorities, Shanghai was able to evade disaster. The Lukouchiao incident which is still unsettled was provoked by the Japanese Garrison in the North under the pretext of the alleged disappearance of a Japanese soldier after manoeuvres late on the night of July 7. Now comes the alleged disappearance in Shanghai of a Japanese marine named Sadao Miyazaki.

1937年7月27日。下午译件 7/27

《明星日报》发表如下简短评论：

士兵失踪等事常为进一步侵略的前奏

某国人员经常据报道失踪。例如，九一八沈阳事变之前中村失踪；仓本（Kuramoto，音译）的失踪在南京引起轰动；某国军队丢失一匹马导致了丰台事件，而一名士兵的失踪则引发了对宛平城的攻击。最近，由于据报道某国海军陆战队一名成员失踪，且海军陆战队采取了广泛的搜索和检查行人的措施，上海陷入了极大的恐慌。

无论失踪是否属实，某国人员事后总能从中获利。实例向我们表明，他们通过中村的失踪控制了中国东北，因丢失一匹马而占领了丰台，并且目前正因一名士兵在卢沟桥失踪而对宋哲元将军施加压力。因此，我们最害怕某国人员的失踪，因为他们中一人的失踪往往导致我们领土的丧失。

我们能做些什么来避免此类情况？我们唯一能做的就是巩固我们的力量，然后将某国人员驱逐出我国，从而制止此类事件。

《上海公共日报》（社论）：

日本是一个言而无信、行而不诚的国家。她时刻都在图谋侵略中国。

以沈阳一名叫中村的日本士兵失踪并声称被中国人谋杀为借口，她强行夺取了我们的东北各省。如果不是中国警察的严密警戒，一名叫仓本的日本领事在南京的失踪本会导致不良后果，使日本得以实现其目标。第三和第四，在上海发生了据称中国人谋杀了一名叫中山（Nakayama，音译）的日本水兵和一名叫加屋（Kayau，音译）的日本平民的事件。幸运的是，由于中日地方当局谨慎处理局势，上海得以免遭灾难。尚未解决的卢沟桥事变是由北方日本驻军以7月7日深夜演习后一名日本士兵据称失踪为借口挑起的。现在又出现了上海一名叫佐藤宫崎（Sadao Miyazaki，音译）的日本海军陆战队员据称失踪的事件。

page_data.en:
July 26, 1937.
Morning Translation.
80211
26. 7. 37
Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE SO-CALLED KIDNAPPING OF A JAPANESE MARINE

Following the disappearance of a Japanese marine on the evening of July 24, the local Japanese Landing Forces mobilized. This created uneasiness among the residents in this locality. The situation became easier yesterday morning, and the sentry posts of the Japanese marines were mostly withdrawn.

The Japanese marines continued searching passengers in buses on Tung Chi Road, Chapei, on the morning of July 25. Colonel Liang Fu-tso (梁扶佐), Officer-in-Charge of the North Station Branch of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, opened negotiations over this matter and the marines abandoned the search.

There are some 20 Japanese marines and a machine gun stationed at the Japanese Cemetery at Pah Sz Jao (八字桥). Some 6 marines are stationed in the Rokusen Garden and some 100 in the Seya Wine Manufacturing Factory.

Although yesterday was Sunday, the Japanese Consulate-General opened its offices at 7 a.m. At 9 a.m. the Consul-General held a meeting with Naval Attache Honda and Rear-Admiral Okohchi, Commander of the Japanese Landing Party, to discuss the matter.

At 11.30 a.m. Mr. Okamoto, the Japanese Consul-General, accompanied by a secretary, called at the Shanghai City Government and interviewed Mr. O.K. Yui, the Acting Mayor. The Consul-General told the Acting Mayor that the Japanese authorities had no intention of enlarging the affair and that the Japanese marines had been withdrawn. He requested the Chinese authorities to avoid misunderstandings.

Mr. Yui replied that the City Government would render assistance in investigating the affair despite the fact that the case did not take place in Chinese controlled territory and expressed regret that armed Japanese marines entered Chinese controlled territory without first seeking the truth of the matter, thereby creating a tense situation. The Acting Mayor requested that the Japanese authorities should exercise vigilance in order to avoid misunderstandings. The conversation lasted about 30 minutes.

The Japanese Consul-General will call on Mr. S. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C., this morning, requesting the Council to investigate the present affair.

The Japanese Consular Police are doing their utmost to find Okazaki, the only witness in the present case. Notwithstanding efforts made in this respect throughout yesterday, it was impossible to trace the witness.

On the afternoon of July 25, the Japanese Landing Party Headquarters invited representatives of the S.M.P., the Police Bureau and the Japanese Consulate to a meeting to discuss joint measures to locate the missing marine. It was decided that the authorities communicate with one another from time to time.

Our reporter visited Hongkew, Kiangwan and Chapei yesterday for an inspection of the districts and found that the districts were quiet and returning to normal.

At 7 p.m. yesterday, Sergeant Nakayama of the Japanese Landing Party, in company with a marine, approached Tai Yang Liao Temple (太陽廟) and vicinity, Chapei, in plain clothes and inspected the areas. Fearing untoward incidents, members of the Peace Preservation Corps escorted them to the North Station Branch and Colonel Liang personally escorted them to the Japanese Landing Party Headquarters.
page_data.zh:
1937年7月26日。
晨间译件。
80211
1937年7月26日
《立报》及其他本地报纸：

所谓的日本海军陆战队员绑架案

继7月24日晚一名日本海军陆战队员失踪后，当地日本陆战队动员起来。这造成了该地区居民的不安。昨日上午局势有所缓和，日本海军陆战队的哨位大多已撤回。

7月25日上午，日本海军陆战队员继续在闸北同济路的公共汽车上搜查乘客。上海市公安局北站分局局长梁扶佐上校就此事项展开交涉，海军陆战队员遂停止搜查。

约有20名日本海军陆战队员和一挺机枪驻扎在八字桥的日本公墓。六三花园内驻扎约6名海军陆战队员，涩谷酿酒厂内驻扎约100名。

尽管昨日是星期日，日本总领事馆仍于上午7时开门办公。上午9时，总领事与海军武官本田（Honda，音译）及日本陆战队指挥官大越（Okohchi，音译）少将举行会议，讨论此事。

上午11时30分，日本总领事冈本先生在一名秘书的陪同下前往上海市政府，会见了代理市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui，音译）先生。总领事告诉代理市长，日本当局无意扩大事态，且日本海军陆战队员已撤回。他请求中国当局避免误解。

俞先生回答说，尽管案件未发生在中国管辖区域内，市政府仍将协助调查此事，并对日本海军陆战队员在未查明真相的情况下进入中国管辖区域、从而造成紧张局势表示遗憾。代理市长要求日本当局保持警惕，以避免误解。谈话持续了约30分钟。

日本总领事将于今晨拜访工部局秘书长费森登（S. Fessenden）先生，请求工部局调查当前事件。

日本领事警察正竭尽全力寻找本案唯一目击者冈崎（Okazaki）。尽管昨天为此做出了努力，但仍无法找到该目击者。

7月25日下午，日本陆战队总部邀请工部局警务处、警察局和日本领事馆的代表开会，讨论寻找失踪海军陆战队员的联合措施。决定各方不时相互沟通。

本报记者昨日视察了虹口、江湾和闸北地区，发现这些地区安静并正恢复常态。

昨晚7时，日本陆战队中士中山（Nakayama，音译）与一名海军陆战队员便衣前往闸北太阳庙及其附近地区进行视察。为防止发生意外事件，保安队成员护送他们至北站分局，梁上校亲自将他们护送至日本陆战队总部。

July 26, 1937. Morning Translation

Lih Pao publishes the following letter from one named Yung Chien-sung (榮健生) :-

Mysterious disappearance of a Japanese seaman : Government asked to handle situation firmly

"Mr. Liao Liao (33),
"Yesterday the Japanese authorities, on the pretext that one of their seamen was reported missing, detailed a large force of marines to stand duty in the district of Hongkew and to search pedestrians and vehicles. The residents in the vicinity were nervous and many of them removed their valuable property elsewhere. Up to the present, the exodus is in progress and the situation has assumed a serious aspect similar to that prevailing on the eve of the 'January 28 Incident.' However, whether or not there is any truth in the disappearance of the Japanese seaman nobody knows, and the report lacks confirmation. Such alarming measures as adopted by the Japanese authorities are excessive. Therefore, we hope that our Government will assume a stern attitude to deal with the present affair and will not seek compromise as it did in the 'January 28 Incident,' thereby allowing the Japanese to gain more ground.
"In the meantime, we hope that our Government will open negotiations demanding that the Japanese authorities refrain from posting sentries. Our residents should be told not to remove and should be made to understand that they are no safer anywhere else."

Lih Pao publishes the following comment :-

On the night of July 24, we were informed that some trouble had taken place in Chapei and that Japanese marines were detailed to stand guard at various places. What is the cause of all this? According to enquiries conducted by a reporter of this paper at various places, it is ascertained that another mysterious disappearance of a Japanese seaman had occurred.
A Japanese seaman was missing. The places where he was reported missing are three. An eye-witness of the affair said that the Japanese seaman was kidnapped by some Chinese, but up to the present this eye-witness cannot be located.
A reporter of this paper made enquiries at the place which was finally claimed by the Japanese to be the place where the Japanese seaman was missing. It was ascertained that nobody there had seen any fighting, not even a slight quarrel. Nevertheless, a Japanese seaman was abducted. The seaman must have been very amenable to his captors.
Supposing that there was actually a Japanese seaman missing, then such alarming activities of the Japanese forces by posting guards and searching pedestrians are unwarranted and have even proved futile. Would a kidnapper loiter on the streets awaiting to be picked up by the Japanese marines?

《立报》刊登了一封署名为荣健生（Yung Chien-sung）的来信：—

日本水兵神秘失踪：要求政府坚决处理局势

“廖廖先生（33），
“昨日，日本当局以一名水兵报告失踪为借口，派遣大量海军陆战队在虹口区执勤，并搜查行人和车辆。附近居民人心惶惶，许多人将贵重财物转移至他处。截至目前，外逃仍在进行，局势已呈现出与‘一·二八事变’前夕相似的严峻态势。然而，日本水兵是否真的失踪，无人知晓，该报道缺乏证实。日本当局采取的此类令人惊恐的措施实属过度。因此，我们希望我国政府能以严厉态度处理当前事件，不要像‘一·二八事变’那样寻求妥协，从而让日本得寸进尺。
“同时，我们希望我国政府展开谈判，要求日本当局停止设置哨兵。应告知我国居民不要搬迁，并使他们明白，他们在其他地方并不更安全。”

《立报》发表如下评论：—

7月24日晚，我们获悉闸北发生了一些骚乱，日本海军陆战队被派往各处站岗。这一切的起因是什么？据本报记者在多处调查，查明又发生了一起日本水兵神秘失踪事件。
一名日本水兵失踪。报告其失踪的地点有三处。该事件的一名目击者称，该日本水兵被一些中国人绑架，但截至目前，无法找到这名目击者。
本报记者在日本人最终声称该日本水兵失踪的地点进行了查询。经查实，那里没有人看到任何打斗，甚至没有轻微的争吵。尽管如此，一名日本水兵却被绑架了。这名水兵对其绑架者一定非常顺从。
假设确实有一名日本水兵失踪，那么日军通过设岗和搜查行人所进行的这些令人惊恐的活动是毫无道理的，甚至已被证明是徒劳的。绑架者会在街上闲逛，等待被日本海军陆战队抓获吗？

Therefore, if the Japanese do not intend to
provoke trouble by means of a pretext, then such activities
are virtually meaningless.
It is our opinion that to deal with such
activities of the Japanese, the authorities and civilians
of this locality should adopt a calm and stern attitude.
Our Government should first protest against
the unwarranted activities of the Japanese marines and ask
them to produce concrete evidence to confirm the disappearance
of a Japanese seaman. We can promise to assist them in the
search for the man, but we cannot accept any responsibility,
because the man is a living person and we have no means to
accept responsibility for him. The disappearance of Mr.
Kuramoto, Japanese Vice-Consul in Nanking, may serve as a
good explanation.
Our civilians residing in Chapei should not
be alarmed and should not give the Japanese a chance to
provide a pretext. We should keep in mind that to-day we
have only to remain calm and firm. It is useless to remove
our homes and all of us have to make up our minds to prepare
for the supreme sacrifice.

Chun Chung Sin Wan (群众新闻) dated July 25 :-

A Stray Japanese Marine

On the night before last (July 25), a Chinese
policeman attached to the North Station Branch Police Bureau
saw a Japanese wearing Chinese clothes loitering at Wang
Pang Bridge (横浜桥).
The policeman brought the man to the Branch
Bureau where, upon questioning by Mr. Liang Fu-chu (梁扶初),
the Officer in charge, it was revealed that the Japanese,
named M. Yoshida, was a marine of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party and had lost his way whilst looking for a Japanese
brothel.
Mr. Liang detailed a policeman to escort the
Japanese marine to the Landing Party Headquarters.

Ta Kung Pao (Taiyuan telegram):

GANG OF JAPANESE ASSAULT POLICE IN TAIYUAN

Recently, on finding that one, Mizutani, who
was driving a motor car for Mr. Gochu from the latter's
residence on Hsin Chen Ka Street (新城街), Taiyuan, Shanse,
did not possess a Driver's Licence, a Chinese policeman on
post duty there immediately tried to persuade the Japanese
driver to stop, but without result. On July 24, the
Japanese drove his motor car out again, and the policeman
further asked him to refrain from driving on, after the
officer had found that the Japanese was once more not in
possession of a Driver's Licence.
Mizutani drove back his car, and soon afterwards,
he and six others went up to the Sub-Station of the Chinese
Police there and attempted to drag Sergeant Kwoh Ts-li
to the Japanese residence. When Zi Shih-tseng, the Sub-
Inspector, mediated, Mizutani and the others assaulted the
police and in consequence, the Sub-Inspector, the Sergeant
and several policemen were injured, and the window panes
of the Station were damaged. Mizutani and the others then
withdrew.
The Police Bureau at Taiyuan has made a
report on the matter to the Pacification Commissioner's
Headquarters and the Provincial Government.

因此，如果日本人不打算借故制造事端，那么此类活动实际上毫无意义。
我们认为，为了应对日本的此类活动，本地当局和民众应采取冷静而严厉的态度。
我国政府应首先抗议日本海军陆战队的无理行动，并要求他们提供确凿证据以证实日本水兵失踪一事。我们可以承诺协助他们寻找此人，但我们不能承担任何责任，因为此人是活人，我们无法为其承担责任。日本驻南京副领事仓本（Kuramoto）先生的失踪可作为很好的解释。
居住在闸北的我国民众不应惊慌，不应给日本人提供借口的机会。我们要记住，今天我们要做的只是保持冷静和坚定。搬迁家园是无用的，我们大家都要下定决心，准备做出最大的牺牲。

7月25日《群众新闻》（Chun Chung Sin Wan）：—

一名迷路的日本海军陆战队员

前晚（7月25日），北站分局警察局的一名中国警察看到一名身穿中式服装的日本人在横浜桥（Wang Pang Bridge）徘徊。
警察将该男子带到分局，经负责人梁扶初（Liang Fu-chu）先生讯问后，得知该日本人名为吉田（M. Yoshida），是日本海军陆战队的一名水兵，在寻找一家日本妓院时迷了路。
梁先生派了一名警察护送这名日本海军陆战队员前往陆战队总部。

《大公报》（太原电）：

日本团伙在太原袭击警察

近日，在山西太原新城街（Hsin Chen Ka Street）谷楚（Gochu，音译）先生住所，发现为其驾驶汽车的日本人水谷（Mizutani）没有驾驶执照，当地执勤的中国警察立即试图劝阻该日本司机停车，但未果。7月24日，该日本人再次驾车外出，警官发现该日本人再次未持有驾驶执照后，进一步要求其停止驾驶。
水谷将车开回，不久后，他与另外六人前往当地中国警察分局，企图将郭子力（Kwoh Ts-li，音译）警长拖至日本人的住所。当副巡官石子增（Zi Shih-tseng，音译）进行调解时，水谷等人袭击了警察，导致副巡官、警长和几名警察受伤，分局的玻璃窗也被损坏。随后水谷等人撤离。
太原警察局已就此事项向绥靖公署和省政府报告。

July 26, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Shanghai Kwangtung Pao (上海廣東報) publishes the following editorial comment :-

HOW TO DEAL WITH THE LATEST SHANGHAI INCIDENT

While the situation in North China is still tense, the so-called disappearance of a Japanese seaman took place in Shanghai on the night of July 24. The Japanese Landing Party in Shanghai took extraordinary steps and detailed marines to stand duty in the districts of Hongkew, Chapei and Kiangwan as a precautionary measure. This threw the whole of Shanghai into a state of alarm similar to that prevailing on the eve of the "January 28 Incident." This action of the Japanese marines is really deplorable.

"Soldier missing," "horse missing," "murder," "bridge protection," etc. are nothing but old tricks of the people of the "friendly nation" intended to manufacture a cause to start aggression on baseless pretexts. The Fengtai Incident, the Lukouchiao Incident and many other disputes in the various parts of China in the past all come under the preceding category. The aggressors have a fixed and premeditated scheme against us. The present incident of the disappearance of a Japanese seaman is of course not accidental.

The chief reasons why the Japanese wish to cause the present unrest are as follows :-
(1) The Lukouchiao Incident has aroused a unanimous and strong reaction from our government and people and this reaction is undoubtedly a severe blow to the aggressors. For this reason, the Japanese fabricate other disputes for the purpose of distracting the attention of our government and people from the events in North China, thereby facilitating the local talks for their domination of North China or conversion of the provinces of Hopei and Charhar into special areas.
(2) Shanghai is the financial and cultural centre of China and also occupies a very important position in the war of resistance of to-day. Therefore, the Japanese take the chance to create disturbance in Shanghai in the hope of routing our battle line of resistance.
(3) By this affair, the Japanese intend to test the attitude and the strength of defence of our military and civil authorities, so that they can make preparations for the occupation of Shanghai and exercise pressure on Nanking and Hangchow in time of need.

Since we are fully aware that the occurrence of the present affair is not accidental but premeditated, we have no difficulty in imagining its close connections with the development of events in the North. In short, the present Shanghai affair is a part of the Japanese scheme to encroach upon us. Even if the present affair quietens down temporarily, there is a possibility of its being re-enacted at any moment.

At this time of crisis, the attitude of our authorities and civilians is very important. In our opinion, the authorities responsible for peace and order in this locality should manifest a strong stand; on one

《上海广东报》发表如下社论：—

如何应对最新的上海事件

尽管华北局势依然紧张，但所谓的日本水兵失踪事件于7月24日晚发生在上海。驻上海的日本海军陆战队采取了非同寻常的措施，派遣海军陆战队员在虹口、闸北和江湾地区执勤，作为预防措施。这使得整个上海陷入了一种与“一·二八事变”前夕相似的恐慌状态。日本海军陆战队的这一行动实在令人遗憾。

“士兵失踪”、“马匹失踪”、“谋杀”、“保护桥梁”等不过是“友邦”人士制造无端侵略借口的老套路。丰台事件、卢沟桥事件以及过去中国各地的许多其他争端都属于前述类别。侵略者对我们有着固定且预谋的方案。此次日本水兵失踪事件当然不是偶然的。

日本希望造成当前动荡的主要原因如下：
(1) 卢沟桥事件引起了我国政府和人民一致而强烈的反应，这一反应无疑是对侵略者的沉重打击。为此，日本制造其他争端，目的是分散我国政府和人民对华北事件的注意力，从而便于其通过地方会谈主宰华北，或将河北和察哈尔省份变为特殊区域。
(2) 上海是中国的金融和文化中心，在当今的抗战中也占据着非常重要的地位。因此，日本趁机在上海制造骚乱，希望摧毁我们的抗战防线。
(3) 通过此事，日本意图试探我国军政当局的态度和防御力量，以便为占领上海做准备，并在需要时对南京和杭州施加压力。

既然我们充分认识到当前事件的发生并非偶然，而是预谋已久的，我们不难想象其与北方事态发展的密切联系。简而言之，当前的上海事件是日本侵华方案的一部分。即使当前事件暂时平息，也有可能随时重演。

在这一危机时刻，我国当局和民众的态度非常重要。我们认为，负责本地治安的当局应表现出强硬的立场；一方面

水兵失踪是进一步制造事端的借口

尽管中国当局不断采取预防措施，但我们的敌人再次大惊小怪。关于7月24日晚发生的滋扰事件（据报道一名名为宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）的日本水兵失踪），甚至连我们的敌人自己也未能确定犯罪现场。
据本报记者获得的消息，我们的敌人在收到所谓海军陆战队成员失踪的报告后，立即派遣大量武装海军陆战队员巡逻上海市管辖下的各区，甚至开枪射击。我们的敌人这样做的目的和意图是侦察中国军事力量，并鼓励其制造事件。
事实上，我们的敌人已经雇佣了一些汉奸监视沪杭铁路沿线各地。因此，如果我们中国人仍然保持冷静而不关注局势，那就为时已晚了。

July 25, 1937. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

ANOTHER INCIDENT IN HONGKEW: JAPANESE SEAMAN ALLEGED
KIDNAPPED

Alleging that a Japanese marine named Satao Miyazaki was missing, the Japanese Naval Landing Party last night turned out in full force to keep guard in the Hongkew area. Pedestrians were searched and the situation took on an aspect no less serious than in the past incidents. The residents, as a result of the tense atmosphere accompanied by various rumours, were thrown into a great turmoil.

According to a Japanese statement, S. Miyazaki, a first class seaman of the Naval Landing Party, aged 25, became involved in a quarrel with certain Chinese while passing the Japanese Cooperative Society, corner of North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads, at 9.30 p.m. yesterday. A motor car arrived at that time and Miyazaki was taken away in it to an unknown destination. A Japanese named Okazaki, who gave his address as 80 Woosung Road and stated that he saw Miyazaki being involved in a fight and that he had picked up a uniform cap and a tie dropped by Miyazaki, made a report to a Japanese marine named Yanagida whom he met on the road. Yanagida thereupon telephoned from the Uchiyama Bookstore to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters. The Japanese marine also requested Okazaki to accompany him to Headquarters, but Okazaki refused to go on the ground that his mother was seriously ill. He left the marine shortly afterwards.

Upon receiving news about the above mentioned affair, Messrs. Okamoto and Yoshioka, Japanese Consul-General and Consul respectively, called on Rear Admiral Okohchi, Officer Commanding the Japanese Naval Landing Party, at the Landing Party Headquarters at 11 p.m. and held a discussion with him. At the same time, the whole Landing Party was mobilized and armed sentinels were sent to North Szechuen Road, Dixwell Road, Scott Road, Kiangwan Road and Darroch Road. Pedestrians were arbitrarily searched by the marines.

Our reporter made a tour of Hongkew at 11 p.m. and found that the number of both the Settlement and the Chinese Police on post duty in the area had been increased. North Szechuen Road and vicinity, however, presented a noisy and bustling air as usual.

Twenty marines were stationed in the middle of the street at the Wang Pang Bridge (横浜桥), while more than twenty others assisted by Japanese detectives of the Shanghai Municipal Police, searched all vehicles and pedestrians passing the spot, with the exception of those passengers or pedestrians who spoke Japanese. Japanese marines were also posted on other roads. A tense atmosphere thus prevailed in the district.

Three different Japanese reports were current last night concerning the scene of the incident; one stated that the affair took place outside the Nippon Commercial Union on Woosung Road, another said it was outside the Japanese Cooperative Society at the corner of North Szechuen

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

虹口又起事端：日籍水兵据称遭绑架

日本海军陆战队声称一名名为宫崎佐太郎（Satao Miyazaki）的日本水兵失踪，昨晚全员出动，在虹口地区警戒。行人受到搜查，局势之严峻不亚于以往各次事件。居民因紧张气氛及各种谣言而陷入极大恐慌。

据日方声明，海军陆战队一等水兵宫崎佐太郎，25岁，于昨晚9时30分途经北四川路与狄思威路（Dixwell Road）拐角处的日本协同组合时，与若干中国人发生争吵。当时有一辆汽车抵达，宫崎被带往不明目的地。一名自称住在吴淞路80号、名为冈崎（Okazaki）的日本人向他在路上遇到的一名名为柳田（Yanagida）的日本水兵报告，称他目睹宫崎卷入斗殴，并捡到了宫崎掉落的一顶制服帽和一条领带。柳田随即从内山书店打电话给海军陆战队总部。该日本水兵还要求冈崎随他前往总部，但冈崎以母亲病重为由拒绝前往。他不久后便离开了该水兵。

获悉上述事件消息后，日本总领事冈本（Okamoto）先生和领事吉冈（Yoshioka）先生于晚上11时前往海军陆战队总部，拜访了日本海军陆战队指挥官大越（Okohchi）少将，并与他进行了讨论。与此同时，整个陆战队动员起来，武装哨兵被派往北四川路、狄思威路、斯科特路（Scott Road）、江湾路和达罗路（Darroch Road）。水兵任意搜查行人。

本报记者于晚上11时巡视虹口，发现该地区值勤的租界巡捕和中国警察人数均已增加。然而，北四川路及其附近仍像往常一样喧闹繁忙。

二十名水兵驻守在横浜桥（Wang Pang Bridge）路中央，另有二十多名水兵在上海公共租界工部局警务处日本侦探的协助下，搜查经过该处的所有车辆和行人，但讲日语的乘客或行人除外。其他道路上也部署了日本水兵。因此，该地区弥漫着紧张的气氛。

昨晚流传着三种不同的日方报告，涉及事发地点；一种说法称事件发生在吴淞路的日本商业联合会外面，另一种说法称发生在北四川路

July 25, 1937.    2.    Morning Translation.

and Dixwell Roads, and the third said it occurred on
Tien Tung An Road (天通庵路). The Japanese finally
concluded, after 11 p.m., that the second report was
correct.
Our reporter then went to make enquiries in
the vicinity of the Japanese Cooperative Society. The
houses nearby were mostly Japanese shops and residences.
The people in the Yung An Garage (永安汽車行), which is
situated opposite the Japanese Cooperative Society, stated
that they did not see any fighting on the street at 9.30 p.m.
The place was in the extra-Settlement road area and policemen
of both the Settlement and the Chinese Police were on duty
at the place. According to an officer of the Dixwell
Road Police Station, the Chinese policeman on duty at the
corner of North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads at 9.30 p.m.
reported that he did not see any fight at that time. The
reporter also learned from Inspector Chang Zing-hai (張靜海)
of the Tsing Ih Li (精一里) Alleyway Sub-Station of the
Police Bureau that the Chinese policeman, named Yeu Hu
(尤虎), who was on duty at the corner of Chang Tsung
Road (長春路) and North Szechuen Road, on the left of the
Japanese Cooperative Society, did not see or hear any
fighting at all. People in the shops and pedestrians
in the vicinity also said that they had no knowledge what-
ever of the fighting.
Enquiries made by the Chinese Police authori-
ties likewise showed that there was no fighting between
a Japanese marine and Chinese as alleged by the Japanese.
Not only was Miyazaki reported to be missing
last night, but Okazaki, the informer and witness of the
alleged incident, also could not be found again after he
made the report to Japanese marine Yanagida. Yanagida
stated that Okazaki wore white trousers and a sports
shirt, and lived at Woosung Road, but the occupants of
80 Woosung Road told the Landing Party that no such person
lived there.
Upon receipt of the news of the aforementioned
occurrence, Mr. O.K. Yui, the Acting Mayor, communicated
with Mr. Okamoto, the Japanese Consul-General, to whom he
suggested that investigations should be made as to whether
the report relating to the missing Japanese bluejacket was
true or not. Mr. Yui also informed Mr. Okamoto that the
Shanghai City Government would render assistance in
conducting investigations, but as the movements of the
Japanese Landing Party would cause great excitement among
the local inhabitants and affect peace and order in this
locality, he asked Mr. Okamoto to prevent the Japanese
Landing Party from continuing their movements.
In reply, Mr. Okamoto explained that the
movements of the Japanese Landing Party were due to the
adoption of precautionary measures, and asked the Chinese
not to entertain any misunderstanding. He also requested
Mr. Yui to render assistance in enquiring about the missing
bluejacket.
While walking along East Wang Pang Road (東橫浜路)
at 11 p.m. last night in plain clothes, Mr. Lieu Lai-pu
(劉來浦), a police officer attached to the North Station
Branch of the Police Bureau, was arrested by Japanese
marines because he was in possession of a pistol. He was
released at 12 midnight at the request of Mr. Liang Fu-chu,
Chief of the North Station Branch Police Bureau.

与狄思威路拐角处的日本协同组合外面，第三种说法称发生在天通庵路（Tien Tung An Road）。日本人在晚上11时后最终认定第二种报告是正确的。
本报记者随后前往日本协同组合附近查询。附近的房屋多为日本商店和住宅。位于日本协同组合对面的永安汽车行（Yung An Garage）的人员表示，他们在晚上9时30分未看到街上有任何打斗。该地点位于越界筑路区域，租界巡捕和中国警察均在此处值勤。据狄思威路捕房一名警官称，晚上9时30分在北四川路与狄思威路拐角处值勤的中国警察报告说，当时未看到任何打斗。记者还从警察局精一里（Tsing Ih Li）弄堂分所的张静海（Chang Zing-hai）巡长处获悉，在日本协同组合左侧、长春路（Chang Tsung Road）与北四川路拐角处值勤的名为尤虎（Yeu Hu）的中国警察，根本未看到或听到任何打斗。附近的店员和行人也表示，他们对打斗一事毫不知情。
中国警方当局的调查同样显示，并未发生日方所称的日本水兵与中国人之间的打斗。
不仅宫崎据称于昨晚失踪，而且据称事件的举报人和目击者冈崎在向日本水兵柳田报告后也再次下落不明。柳田称冈崎身穿白裤子和运动衫，住在吴淞路，但吴淞路80号的住户告诉陆战队，那里并没有此人居住。
接到上述事件的消息后，代理市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）先生与日本总领事冈本先生取得联系，建议调查关于日本水兵失踪的报告是否属实。俞先生还告知冈本先生，上海市政府将协助进行调查，但由于日本陆战队的行动会引起当地居民的极大恐慌并影响该地区的和平与秩序，他请冈本先生阻止日本陆战队继续行动。
作为回应，冈本先生解释说，日本陆战队的行动是出于采取预防措施的需要，并请中方不要产生任何误解。他还请求俞先生协助查询失踪水兵的下落。
昨晚11时，警察局北站分局警官刘来浦（Lieu Lai-pu）先生身着便衣沿东横浜路（East Wang Pang Road）行走时，因携带手枪被日本水兵逮捕。经警察局北站分局局长梁福初（Liang Fu-chu）先生请求，他于午夜12时被释放。

July 27, 1937.

NIPPO

JAPANESE FLAG INSULTED:CHINESE EMPLOYEES KIDNAPPED:
JAPANESE AUTHORITIES DRAW ATTENTION OF SHANGHAI
CITY GOVERNMENT

In connection with the insult
to the Japanese flag and the kidnapping of two Chinese
employees of the Seibi Noen, a truck farm of Shuitcn Road,
Kiangwan, by Chinese, Chancellor Fukui of the Japanese
Consulate-General, at 3.30 p.m. July 26 called on Mr. Chou,
Secretary of the Shanghai City Government, drew his
attention to the affair and requested him to arrest the
persons responsible for the incident.
The Japanese Consular Police
requested the Chinese Police Bureau to effect the release
of the two Chinese employees of the Seibi Noen who were
kidnapped at 8 p.m. July 22 by the members of the Peace
Preservation Corps.

THE MIYAZAKI INCIDENT

In connection with the mystery
surrounding the disappearance of Miyazaki on the night
of July 24 various rumours are being circulated but none
of them is reliable. The investigation headquarters
of the Naval Landing Party is receiving numerous reports,
but most of them are based on guess work.
The Headquarters will hold
meetings at 9 a.m. , 3 p.m. and 9 p.m. daily from July 26
with officers concerned in the case to exchange opinions
and information for further investigation.
It is reported that on the
night of July 26 the area of investigation was narrowed
and it is expected that within a few days the key to the
case will be obtained.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE EMERGENCY COMMITTEE FORMED

The situation in the North has
again become grave as a result of illegal firing on
Japanese soldiers by Chinese troops at Langfang. Japanese
residents in Shanghai are much worried about the development
of the new incident. The Japanese Consular authorities,
the S.M.P. and the French Police are making every effort
to suppress harmful rumours and anti-Japanese terrorists
and to prevent recurrence of unhappy incidents. Japanese
residents are exercising great care not to cause any
trouble with Chinese. Especially are they adopting a
calm attitude with a careful watch on the development of
the situation. However the Japanese residents have been
considering the formation of an emergency committee in
case of further trouble.

1937年7月27日。

《日本新闻》（NIPPO）

侮辱日本国旗：中国雇员遭绑架：
日本当局提请上海市政府注意

就侮辱日本国旗以及江湾水电路（Shuitcn Road）Seibi Noen 卡车农场的两名中国雇员被中国人绑架一事，日本总领事馆副领事福井（Fukui）于7月26日下午3时30分拜访了上海市政府秘书周先生，提请其注意此事，并要求逮捕对此事件负责的人员。
日本领事警察请求中国警察局释放于7月22日晚8时被保安团成员绑架的 Seibi Noen 的两名中国雇员。

宫崎事件

就7月24日晚宫崎失踪之谜，各种谣言流传，但均不可靠。海军陆战队调查总部收到大量报告，但大多基于猜测。
自7月26日起，总部将于每天上午9时、下午3时和晚上9时举行会议，与案件相关人员交换意见和信息，以便进一步调查。
据报道，7月26日晚调查范围已缩小，预计几天内将获得破案关键。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

成立日本紧急委员会

由于中国军队在廊坊非法向日军士兵开火，北方局势再次变得严峻。在上海的日本居民对新事态的发展深感忧虑。日本领事当局、上海公共租界工部局警务处和法国警察正竭尽全力遏制有害谣言和反日恐怖分子，并防止不幸事件再次发生。日本居民格外小心，以免与中国人发生任何纠纷。特别是他们保持冷静态度，密切关注事态发展。然而，日本居民一直在考虑，若发生进一步麻烦，则成立一个紧急委员会。

July 27, 1937.

At 4.30 p.m. July 26 the
representatives of the Japanese Consulate-General, the
Japanese Navy and Army authorities, the Japanese Residents'
Corporation, the Japanese Chamber of Commerce, the Japanese
Cotton Mill Owners' Association, and the Japanese
Amalgamated Association of Street Unions held a meeting
at the Japanese Club and formed an emergency Committee.
Mr. Okamoto, Japanese Consul-General, was elected Chairman
of the Committee. After discussing the present situation
the meeting closed at 5.30 p.m. The object of the
Committee is to give proper protection to Japanese
residents in case of further trouble and the Committee
was not formed in expectation of the worst.

FRESH ANTI-JAPANESE INCIDENTS ARISE

Since the outbreak of the
Lukouchiao incident the anti-Japanese feelings among the
Chinese in Shanghai have been running high and have led up
to the Miyazaki incident. This is followed by an insult
to the Japanese flag by the Chinese, thus aggravating
anti-Japanese feelings. The members of the Peace
Preservation Corps have been holding exercises every night.
It is reported that 6 Chinese
who are reported to be ex-employees of the N.Y.K. were
arrested by members of the Peace Preservation Corps in
the vicinity of the City Government about a week ago for
being in the employ of Japanese. They were sent to the
Chinese Police Bureau which has maintained great secrecy
about the case. The Chinese are reported to be still
under arrest.

1937年7月27日。

7月26日下午4时30分，日本总领事馆、日本海陆军当局、日本居留民团、日本商会、日本棉纺同业公会和日本街道工会联合会的代表在日本俱乐部举行会议，成立了一个紧急委员会。日本总领事冈本先生当选为委员会主席。会议讨论了当前局势，于下午5时30分结束。委员会的宗旨是在发生进一步麻烦时给予日本居民适当保护，成立该委员会并非预期最坏情况的发生。

新的反日事件发生

自卢沟桥事变爆发以来，上海中国人的反日情绪高涨，并导致了宫崎事件。随后又发生了中国人侮辱日本国旗的事件，从而加剧了反日情绪。保安团成员每晚都在进行演习。
据报道，约一周前，6名据称为前日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）雇员的中国人在市政府附近因受雇于日本人而被保安团成员逮捕。他们被送往中国警察局，该局对此案严加保密。据报道，这些中国人目前仍被拘押。

NIPPO

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES ENQUIRE INTO MIYAZAKI INCIDENT:
INFORMER OKAZAKI MUST BE LOCATED

At 8 p.m. July 25 Admiral
Okohchi, Adjutant officer Fukumi, of the Naval Landing
Party, Mr. Matsuyama, officer in charge of the information
section, Assistant Naval Attache Okino, Mr. Kitamura,
Chief of the Japanese Consular Police, Mr. Tajima, officer
in charge of the First Section, Mr. Okumura, officer
in charge of the Judicial section of the Japanese Consular
Police, Deputy Commissioner Uyehara, Assistant Commissioner
Kakegawa, Superintendent Kasumi, of the S.M.P., and
Captain Tsukamoto, officer in charge of the local Japanese
Military Police, held a conference at the Naval Landing
Party Headquarters to discuss ways and means of furthering
the investigation into the kidnapping of Miyazaki. The
authorities are basing their investigation on two theories;
namely that the man may be still detained alive at a
certain place or he may have been murdered.
Miyazuki is reported to have
been a model sailor when at the Kure Naval Base. He
has served four years this May and since the arrived in
Shanghai he has been sending Yen 25 to his home every
month out of his salary of Yen 35. Therefore there is
no ground for saying that he has concealed himself as
is stated in certain Chinese quarters.
Adjutant Fukumi of the Naval
Landing Party states that the first thing to do is to
locate Okazaki as through him the truth of the incident
can be learned. It is difficult to say whether a person
called Okazaki really exists or not, but it is clear-
that some one stated his name was Okazaki. The
headquarters of the investigation has decided to make
an organized enquiry with the assistance of various
authorities as it is inconvenient for the individual
organs to conduct separate investigations.

IS THE ELUSIVE INFORMER A KOREAN?

The Japanese Consular Police
and the S.M.P. are making exhaustive investigations to
locate Okazaki, but so far no clues have been obtained.
The Japanese Street Unions are assisting the police in the
investigation but without success.
As it is thought that Okazaki
may be a Korean, the 2nd Section of the Japanese Consular
Police have made thorough investigations among Koreans
but without success. However the Section is continuing
further investigation in that direction.

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES TO SUPPRESS RUMOURS

Since the report of the Miyazaki
incident various rumours have been circulated among
Japanese residents. The Japanese Naval Landing Party

《日日新闻》

日本当局调查宫崎事件：
必须找到线人冈崎

7月25日晚8时，海军陆战队司令大角（Okohchi）海军上将、副官福见（Fukumi）中尉、情报科科长松山（Matsuyama）先生、海军助理武官奥野（Okino）先生、日本领事警察署长北村（Kitamura）先生、第一课课长田岛（Tajima）先生、日本领事警察司法科科长奥村（Okumura）先生、工部局警务处副总巡捕上原（Uyehara）、助理总巡捕挂川（Kakegawa）、警司霞（Kasumi），以及当地日本宪兵队负责人塚本（Tsukamoto）队长，在海军陆战队总部举行会议，讨论推进宫崎绑架案调查的方法与途径。当局的调查基于两种推测；即此人可能仍被活囚于某处，或者可能已被谋杀。
据报道，宫崎（Miyazuki）在吴淞海军基地服役期间是一名模范水兵。他于今年五月服役满四年，自抵达上海以来，每月从35日元的薪水中寄25日元回家。因此，某些中方人士所称其潜逃的说法毫无根据。
海军陆战队副官福见表示，首要任务是找到冈崎，因为通过他可以了解事件的真相。很难说是否真有一个名叫冈崎的人存在，但显然有人声称自己名叫冈崎。调查总部决定在各有关当局的协助下进行有组织的查询，因为各个机构分别进行调查多有不便。

 elusive 线人是朝鲜人吗？

日本领事警察和工部局警务处正在进行全面调查以寻找冈崎，但迄今未获任何线索。日本街道联合会正在协助警方调查，但未有成效。
由于认为冈崎可能是朝鲜人，日本领事警察第二课已在朝鲜人中进行了彻底调查，但未有成效。然而，该课正继续朝此方向进行深入调查。

日本当局将压制谣言

自宫崎事件报道以来，各种谣言在日本侨民中流传。日本海军陆战队

authorities are desirous that Japanese residents should
exercise great care, and they will suppress rumour mongers
with the assistance of the Japanese Consular authorities.

OKAZAKI SUSPECTED AGENT OF TERRORIST GANG

As regards the true identity
of Okazaki who gave the information of the Miyazaki
incident, the authorities concerned are faced with
difficulties and many theories have been advanced. Judging
from the information collected by the authorities and
the theories advanced by the general public, the informer
Okazaki is believed to be connected with the kidnappers
and he may have deliberately given the information in
order to complicate matters. The incident is believed
to have been well planned. For this reason, Okazaki is
believed to be an agent of a terrorist gang.

NICHI-NICHI

FOREIGN AMBASSADORS ENCOURAGING NANKING TO RESIST
JAPAN

A special telegram from Nanking
reports that as it is feared that the situation in the
North may become worse , the American , Italian, German
and French Ambassadors are returning to Nanking from July
24. The British and Soviet Ambassadors returned to
Nanking earlier than the other Ambassadors in order to
begin their diplomatic activities. The Ambassadors are
reported to be instigating the National Government to
put up resistance against Japan with a view to checking
Japanese influence.

Paying close attention to the
activities of the Ambassadors, Mr.Hitaka, Counsellor of
the Japanese Embassy, twice called on the British Ambassador
on July 25 to exchange opinions over the present situation
and to explain Japan's attitude. Mr. Hitaka will
call on the American, French, German, Soviet and Italian
Ambassadors to-night or to-morrow for the same purpose.

THE SEARCH FOR OKAZAKI;WAITRESS QUESTIONED

Acting on information that last
year a Japanese whose description tallies with that of
Okazaki was escorted here from Hankow, the local Japanese
authorities examined the passenger lists of the N.K.K.
steamers for last year but the name Okazaki could not
be found. Certain quarters advanced the theory that the
informer may be leading a double life. The Japanese
authorities with the assistance of the French Police and
the Chinese Police Bureau are keeping a watch on various
wharves and stations.

At 4 p.m. yesterday the Japanese
Consular Police summoned a Japanese waitress named Shigeko
Maeta, age 24 , of the Shanghai Club in Mei-Mi Li alleyway

当局希望日本侨民格外谨慎，并将借助日本领事当局的力量镇压造谣者。

冈崎涉嫌为恐怖团伙代理人

关于提供宫崎事件信息的冈崎的真实身份，有关当局面临困难，并提出了多种推测。根据当局收集的信息和公众提出的推测，线人冈崎被认为与绑匪有关联，他可能是为了 complicating matters（使事态复杂化）而故意提供信息。据信该事件是经过周密策划的。因此，冈崎被认为是一个恐怖团伙的代理人。

《日日新闻》

外国大使鼓励南京抵抗日本

来自南京的特电报道称，由于担心华北局势可能恶化，美国、意大利、德国和法国大使将于7月24日起返回南京。英国和苏联大使比其他大使更早返回南京，以便开始其外交活动。据报道，这些大使正在煽动国民政府抵抗日本，以遏制日本的影响。

日本大使馆参事日高（Hitaka）先生密切关注大使们的活动，于7月25日两次拜访英国大使，就当前局势交换意见并解释日本的立场。日高先生将于今晚或明天出于同样目的拜访美国、法国、德国、苏联和意大利大使。

搜寻冈崎；女侍应受讯问

根据去年有一名体貌特征与冈崎相符的日本人从汉口被护送至上海的情报，当地日本当局查阅了去年日清汽船株式会社（N.K.K.）轮船的乘客名单，但未找到冈崎的名字。某些方面提出推测，认为该线人可能过着双重生活。日本当局在法国警察和中国警察局的协助下，正在监视各个码头和车站。

昨日下午4时，日本领事警察传唤了一名名为前田茂子（Shigeko Maeta）的日本女侍应，年龄24岁，系位于王胖桥附近美美里弄堂上海俱乐部的雇员

JAPANESE AMALGAMATED ASSOCIATION OF STREET UNIONS
HOLDS MEETING

At 2 p.m. July 25 the Standing
Committee of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of
Street Unions held an emergency meeting to exchange

development of the affair as desired by the Consular

CHINESE MERCHANT VOLUNTEER CORPS THREATEN CHINESE
EMPLOYEE OF JAPANESE FIRM

It is reported that at 10 a.m.
July 23 a Chinese named Tang Yao-sung, employee of the
Japanese Benzine Cleaning shop No. 120 Meichow Road,
entered Chinese controlled territory at Yangtszepoo in
a motor car, when several members of the Chinese Merchant
Volunteer Corps surrounded him and said, "Are you working
with Japanese? From to-day we will shoot and kill anyone
who works in a Japanese shop."
The Chinese employee made good
his escape.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES REQUEST JAPANESE RESIDENTS
TO MAINTAIN CAREFUL ATTITUDE

It is reported that the Japanese
authorities are desirous of having Japanese residents
maintain a careful attitude, as small matters may develop
into serious affairs owing to the present disturbed
situation prevailing in this part of China as a result
of the northern incident.

SECRET SOCIETY MEMBERS HOLD MEETING AT MOON
PALACE HOTEL ON THE NIGHT OF
MIYAZAKI INCIDENT

The activities of the local
secret societies are being watched carefully by the
authorities concerned since the Miyazaki incident. The
Police have ascertained that several members of a certain
secret society held a meeting at the Moon Palace Hotel on
the night of the Miyazaki incident. It has not yet been
ascertained whether the meeting was connected with the
incident or not, but it is a significant fact that the
accused in the Nakayama murder case used the Moon Palace
as their meeting place and the accused in the Kayau murder
case used the Jukong Road Hotel in the vicinity of the
Moon Palace Hotel. In connection with the meeting mentioned
above the Special Political Office of the S.M.P. immediately
started its activities.

宫崎事件当晚秘密社会成员在月宫饭店集会

自宫崎事件以来，有关当局正密切监视当地秘密社会的活动。警方已查明，某秘密社会的几名成员在宫崎事件当晚于月宫饭店举行了一次会议。尚不清楚该会议是否与事件有关，但值得注意的是，中山谋杀案的被告曾使用月宫饭店作为集会地点，而加藤（Kayau）谋杀案的被告则使用了月宫饭店附近的菊康路旅馆。针对上述会议，工部局警务处特别政治股立即展开了行动。

NIP-O

JAPANESE SAILOR MISSING; LANDING PARTY TAKES
PRECAUTIONS

At about 9.25 p.m. July 24 a Japanese youth approached a Japanese named Yanagida, First Class sailor, of the Third Battalion of the Naval Landing Party, while the latter was walking along Szechuen Road near the Uchiyama Magazine Department on his way back to the Landing Party Headquarters, and informed him that a Japanese sailor had been put into a motor car and carried away a moment before from an alleyway adjoining the Japanese Co-operative Society, corner of North Szechuan Road and Dixwell Road. He further stated to Yanagida that the victim seemed to have been fighting and had left a sailor's hat and a black necktie. These were handed over to Yanagida by the youth. Yanagida immediately communicated with the Landing Party Headquarters through the telephone of the Uchiyama Magazine Department and requested the man to accompany him to Headquarters. The man then excused himself on the ground that his mother was very sick and gave his name as Yoshio Okazaki and his address as No. 85 Woosung Road. Okazaki then left the place and the sailor, Yanagida, went to Headquarters to make a report on the incident. Upon receiving the information, the Landing Party Headquarters called an emergency mobilization and detailed sentries to the vicinity of Yangpang Bridge, north of Hongkew Creek.

Upon examining members of the Landing Party the authorities ascertained that the hat and necktie were the property of a first class sailor named Satao Miyazaki, age 21, attached to Headquarters battalion and that he was out on leave. The Landing Party authorities attempted to find Yoshio Okazaki at No. 85 Woosung Road to make further inquiries but they found that no such person was living there. The same authorities made extensive inquiries from Japanese residents in the Hongkew District regarding Yoshio Okazaki, but so far no one has been able to place him. According to Yanagida Okazaki was about 22 years of age, five feet and three inches tall, thinly built, pale, round face, small eyes, thin eye brows. He was dressed in a white tennis hat, short sleeved shirt and white trousers. Judging from his speech he was undoubtedly Japanese. The Japanese Consular Police authorities say that no such person is in the registration book. It is said that Okazaki did not take note of the licence plate of the motor car in question.

The Japanese Consular authorities, with the assistance of the S.M.P. and the Chinese Police Bureau started activities to search for missing sailor and to prevent the public from becoming excited.

It is reported that the Dixwell Road Police always have a policeman in the vicinity of the place in question, but Constable No. 440 who was on duty at the time when the reported incident took place made no report of any unusual happening in that area.

《日报》

日本水兵失踪；陆战队采取预防措施

7月24日晚9时25分左右，一名日本青年接近日本海军陆战队第三大队一等水兵柳田（Yanagida），当时后者正沿四川路行走，途经内山书店附近，准备返回陆战队总部。该青年告知柳田，片刻前在四川北路与狄思威路拐角处的日本消费组合旁的一条弄堂里，一名日本水兵被推入一辆汽车带走。他还向柳田表示，受害者似乎曾进行过搏斗，留下了一顶水兵帽和一条黑色领带。这些物品由该青年交给柳田。柳田立即通过内山书店的电话与陆战队总部联系，并要求该男子陪同他前往总部。该男子随后以母亲病重为由推脱，并报出姓名为冈崎芳雄（Yoshio Okazaki），地址为吴淞路85号。随后冈崎离开现场，水兵柳田前往总部报告此事。接到消息后，陆战队总部宣布紧急动员，并派遣哨兵前往虹口港以北的洋泾桥附近。

经对陆战队成员进行核查，当局确认帽子和领带属于隶属总部大队的21岁一等水兵宫崎佐太郎（Satao Miyazaki）所有，且他当时正在休假。陆战队当局试图前往吴淞路85号寻找吉雄·冈崎以作进一步询问，但发现那里并无此人居住。同一当局就吉雄·冈崎一事向虹口区日本侨民进行了广泛查询，但迄今无人能指认其人。据柳田称，冈崎约22岁，身高5英尺3英寸，身材瘦削，面色苍白，圆脸，小眼睛，眉毛稀疏。他头戴白色网球帽，身穿短袖衬衫和白裤子。从其谈吐判断，他无疑是日本人。日本领事警察当局称，登记册中查无此人。据说冈崎并未记下涉事汽车的车牌号码。

日本领事当局在工部局警务处和中国警察局的协助下，开始行动搜寻失踪水兵，并防止公众产生恐慌情绪。

据报道，狄思威路巡捕房通常在该地区附近部署一名警察，但在报告的事件发生时值勤的440号巡警并未报告该区域有任何异常情况。

CONSULAR POLICE ACTIVE TO LOCATE OKAZAKI

The Japanese Consular Police
have mobilized their entire force and have commenced

MR. YOSHIOKA STATES JAPANESE SAILOR KIDNAPPED BY
CHINESE

Mr. Yoshioka, officer in
charge of general affairs at the Japanese Embassy, called
at the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters to
exchange intelligence reports with the latter. At 11.30
p.m. he stated to newspaper reporters that he had no
knowledge of the details of the incident as he had received
no further information, but that the incident was believed
to have taken place at a dark place in an alleyway lying
along the north side of the Japanese Co-operative Society
and that judging from the circumstances the sailor had been
kidnapped by Chinese.

HONGKEW_ AND CHAPEI RETURN TO NORMAL 


The situation in the vicinity of North Szechuen 
Road Extension and Chapei, which were thrown into a state of 
great consternation on the night of July 24 following the 
reported disappearance of Satao hiyazaki, a Japanese seaman, 
returned to normal yesterday. With the exception of the 
railway crossing at Tien Tung an ( K Nua } where two 
Japanese marines stood on guard duty, all the Japanese 
forces stationed in the old site of the Seya Brewery behind 
the Rokusan Garden on angwan Road, the Japanese Cemetery 
at Peh Sz Jao (/\ F i ), the Japanese Primary School on 
North Szechuen Road and the Japanese Primary School far 
Girls on Euyang Road were withdrawn between noon and 2 peM. 
yesterday to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters on 
Ki angwan Road. Japanese patrols, either on foot or on 
motor cycles, were also fewer, The public were greatly 
relieved and the exodus nearly died down. 

Despite the diligent enquiries conducted by 

\ the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau and the Shanghai 
Municipal Police in conjunction with the Japanese Naval 

Landing Party and the Japanese Consular Police, no trace 
has yet been found of the missing Japanese seaman. It 
also remains unsolved whether or not there is such a person 
as the so-called nnly eye-witness Okazaki, whose name and 
address cannot be confirmed, 

At 11.30 a.m. yesterday, Mr. Okamoto, the 
Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai, c{lled on Mr. S. 
Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal 
Council, requesting the Settlement authorities to continue 
to assist in the investigation. According to information 
given out yesterday afternoon by the Police, the missing 
Japanese seaman wes said to have safely returned to his 
barrackse 

On the surface, the situation in Hongkew has 
returned to normal, but the Japanese marines are still 
active. When making a tour of inspection yesterday, 
a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency (K & de) witnessed 
several military trucks fully loaded with Japanese marines 
in full war kit, proceeding to the western district of 
Shanghai by way of North Szechmen Road and Nanking Road. 
According to certain residents in Hongkew, a large number 
of Japanese marines were transferred to the Toyoda Cotton
